title: fix: refresh conversation lists safely on reconnect
body:
Refreshes the conversation list from page one after a WebSocket reconnect while retaining the cached list if the refresh fails. It keeps the active conversation up to date and prevents stale responses from inactive or cached tabs from overwriting the current view.

## Related

This reconnect work was split from https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/pull/15523 so the shared tab-cache changes can be reviewed separately.

## How to reproduce

1. Load enough conversations to populate multiple pages and open an older conversation.
2. Disconnect the browser from the network, then update the active conversation from another session.
3. Restore the network and switch to another cached assignee tab while the reconnect request is pending.
4. Before this fix, the old response can overwrite the newly active tab, the selected conversation metadata can remain stale, and the selected item can break the server-provided list order.
5. After this fix, the active tab remains authoritative, the active conversation metadata and messages refresh, and the page-one order is preserved.
6. Make the reconnect request fail and verify the existing cached list remains available.

## What changed

- Replaces the reconnect delta query with a fresh page-one request.
- Invalidates in-flight list requests whenever chat-list filters change, including cached assignee-tab switches.
- Replaces cached conversations and resets pagination only after a successful response.
- Preserves the server response order while merging the selected conversation's local message state.
- Retains an active conversation outside page one and refreshes its conversation metadata before syncing messages.
- Shares request freshness across standard, advanced-filter, and saved-folder list requests.
- Clears the loading state when the current standard-list request fails.

title: feat(whatsapp): route campaigns to BSUID recipients
body:
BSUID-only contacts can now be included in one-off WhatsApp campaigns for Meta Cloud inboxes instead of being skipped because the contact has no phone number. Campaign delivery resolves a unique BSUID for the selected inbox, sends supported templates through Meta's `recipient` contract, and keeps existing phone-number campaign delivery unchanged.

Fixes https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-7802/support-bsuid-recipients-in-whatsapp-campaigns-and-bulk-sends

### Things to know

- This PR is intentionally scoped to Meta Cloud WhatsApp campaigns.
- Twilio WhatsApp campaign support is deferred; this PR does not change Twilio campaign UI, template parsing, provider submission, or analytics.
- A phone number remains the preferred campaign destination when present.
- Phone-less recipients require exactly one BSUID on the selected inbox. Missing or ambiguous identities are skipped/failed per recipient instead of selecting another merged identity.
- Authentication templates are blocked for BSUID-only campaign recipients before provider submission.

### How to test

1. Create a one-off WhatsApp campaign using a Meta Cloud inbox and an audience containing a contact with no phone number but exactly one BSUID ContactInbox in that inbox.
2. Select an approved non-authentication template and start the campaign.
3. Confirm the provider request addresses that contact by BSUID and the recipient is not skipped for a missing phone number.
4. Add a phone number to the same contact and confirm the campaign still sends to the phone number.
5. Add two BSUID ContactInboxes for the same contact and selected inbox; confirm the recipient is not sent because Chatwoot refuses to choose an ambiguous destination.
6. Select an authentication template for a BSUID-only recipient; confirm Chatwoot blocks it before provider submission.

title: fix: preserve line breaks in Copilot reply suggestions
body:
## Description

Applying a Copilot reply suggestion (**Use this**) inserts the reply through the plain-text editor path on every channel, so the line breaks render at first but collapse into a single paragraph the moment the agent edits the draft.

The rich-vs-plain branch is gated by a `conversationInboxType` prop that is never passed down from `Dashboard.vue`, so it always defaults to `''` and the plain-text path (`schema.text(content)` with raw newlines) is always taken. Those raw newlines are not real `paragraph`/`hard_break` nodes, so ProseMirror's whitespace normalization collapses them when the contenteditable DOM is re-read on the next edit.

This change always inserts the suggestion through the rich editor, which parses the markdown into proper nodes and already strips formatting the channel does not support. The now-dead `conversationInboxType` prop chain (`CopilotContainer → Copilot → CopilotAssistantMessage`) is removed.

**Follow-up in this PR:** routing the suggestion through the rich path exposed an `insertAtCursor` quirk — inserting multi-block content into an *empty* reply box splits the editor's empty starter paragraph, leaving a stray blank first line (and a trailing one). `insertAtCursor` now replaces the whole doc when it is a single empty paragraph and the inserted content is block-level, instead of inserting into it. Covered by two new unit tests in `editorHelper.spec.js`.

Fixes #14764

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How Has This Been Tested?

The collapse reproduces on web, email and API inboxes (all take the plain-text path because the gating prop is unset).

The mechanism was verified with a ProseMirror round-trip using the editor's own schema: content inserted via `schema.text()` collapses multi-line text into a single paragraph when the DOM is re-read on edit, whereas the markdown-parsed rich path (`paragraph`/`hard_break` nodes) round-trips without loss. After the change, **Use this** always uses the rich path, so the inserted reply keeps its line breaks when edited.

The empty-editor case (blank first line) is covered by unit tests: inserting multi-paragraph content into an empty editor yields exactly the inserted paragraphs, with existing-content behaviour unchanged (`pnpm exec vitest run app/javascript/dashboard/helper/specs/editorHelper.spec.js` — 100 passed).

- [x] I have performed a self-review of my code

title: fix(instagram): display button postbacks as incoming messages
body:
Instagram button-click postbacks that reach Chatwoot now appear as incoming messages in both Instagram Login and Facebook Login inboxes. Previously, these events were acknowledged but skipped by the Instagram webhook job.

Postbacks use the existing Instagram message flow, preserving their external message IDs and reusing its contact lookup, duplicate detection, authorization handling, and conversation selection. Event types are evaluated per item so a batch containing a postback followed by a regular message or read event is routed correctly.

### Closes

Fixes https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/issues/13033

### Things to know

- This handles received `postback` events. Webhook subscriptions and updates to existing connected inboxes are outside this PR.
- Quick replies delivered as `message.quick_reply` continue through the normal message path.
- This does not establish the cause of https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/issues/14584, which reports missing webhook delivery.

### How to test

1. With Instagram postback delivery configured, click an icebreaker or template button for an Instagram Login inbox. Confirm the selected title appears as an incoming message.
2. Repeat for an Instagram inbox connected through Facebook Login.
3. Replay the same event. Confirm that only one message exists for its message ID.
4. For a known contact, make profile lookup unavailable and send another postback. Confirm the message still appears.
5. Enable the single-conversation setting, resolve the conversation, and send a new postback. Confirm the existing conversation is reused.
6. Deliver a batch containing a postback and a normal DM. Confirm each retains its own message text.

title: feat: improve Captain playground test setup
body:
Adds a session-only test setup panel to the Captain V2 playground so teams can test saved or temporary scenarios, response guidelines, guardrails, and pasted knowledge without changing assistant configuration. Temporary items can be promoted individually by administrators, and each response exposes safe run details for scenario handoffs and tool calls.

## Closes

- https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-8057/make-the-captain-playground-better

## What changed

- Adds a responsive, tabbed test setup panel with saved items collapsed by default.
- Supports saved and disabled scenario selection, temporary scenarios and rules, and up to 10,000 characters of pasted knowledge.
- Lets administrators save temporary scenarios, guidelines, and guardrails individually, and save pasted knowledge as a Markdown document.
- Applies runtime-only prompt and agent overrides and returns sanitized tool and handoff run details.
- Keeps Captain V1 and production agent flows unchanged; customer and conversation targeting are not included in this version.

## How to test

1. Open a Captain V2 assistant playground and confirm saved scenarios, guidelines, guardrails, and knowledge counts load after refresh.
2. Add or exclude temporary and saved items, send messages, and inspect run details.
3. As an administrator, promote one temporary item and confirm it remains included without clearing the chat.

5. Reset test setup and confirm temporary content and messages clear while the latest saved configuration is restored.
6. Check the panel on a narrow viewport and confirm the V1 playground remains unchanged.

title: fix(auth): show OAuth error toast after snackbar mounts
body:
Personal email signups through Google now show the existing error toast when redirected back to login. The message remains visible for six seconds.

The login page previously emitted the toast before the snackbar subscribed to events. Emit it after mounting and the next Vue tick so the snackbar receives it.

## How to reproduce

1. Open `/app/login?error=business-account-only` while signed out, or attempt Google signup with a new personal email on an installation that requires work emails.
2. Confirm the work-email error toast appears for six seconds.
3. Confirm the `error` query parameter is removed after the toast is triggered.

The key is masked by default with show and copy controls, and rotating asks for confirmation since the old key is revoked immediately. ## Masked key ### Website Channel ### API Channel ## Rotate warning

title: fix: prevent stale messages when switching conversations
body:
Fixes a frontend race that can leave messages from a previously opened conversation visible in the current conversation until the page is refreshed.

Switching A → B → A before A’s history finishes loading can request the same page twice. Both responses prepend the same messages. If reconnect sync later sorts those duplicates, Vue can leave stale bubbles behind while reconciling duplicate message keys.

History loads now share pending requests for the same account, conversation, and pagination cursors. History merges skip existing message IDs, preserving newer realtime updates, and failed loads remain eligible for retry. Regression specs cover rapid switching, response isolation, failure and retry, pagination, and overlapping history.

## How to reproduce

1. Choose two conversations, A and B, with distinct messages and enough history to scroll.
2. Open browser DevTools and set Network throttling to **Slow 3G**.
3. Reload the page to clear the frontend conversation cache.
4. Open A, switch to B, then return to A **before A’s message history finishes loading**.
5. Wait for the requests to finish. Repeat from step 3 if needed, since this depends on timing.
6. Briefly disconnect and reconnect your network to trigger reconnect sync, then switch between A and B.

**Before the fix:** Duplicate messages may appear, and reconnect sync can leave stale message bubbles from another conversation visible until a refresh.

**Expected after the fix:** Each conversation shows only its own messages, without duplicates. Scrolling up continues to load older messages correctly.

title: fix: stray backslash and vanishing signature separator in replies
body:
# Pull Request Template

## Description

This PR fixes stray `\` characters and missing `--` signature separators when replies contain empty lines above the email signature. Empty lines and Shift+Enter line breaks are now preserved as composed across delivered emails, dashboard bubbles, text channels, and webhook payloads.

### https://github.com/chatwoot/prosemirror-schema/pull/59

### What changed

* Bump `@chatwoot/prosemirror-schema` to 1.4.5, which fixes markdown serialization of empty lines, hard breaks, and setext underline escaping at the source.
* Strip the escaped signature delimiter cleanly when toggling or removing the signature, so it never leaves a trailing `\`.
* Unescape the serializer's underline escape (`\--` → `--`) in `WebhookContentNormalizer`, so API-channel and webhook consumers receive the original text.
* Add end-to-end rendering specs covering every editor output shape with 23 byte-exact fixtures across cmark, both email modes, and all channel renderers.

Fixes https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-8062/email-replies-show-a-stray-backslash-instead-of-the-signature

## Type of change

### How to reproduce

On an email inbox with a message signature enabled, type a reply and press Enter at the end, leaving an empty line above the `--` separator, then send. The delivered email and email bubble show a stray `\` where the empty line should be, and the `--` separator disappears.

title: feat: (8/8) complete Shopify App Pricing lifecycle
body:
## Description

Completes the Shopify App Pricing lifecycle for Shopify-origin workspaces while leaving the existing Stripe billing and legacy Shopify integration paths unchanged. Subscription state is refreshed from the Shopify Partner API on billing visits and hourly, and uninstall events immediately revoke credentials and remove Shopify-owned entitlements.

This PR is stacked on #15242 and should be reviewed after it.

## Closes

- [PLA-170](https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/PLA-170/resolve-shopify-app-store-billing-rejection)

## What changed

- Preserves Shopify App Pricing return parameters through authentication and refreshes subscription state on every Shopify billing-page visit.
- Adds hourly reconciliation jobs for feature-enabled Shopify-billed accounts.
- Handles HMAC-verified app/uninstalled events by suspending Shopify billing access, removing plan entitlements, disabling the hook, and revoking stored credentials.
- Supports secure reinstall of a retained Shopify integration and routes Shopify-billed workspaces back to billing.
- Prevents Shopify-billed workspaces from disconnecting the integration inside Chatwoot; Shopify remains the owner of that lifecycle.
- Removes the superseded post-login pending-install completion endpoint and UI flow.
- Keeps every new callback, webhook, scheduled job, redirect, and UI behavior behind the global and account Shopify feature gates.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality not to work as expected)
- [ ] This change requires a documentation update

## How to test

1. Enable the global Shopify integration switch and the Shopify integration account feature.
2. Complete a Shopify-initiated install and confirm a new user lands on signup with the pending installation securely attached.
3. Select a Shopify App Pricing plan and confirm the return reaches the same Chatwoot billing route and shows the verified plan.
4. Revisit billing and confirm the displayed subscription reflects the latest Shopify state.
5. Send a signed app/uninstalled webhook and confirm the workspace loses Shopify plan access and the stored integration credentials are revoked.
6. Reinstall the app and confirm the retained workspace reconnects and returns to billing.
7. Disable either feature gate and confirm the Shopify lifecycle paths do not mutate data.
8. Confirm a non-Shopify-billed account can still connect and disconnect Shopify normally.

title: feat: (7/8) add Shopify App Pricing UI
body:
This adds the Shopify-specific signup and billing experience while preserving the existing Stripe billing screen and behavior for all non-Shopify accounts. Feature-enabled Shopify accounts use the same billing route, see a simpler Shopify subscription summary, and manage plans through Shopify-hosted App Pricing.

Closes

- https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/PLA-170/resolve-shopify-app-store-billing-rejection

Depends on #15240.

How to test

1. Keep the Shopify feature disabled and verify regular signup and Stripe billing behave as before.
2. Enable the global and account Shopify flags, then visit /app/auth/signup?shopify_pending_install=<valid-token> and complete registration.
3. Confirm the email and verify a pending Shopify account lands on Settings → Billing instead of onboarding or the product dashboard.
4. Open Shopify App Pricing from Billing, select a plan, and return to Chatwoot; verify the subscription refreshes and the account can enter the product once entitled.
5. Disable the account Shopify flag and verify the Shopify account never falls back to the Stripe component.

What changed

- Added a small billing-provider dispatcher without modifying the current Stripe billing component.
- Added the Shopify billing page with normalized plan, status, price, trial/renewal, last-verified, retry, and stale-state handling.
- Passed pending install identity through signup and email confirmation.
- Added billing-only route guards for pending, missing, and expired Shopify subscriptions.
- Added focused frontend and request coverage for provider selection, signup, redirects, return refresh, errors, and feature gating.

The existing Shopify install callback is intentionally activated in the final lifecycle PR so this stack remains safely dormant until jobs and webhooks are ready.

title: feat(shopify): (6/8) add provider-aware billing APIs
body:
Shopify-origin accounts now have a provider-neutral billing summary and are sent to the Shopify-hosted App Pricing page from the existing billing checkout action. Stripe accounts retain their current subscription, portal, currency, and credit top-up behavior, while Shopify actions fail closed when the integration gate is disabled.

This PR is stacked on #15238.

## Closes

- [PLA-170](https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/PLA-170/resolve-shopify-app-store-billing-rejection)

## What changed

- adds an admin-only billing summary with provider, subscription state, plan, amount, currency, billing dates, allowed actions, and verification time
- supports a forced Shopify verification on billing return before refreshed entitlements are exposed
- dispatches the existing checkout action to Stripe Billing Portal or Shopify App Pricing without changing the redirect response contract
- builds the Shopify pricing URL from the trusted installed shop and a validated Shopify app handle
- rejects Stripe customer creation, currency selection, and credit top-ups for Shopify-billed accounts
- keeps every Shopify billing action behind the shared global and account feature gate

## How to test

1. Configure the Shopify app handle, enable the global Shopify integration, and enable the account Shopify feature.
2. For a Shopify-origin account, load the billing summary and confirm it returns the normalized Shopify snapshot and only the Shopify-supported actions.
3. Start checkout and confirm the redirect points to the installed store App Pricing page in Shopify Admin.
4. Return after choosing a plan and request a refreshed summary; confirm the Partner subscription is verified and the updated plan state is returned.
5. Confirm currency selection and credit top-up actions are rejected for the Shopify account.
6. Disable either Shopify feature gate and confirm summary, refresh, and checkout return not found without falling through to Stripe.
7. For a Stripe account, confirm subscription setup, Billing Portal checkout, currency selection, and credit top-ups continue unchanged.

title: feat(shopify): (5/8) verify app pricing subscriptions
body:
Shopify-origin accounts can now verify their managed-pricing subscription through the Shopify Partner API and reconcile the matching Chatwoot plan, features, limits, and access state. The existing Stripe billing path remains unchanged, and every provider call and account mutation is bounded by the Shopify installation and account feature gates.

This PR is stacked on #15234.

## Closes

- [PLA-170](https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/PLA-170/resolve-shopify-app-store-billing-rejection)

title: feat(whatsapp): route BSUID calls through the active identity
body:
WhatsApp customers can become addressable only by a BSUID after WhatsApp stops sharing their phone number. Text messages already follow the exact identity attached to the conversation, but outbound calling still assumes that the contact has a phone number. This hides or rejects the call action for BSUID-only customers and can select the wrong destination after contacts are merged.

This PR makes the current conversation's WhatsApp identity authoritative for outbound calls. Calls and call-permission requests use the exact `ContactInbox#source_id` attached to that conversation. Phone-number calling continues to work as before.

### What changed

- Show the call action for a BSUID-only conversation when its WhatsApp inbox has calling enabled.
- Send the BSUID in Meta's `recipient` field for outbound calls and call-permission requests.
- Keep phone-number recipients on the existing `to` field.
- Preserve the selected conversation instead of guessing between identities owned by a merged contact.
- Keep contact-level calling phone-only when no conversation has established the destination.

### Things to know

- This change applies to Meta Cloud WhatsApp calling. Twilio Voice does not use the WhatsApp BSUID calling API and remains unchanged.
- This PR is based on [#15175](https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/pull/15175). Once that PR is merged, this PR should be retargeted to `develop`.

### How to test

1. Use a Meta Cloud WhatsApp inbox with calling enabled.
2. Open a conversation whose `ContactInbox#source_id` is a BSUID and whose contact has no phone number.
3. Confirm the call action is available and start an outbound call.
4. Confirm the call remains in the same conversation and Meta receives the BSUID as `recipient`.
5. Test a customer without call permission and confirm the permission request is sent to the same BSUID identity.
6. Confirm a normal phone-number conversation still places the call using the existing flow.

### Fixes

Fixes https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-7807

title: fix: Brazil whatsapp duplicate contacts
body:
# Pull Request Template

## Description

Fixes #13986

This PR fixes duplicate WhatsApp contacts created for Brazilian and Argentine phone number variants.

When WhatsApp Coexistence receives device-initiated or echo messages, the same customer can arrive with different valid number formats. For example, Brazil numbers may arrive with or without the extra mobile 9, and Argentina numbers may arrive with or without the extra 9 after country code 54.

Previously, Whatsapp::PhoneNumberNormalizationService checked only one normalized number format. If an existing contact_inbox was stored using the alternate format, Chatwoot did not find it and created a duplicate contact and conversation.

This change updates the normalization lookup to:

- Check the incoming number first.
- Check the normalized number.
- Check Brazil-specific alternate formats.
- Check Argentina-specific alternate formats.
- Reuse the existing contact_inbox if any candidate matches.
- Fall back to the original incoming number if no existing contact is found.

This preserves existing behavior for new contacts while preventing duplicate contacts for known WhatsApp number variants.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)


## How Has This Been Tested?

Tested using the affected WhatsApp and Twilio inbound message specs.

Run:
bundle exec rspec spec/services/twilio/incoming_message_service_spec.rb
bundle exec rspec spec/services/whatsapp/incoming_message_service_spec.rb

Verified scenarios include:

Brazilian WhatsApp numbers with and without the ninth digit.
Argentine WhatsApp numbers with and without the extra 9 after country code.
Existing contact inbox is reused when an alternate number format already exists.
New contact inbox is created using the original incoming number when no existing contact is found.

title: fix(widget): prevent duplicate email-collect messages
body:
## Pull Request Description

The email-collect web-widget template can run twice for the same conversation and create a duplicate pair of messages (the "Give the team a way to reach you." line + the email-input box appear twice in the widget).

`MessageTemplates::HookExecutionService#should_send_email_collect?` guards only with `email_collect_was_sent?` (does an `input_email` message already exist?), checked outside any lock. When two hook executions race for the same conversation — e.g. two incoming widget messages in quick succession — both pass the guard before either commits, so each creates the pair. Because the two messages are created in one transaction, the within-run after_create_commit re-trigger is already safe; the gap is the lack of serialization across separate executions.

This:
- Serializes creation in `MessageTemplates::Template::EmailCollect#perform` with `conversation.with_lock` and re-checks inside the lock, so concurrent executions can't both create the pair. (`reload` first because the conversation passed in from the message hook can carry an unpersisted `display_id` change, which Rails refuses to row-lock.)
- Adds `return false unless message.incoming?` to `should_send_email_collect?`, so the hook only reacts to the contact's incoming message and never to the template messages it creates — consistent with `should_send_out_of_office_message?`.

## Type of change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How Has This Been Tested?
- `spec/services/message_templates/template/email_collect_spec.rb` — added a test that invoking the template twice for the same conversation creates only one pair.
- Existing `hook_execution_service` specs (OSS + enterprise) pass.

Telegram escapes the literal tags because its provider payload uses HTML parse mode, while the other text-based channels retain the original content. ## Closes Closes #13493 ## How to reproduce 1. Send `\nasdf` through a WhatsApp or another text-based inbox. 2. Without this change, the outbound markdown renderer returns an empty string and the message cannot be delivered. 3. With this change, the original content is retained. Telegram displays the same literal text through an HTML-safe payload. ## What changed - Render CommonMark HTML block and inline HTML nodes from their stored string content. - Escape those nodes specifically in the Telegram renderer to preserve literal text without treating it as provider markup. - Add exact regression coverage for all affected channel mappings, tags-only content, trailing content, inline HTML, Twilio WhatsApp routing, and the final Telegram request payload.

title: fix(whatsapp): skip tracking-only webhook jobs
body:
WhatsApp tracking callbacks currently create background jobs even though Chatwoot does not consume them. This change acknowledges payloads containing only `tracking_events` after signature verification and the inactive-number check, then skips enqueueing them to reduce unnecessary webhook processing.

- Send a validly signed tracking-only webhook for a number in `INACTIVE_WHATSAPP_NUMBERS`. Expect HTTP 422 and no job.
- Send the same payload with an invalid signature to an inbox that requires signature verification. Expect HTTP 401 and no job.
- Send and receive a normal WhatsApp message. Confirm incoming messages appear and delivery/read indicators continue to update.

title: fix(attachment): resolve inline audio URL via configured Active Storage route
body:
## Description
`Attachment#inline_audio_url` hardcoded `rails_storage_redirect_url`, so audio playback ignored `config.active_storage.resolve_model_to_route`. On S3 setups configured with `:rails_storage_proxy` (required to avoid CORS/ORB failures) audio URLs still pointed directly at S3, and Chrome blocked the cross-origin range request with `ERR_BLOCKED_BY_ORB`, so playback failed. This switches the method to `url_for(file)` — the same helper `file_url` already uses — so the configured Active Storage route is honoured. Fixes #15006.

### Root cause
`app/models/attachment.rb:118-122` called `Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.rails_storage_redirect_url(file, disposition: 'inline')`, which always builds a redirect URL regardless of `resolve_model_to_route`. `file_url` (`:57`) uses `url_for(file)` and respects the setting — audio was the only inconsistency.

### Solution
Use `url_for(file)` in `inline_audio_url`, mirroring `file_url`.
- Default installs (`:rails_storage_redirect`) are unchanged — they keep redirect URLs, preserving the audio-on-redirect behavior introduced in #14440 (which keeps large recordings off the proxy range-limiter).
- Only installs that explicitly set `:rails_storage_proxy` now serve audio through the proxy — exactly what those admins configured, and consistent with all other media via `file_url`.
- Inline playback is preserved by the `content_types_allowed_inline` allowlist in `config/initializers/active_storage.rb`, so dropping the explicit `disposition: 'inline'` has no effect on playback.
- The `ActiveStorageProxyRangeLimit` mitigation from #14440 is untouched and still applies to any proxy traffic.

Note: the issue also mentions opus S3 object-metadata handling (Meta error 131053). That is a separate, larger change and is intentionally out of scope here.

## Type of change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How Has This Been Tested?
- Added `spec/models/attachment_spec.rb` example asserting the audio `data_url` honours `resolve_model_to_route` when the proxy route is configured; it fails without the fix (URL was `.../blobs/redirect/...`) and passes after.
- `bundle exec rspec spec/models/attachment_spec.rb` ✅ (27 examples, 0 failures)
- `bundle exec rubocop --parallel` ✅
- Manual QA: N/A — reproducing requires an S3 backend with `resolve_model_to_route = :rails_storage_proxy`; behavior is covered by the spec.

title: feat(shopify): add gated billing infrastructure
body:
This is the infrastructure stage of Shopify installation and billing, split from #13550 so it can be reviewed and merged before the shared signup and authentication changes. It adds gated Shopify subscription verification, billing details, plan mapping, and lifecycle cleanup for Shopify-billed accounts.

Existing accounts default to Stripe billing. The new Shopify billing flow requires both `ENABLE_SHOPIFY_INTEGRATION` and the account-level `shopify_integration` feature. The global switch defaults to disabled. This PR is not a rollout of the complete merchant installation journey.

### Related

- Stacked follow-up: #13550, which should merge only after this PR and a final end-to-end sanity check.
- Related: https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-6500/support-shopify-app-store-install-flow-for-merchant-initiated
- Related: https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/PLA-170/resolve-shopify-app-store-billing-rejection

### What changed

- Shopify domain validation, feature gates, API clients, secure pending-install storage, and subscription snapshots.
- Shopify billing identity, hosted pricing URLs, billing summary API/UI, plan mapping and fixed plan limits.
- Subscription sync/reconciliation and signed uninstall/privacy cleanup.
- Shopify configuration fields and integration availability checks.

### Things to know

- Shared signup/auth controllers, password reset, resend confirmation, mailers, user/notification callbacks, Google OAuth, MFA, and auth navigation are unchanged from `develop`.
- The minimal shared integration points include account billing identity, account serialization, billing controller/routes/UI, provider-specific plan resolution, Stripe-event protection, hook validation, configuration screens, and the hourly scheduler. These still need review; this PR is not exclusively new files.
- The complete installation/callback/signup wiring remains in #13550. Do not enable this as a standalone merchant rollout.
- No database migration or schema change is included. The duplicate-hook cleanup and unique indexes remain in #13550, along with their database-level tests.
- Captain reservation accounting, IMAP processing changes, notification callback changes, and global configuration-loader changes remain in #13550.
- Uninstall/privacy cleanup intentionally works while the global feature is disabled.
- The existing Stripe plan feature catalog is preserved; Shopify-specific entitlement cleanup has its own feature set.

### How to test

1. With Shopify disabled, verify ordinary signup, login, confirmation resend, password reset, and existing Stripe billing continue working; Shopify should be absent from the integrations list and direct details should be unavailable.
2. In a disposable cloud-mode test instance, configure the Shopify Partner API, app handle, and test plan catalog. Enable the global and account Shopify flags for a pre-provisioned Shopify-origin account with a connected development-store hook.
3. Open Settings → Billing. Verify that it displays the Shopify subscription and that Manage in Shopify opens Shopify-hosted pricing.
4. Select a development-store plan only when Shopify confirms there will be no charge. Return to billing and verify the authoritative plan, state, renewal date, and fixed account limits.
5. Confirm ordinary accounts continue using Stripe checkout and billing. A Shopify account must not enter Stripe subscription or top-up actions.
6. Verify signed uninstall cleanup clears store credentials and removes Shopify entitlements, including while the integration flag is off.

The full first-install, signup, confirmation, and reinstall/reconnect test belongs to #13550 after this infrastructure is merged.

title: feat: expose Captain in assignment dropdown
body:
Adds the Captain assistant attached to an inbox to the conversation assignment dropdown and lets agents explicitly assign conversations to it through the typed AI-assignee contract.

## Closes

- https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-7452/add-captain-to-the-assignment-dropdown

## Why

Captain ownership is supported by the backend, but agents need an explicit way to assign or hand a conversation back to the inbox's Captain assistant. Manual assignment is a human decision and should not be blocked by the audience, business-hours, response-quota, or external-bot rules used for automatic Captain engagement.

## What this change does

- Replaces the Agent Bot-only assignable-agents opt-in with `include_ai_assignees`, returning typed User, AgentBot, and Captain owners.
- Adds the Captain assistant to the conversation assignment dropdown when the same assistant is attached to the requested inbox.
- Accepts a manual Captain assignment only when the selected assistant is attached to the conversation inbox.
- Assigns Captain as the AI owner, clears the human owner, and moves the conversation to `pending`.
- Removes the temporary Captain assignment rollout guard.
- Displays Captain-owned conversations with the AI-assignee icon in conversation cards.
- Keeps automatic Captain engagement and eligibility behavior unchanged.
- Leaves human-only and bulk assignment surfaces unchanged.

This PR is stacked on #15421.

## Validation

1. Attach a Captain assistant to an inbox.
2. Open a conversation from that inbox and expand the assignee dropdown.
3. Verify the Captain assistant appears alongside human agents and Agent Bots.
4. Assign Captain and verify it becomes the displayed owner and the conversation moves to `pending`.
5. Verify an assistant that is not attached to the conversation inbox cannot be assigned.
6. Verify Captain is not offered in human-only or bulk assignment surfaces.

title: fix: load ChatwootHub before stubbing edition in specs
body:
Fixes the backend FOSS CI failures caused by the paid self-hosted plan specs added in #15760. PRs containing those specs can fail before the plan checks even run.

The FOSS job removes Enterprise code. These tests then pretend Enterprise is installed, and loading `ChatwootHub` for the first time tries to load the missing Enterprise extension. That crashes with `undefined method 'const_defined?' for false`.

The fix explicitly loads `ChatwootHub` before the tests override the edition checks. This lets it load using the actual installation state, then allows each test to simulate its plan as intended.

title: fix(filters): use local calendar dates in saved filters
body:
Date filters now keep conversations on the calendar day the user expects. Applying or saving a filter records the browser's timezone, so a conversation started late in the evening is no longer excluded just because its UTC date is already the next day.

### The bug

A conversation created on **September 7 at 9:49 PM in Brasília** is stored as **September 8 at 00:49 UTC**. A folder with `Created at > September 6` and `Created at < September 8` compared the UTC date and excluded it. The September 7 report used the viewer's timezone and included it, leaving the folder with three conversations while the report showed four.

### The fix

- Save the browser's IANA timezone with `Created at` and `Last activity at` filter conditions. Named timezones account for daylight-saving changes on the date being filtered.
- Convert stored timestamps to that timezone before comparing calendar dates, and use the same timezone for `Days before`.
- Apply the same date comparison in frontend filtering. Saved-folder unread counts use the same backend conditions.
- Preserve the saved timezone when editing folders or contact segments. The shared date-filter path also fixes contact timestamp filters.

Existing folders and API filters without a timezone retain their previous UTC behavior. **Open and update an existing folder once to adopt timezone-aware filtering.** Date-only custom attributes are not timezone-converted, and automation payload generation keeps its existing behavior.

### How to reproduce

1. Use a browser in `America/Sao_Paulo` and a conversation created at `2026-09-08 00:49 UTC`, which appears as September 7 at 9:49 PM locally.
2. Apply `Status = All`, `Created at > September 6`, and `Created at < September 8`, then save the folder.
3. Before this fix, the conversation is missing even though it appears in the September 7 report. With this fix, it appears in the folder and stays there after reloading.
4. Edit the saved folder and update its name. Its timezone and matching conversations should stay the same.

### Closes

Support report: https://app.chatwoot.com/app/accounts/1/conversations/91709

title: fix(whatsapp): temporarily disable contact-info action during browsing
body:
Temporarily hide the WhatsApp Request Contact Info action in conversation responses to remove message-history lookups from routine inbox browsing. Conversation payloads keep the existing fields but return `available: false`, `reason: null`, and `delivery_mode: null`.

This is an alternative to #15825. Instead of displaying an action that can later fail because of a pending request in older history, this mitigation hides the dedicated action entirely while a cheaper pending-state approach is considered.

## What changed

- Return disabled contact-info availability from the shared conversation partial without invoking eligibility checks.
- Disconnect the batch lookup from list rendering while retaining the service code for re-enabling the feature.

Check conversation lists, filtered lists, contact conversation lists, and individual conversation responses. Each should return the disabled contact-info payload.

title: fix(contacts): default the contacts list to most recent activity first
body:
The Contacts page could fail to load on larger accounts. When a user has never picked a sort, the list asked for contacts ordered by **oldest** activity first. No index can serve that order, so every page load read every contact in the account just to return 15. When those rows aren't cached, or the database disk is under load, that runs past the 14s statement timeout and the page never loads. The page now defaults to **most recent** activity first. The existing `(account_id, last_activity_at DESC NULLS LAST)` index serves that order, so a page load reads about 20 pages whatever the account's size. Users who picked a sort keep it.

## Closes

- No existing issue. Found via recurring `PG::QueryCanceled` / `Rack::Timeout` errors on `contacts#index`.

## How to reproduce

1. On a large account, open **Contacts** as a user who has never changed the sort.
2. The page sends `GET /api/v1/accounts/:id/contacts?sort=last_activity_at`, which becomes `ORDER BY last_activity_at ASC NULLS LAST LIMIT 15`.
3. Postgres fetches and sorts every listed contact of the account. When those pages come from disk, the request hits the statement timeout.

## What changed

- `ContactsIndex.vue`: when no `contacts_sort_by` UI setting is saved, the default sort is now `-last_activity_at` instead of `last_activity_at`.
- Measured on production for a ~57k-contact account:
  - old default: 57,768 pages read per load (56 ms cached, about 24s from disk at the measured ~0.42 ms per page);
  - new default: an index scan that stops after 15 rows.
- Contact search uses the same plan for either sort direction (trigram bitmap scan, then a sort of the matches), so it is unaffected.
- Known trade-off: on accounts made up mostly of anonymous visitors, the new order walks more of the activity index before finding 15 listed contacts. A partial index restricted to listed contacts removes that cost if it shows up.

title: feat: resolve IP location for sign-in and sign-out audit logs
body:
# Pull Request Template

## Description

Sign-in and sign-out write one audit row per account the user belongs to using `insert_all!`, which bypasses the `after_create_commit` that enqueues the IP geolocation lookup added in #15455. Session audits were the only rows that never got a city or country.

Restoring the callback would undo #15572, which took a 500-account sign-in from 2016 queries to 519. Since every row from one sign-in shares a `remote_address` and `request_uuid`, this enqueues a single job per sign-in that resolves the address once and applies it to that request's rows in one `update_all`, scoped to accounts with `ip_lookup` enabled. Constant cost regardless of membership count.

The second commit fixes a defect found while testing. `audit_event_rows` used `::Audited.store[:current_request_uuid] || SecureRandom.uuid`. Rails strips an inbound `X-Request-Id` to an empty string when it holds only punctuation, and `""` is truthy, so those rows were written with a blank uuid and the new job would skip the batch. Now uses `.presence`.

Fixes https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-8135

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

## How Has This Been Tested?

New job spec: one lookup applied to every row of a request, isolation from other requests, a batch spanning eligible and ineligible accounts, no lookup for ineligible or empty scopes, error swallowing.

Session controller spec: exactly one job enqueued for a user in four accounts, and rows still share a generated uuid when the request id sanitises to blank. Verified that spec fails without the `.presence` fix.

27 examples, 0 failures locally. Rubocop clean.

title: fix(twilio): preserve incoming quoted replies
body:
Incoming WhatsApp replies through Twilio lose their quoted-message context, leaving agents unable to tell which earlier message the customer means. This change displays the referenced message when it exists in the same conversation.

The Twilio callback now accepts `OriginalRepliedMessageSid` and passes it to the existing message reply resolver as `in_reply_to_external_id`.

### Things to know

- Applies to incoming quoted replies. Sending quoted replies through Twilio remains unchanged.
- Uses the existing same-conversation lookup; references to unavailable messages retain the existing unresolved-reply behavior.
- Previously received messages are not backfilled.

### How to reproduce

1. In a Twilio WhatsApp conversation, reply to an earlier message using WhatsApp's reply action.
2. Before this fix, Chatwoot displays the reply without the quoted message even when Twilio supplies its SID.

### How to test

1. Reply to a recent message in an existing Twilio WhatsApp conversation.
2. Confirm the incoming reply displays the original message in its quote preview.
3. Click the quote preview to navigate to the original message.

Locally verified by posting a mock Twilio webhook to the callback endpoint: the incoming message persisted both reply identifiers and displayed the original message in the conversation UI. Regression coverage checks that the controller forwards the quoted SID and the incoming-message service persists both reply identifiers. The focused Twilio suite passed with 52 examples and no failures; RuboCop and diff checks also passed.

title: fix(voice): answer WhatsApp calls from the conversation when the call is not in the store
body:
Answering an incoming WhatsApp call from the call bubble in the conversation could show "Internal Server Error", and the caller then saw the call as missed. This happened when the call wasn't in the agent's calls store: it rang while the agent wasn't online, or it was dismissed earlier. In that case the dashboard fell back to the Twilio flow and requested a Twilio token for the WhatsApp inbox.

## Closes

- https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-8174

## How to reproduce

1. Set your availability to Busy or Offline and receive a WhatsApp call on an inbox with calling enabled.
2. Open the conversation and click Answer on the ringing call bubble.
3. Before: "Internal Server Error" and the call ends as missed. After: the call connects.

## What changed

- The call bubble adds the call to the calls store from its own message data before joining, so the WhatsApp answer path is used.
- `ConferenceController` only resolves Twilio inboxes, so the Twilio token and conference endpoints return 404 for other inboxes instead of 500.

title: fix(ci): document RubyLLM audit exception
body:
## Description

Restore the dependency-audit CI check by adding a documented exception for RubyLLM's CVE-2026-67991 on Chatwoot's supported runtime. The change adds only this advisory to `.bundler-audit.yml`, with the applicability rationale and removal condition. RubyLLM remains at 1.15.0 and every other advisory remains subject to the existing audit configuration.

### Advisory verification and applicability

[CVE-2026-67991 / GHSA-42r3-x6vx-x49x](https://github.com/rubysec/ruby-advisory-db/blob/44784c295391577f25d198a9205eae4ba73ec4da/gems/ruby_llm/CVE-2026-67991.yml) describes polynomial-time name normalization on Ruby 3.1.x when a very long crafted class, agent, or tool name reaches the affected operation. The released 1.15.0 gem contains the regex inline in `RubyLLM::Tool#name`; the advisory's later `Utils.underscore` reference does not mean released gems were unaffected.

The exception is based on the application's runtime and actual input paths:

- **Runtime:** the Gemfile, `.ruby-version`, CircleCI and Docker images specify Ruby 3.4.4. A bounded local probe of the installed `Tool#name` method reproduced quadratic behavior on Ruby 3.1.0, but linear behavior on Ruby 3.4.4. The latter also reports this regex as linear-time, consistent with [Ruby's regex memoization introduced in 3.2](https://www.ruby-lang.org/en/news/2022/12/25/ruby-3-2-0-released/).
- **Built-in tools:** names come from fixed application classes, rather than user-generated class names.
- **Custom tools:** [slugs are limited to 64 characters](https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/blob/e16d8f2fa4bd00c65747de0b8363f0e05092e36c/enterprise/app/models/captain/custom_tool.rb#L38-L65). [Toolable overrides the name method](https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/blob/e16d8f2fa4bd00c65747de0b8363f0e05092e36c/enterprise/app/models/concerns/toolable.rb#L8-L25) to return that slug directly, bypassing RubyLLM's normalizer.
- **Agent handoffs:** Chatwoot uses `Agents::Agent` from ai-agents; its handoff tools override naming with a separate lowercase/filter conversion. Scenario handoff names also have a length budget. Ordinary prompt/message text does not automatically enter the affected normalization operation.

Local timings for synthetic all-capital class names:

| Characters | Ruby 3.1.0 | Ruby 3.4.4 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 5,000 | 104 ms | 0.85 ms |
| 10,000 | 430 ms | 1.72 ms |
| 20,000 | 1,676 ms | 3.31 ms |

These measurements characterize the reported regex behavior, not production capacity. Ruby 3.1.0 was used only for the isolated method probe; Chatwoot itself was not run on that unsupported version. Live deployment runtimes were not remotely inspected.

### Why this PR does not upgrade RubyLLM

As of 16 September 2026, stable 1.16.0 still contains the pattern and still matches the advisory. The [upstream fix](https://github.com/crmne/ruby_llm/commit/9d75b033d7d00c4e1baa9b0afb4828faa8bd6602) is released starting with 2.0.0.rc1; the latest release is 2.0.0.rc4, also a prerelease.

`ai-agents 0.12.0` requires `ruby_llm ~> 1.14`. An isolated Bundler resolution rejects 2.0.0.rc4. Bypassing the constraint for a compatibility probe makes `require 'agents'` fail on the removed `param` method. Chatwoot [requires agents unconditionally during initialization](https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/blob/e16d8f2fa4bd00c65747de0b8363f0e05092e36c/config/initializers/ai_agents.rb#L1-L3), so simply widening that constraint can prevent application startup, including when Captain is unused.

The [2.0 migration](https://github.com/crmne/ruby_llm/blob/v2.0.0.rc4/docs/_reference/upgrading.md) also affects existing Chatwoot behavior:

| Surface | Required migration |
| --- | --- |
| Captain V2 / scenario handoffs | Replace removed `Tool::Halt`, update instruction/tool replacement APIs, and preserve runner state and handoff control. |
| Built-in/custom tools and Copilot | Update `param`/`params`, parameter-schema readers, tool registration, provider options and callbacks. |
| Rewrites, replies, summaries, labels and other Captain tasks | Replace direct token readers; current response conversion can otherwise fail after a successful provider response. |
| Images and conversation replay | Replace `RubyLLM::Content` with the new attachment/message API. |
| Structured generation | Read parsed output through `response.parsed`; current Hash consumers can otherwise produce empty overview points, blank article fields or raw JSON taglines. |
| OpenAI-compatible endpoints | Make protocol selection explicit: 2.0 defaults to `/responses` instead of `/chat/completions`. Existing `response_format` options and custom endpoints need adaptation or an explicit Chat Completions protocol. |
| Request behavior / observability | Validate temperature settings, token/cost tracing and the renamed model-registry refresh method. |

The isolated request probe confirmed the protocol change and that a GPT-5.2 request configured with temperature 0.5 sends 1.0 under 1.15 and 0.5 under rc4. No live provider requests were made.

There is no `acts_as_chat`/`acts_as_message` persistence integration in Chatwoot, so the upstream Rails data migration does not automatically apply. Embedding/moderation readers used here still exist, and legacy speech/PDF operations use the separate OpenAI client. RubyLLM remains MIT licensed. A supported upgrade should be coordinated with ai-agents instead of being folded into this audit exception.

### Removal condition

Remove the exception when Chatwoot adopts a supported patched RubyLLM/ai-agents combination, including a recognized compatible 1.x backport if one becomes available. Reassess it if the supported Ruby runtime or tool-name construction changes. This records advisory applicability; it does not claim that RubyLLM 1.15.0 includes the upstream fix.

The original audit failure was reproduced against ruby-advisory-db `44784c295391577f25d198a9205eae4ba73ec4da`. The actual changed configuration now passes the refreshed audit, YAML formatting and whitespace checks. The prior investigation passed 528 existing focused specs on this application revision; after adding the exception, all 131 selected Captain base-task, custom-tool and scenario specs passed again. Existing Rails enum deprecation warnings remain unchanged. No new specs were added for the configuration-only change.

## Closes

No linked ticket.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How to reproduce

1. On the parent commit, run the CircleCI dependency-audit check with an updated ruby-advisory-db. It reports RubyLLM 1.15.0 / CVE-2026-67991 and exits unsuccessfully.
2. Run the same check on this branch. It succeeds with the documented exception; the gem versions and application behavior remain unchanged.

title: fix: Configure increased redis reconnection attempts
body:
Add reconnect attempts configuration for Redis.

## Description

This PR fixes an issue where Chatwoot stops delivering websocket updates after Redis is restarted.

For the past few months, `needrestart` has been silently restarting services that depend on upgraded libraries during system updates, including Redis. This is the case for me, and maybe it will be for other people as well.

Issue is When Redis restarts, Action Cable loses its Redis subscription connection.

The root cause is that the Redis client used by Action Cable only performs a limited reconnect attempt. If Redis is unavailable during that window, the subscription remains disconnected permanently. As a result, websocket connections stay open and continue sending pings, but no real-time updates are delivered to clients.

This change configures Redis subscription reconnection attempts with exponential backoff, allowing Action Cable to recover automatically from temporary Redis outages and service restarts.

Closes #14705

## Type of change

* [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How Has This Been Tested?

### Reproduction Steps

1. Deploy Chatwoot v4.8.0.
2. Open the Chatwoot admin panel.
3. Verify that real-time updates are working.
4. Restart Redis:
```sh
sudo systemctl restart redis-server

```


5. Send a new message or trigger a real-time event.

### Before this change

* Websocket connections remain open.
* Only ping frames are exchanged.
* No real-time updates are delivered.
* Chatwoot requires a restart to restore functionality.

### After this change

* Action Cable automatically reconnects to Redis.
* Real-time updates continue working after Redis becomes available.
* No Chatwoot restart is required.

title: fix(whatsapp): upload attachments to the media endpoint and send media_id
body:
WhatsApp Cloud attachments are now uploaded to Meta's media endpoint and sent by `media_id` instead of a public `link`. Meta no longer downloads the file from the Chatwoot server, so outbound media stops failing intermittently with `131053: Media upload error` on hosts that share an ASN with other Chatwoot/Evolution API instances — Meta's `fwdproxy` rate limits per destination ASN, not per WABA account. It also removes the secondary failure where `fwdproxy` does not follow ActiveStorage's `302` redirect and reports `Unsupported mime type text/html`.

Operators who need the previous behaviour can set `WHATSAPP_MEDIA_UPLOAD_STRATEGY=link`. No migrations, no config required on upgrade.

Supersedes #15069 by @AdarshJ173, which established this approach and the `media_id` direction. The review points raised by @nestordavalos on that PR are addressed here.

## Closes

- Closes #13540
- Supersedes #15069

## How to reproduce

On a WhatsApp Cloud inbox, send an image, document or voice note from an instance whose hosting provider shares an ASN with other Chatwoot deployments (e.g. Hostinger, ASN 47583). Meta's webhook returns:

```
Downloading media from weblink failed with http code 429
ratelimit reason: Request ratelimit by fwdproxy
[GlobalCountingRatelimiter] Request hit ratelimit policy — destination matcher asn_list: 47583
```

After this change the file is uploaded first and the message references the returned `media_id`, so Meta never fetches it from us.

## What changed

- **New `Whatsapp::MediaUploadService`** — streams the blob to `POST /{version}/{phone_number_id}/media` as multipart form data and returns `{ 'id' => media_id }`, or `nil` when the upload is disabled or fails.
- **`WhatsappCloudService#build_attachment_content`** sends the returned media object, falling back to `{ 'link' => download_url }` so a media-endpoint failure never blocks a message.
- Uses `Faraday::Multipart::FilePart`, matching `Telegram::SendAttachmentsService`, the codebase's existing multipart upload. The file part carries an explicit filename and content type.
- Reads the blob through `blob.open` and streams it via Faraday's `CompositeReadIO`, so large attachments are never buffered in memory and any ActiveStorage backend works.
- Follows `WHATSAPP_API_VERSION` via `GlobalConfigService`, matching `calls_phone_id_path` in the enterprise provider, rather than pinning a version in source.
- Falls back to the link on `Faraday::Error` or a non-success response only; other errors surface instead of silently degrading.
- Logs one warning naming the fallback and Meta's own error, including for non-JSON error pages: `[WHATSAPP] Media upload failed, falling back to link for account … attachment …: HTTP 429 Request ratelimit by fwdproxy`.

The `voice`/`caption`/`filename` fields and the existing `audio/opus` → `audio/ogg` normalisation are unchanged; the normalisation now also governs the uploaded part's content type.

title: fix: Widget DirectUpload CSRF error
body:
## Problem
Widget file uploads via ActiveStorage DirectUpload fail on production with:

```text
ActionController::InvalidAuthenticityToken (Can't verify CSRF token authenticity.)
```

This occurs because `Api::V1::Widget::DirectUploadsController` inherits from `ActiveStorage::DirectUploadsController` → `ActiveStorage::BaseController`, which has protect_from_forgery with: :exception enabled.

While CSRF works on same-origin, it fails in production because the widget is embedded in an iframe on third-party customer sites (cross-origin)


## Solution
Skip CSRF verification for the widget direct uploads endpoint - this is safe because:

- Widget endpoints authenticate via website_token + X-Auth-Token (token-based auth)
- CSRF protection is designed for session-based auth, not token-based auth

title: fix(sessions): read MAX_USER_SESSIONS from ENV dynamically to avoid YJIT constant caching
body:
Ruby 3.4 with YJIT enabled inlines constant values at compile time, so `stub_const` in tests can't replace a class-level constant that YJIT has already cached — the spec calls still see the original value and the session-limit tests return 200 instead of 409.

## What changed

- Removed the `MAX_SESSIONS` class constant from `DeviseOverrides::SessionsController`
- `sessions_limit_reached?` now reads `ENV.fetch('MAX_USER_SESSIONS', 25).to_i` directly on each call (with a guard for `<= 0`)
- Updated the spec to use `with_modified_env` instead of `stub_const` so the limit is configurable at test time without hitting the YJIT cache

## How to test

Run the session limit enforcement specs:

```
bundle exec rspec spec/controllers/devise_overrides/sessions_controller_spec.rb
```

All tests should pass, including on Ruby 3.4 with YJIT enabled.

title: fix: return 404 instead of 500 for unknown portal slugs
body:
Fixes #15797 - credit to @Uankur for the precise report and diagnosis (exact citations, repro curls, and the proposed direction); this PR implements the fix they sketched, verified independently against current `develop`. @Uankur - would love your eyes on this.

## Problem

`GET /api/v1/accounts/:account_id/portals/:slug` returns HTTP 500 when the slug does not exist in the account. `fetch_portal` uses `find_by(slug:)`, which returns nil instead of raising, and `show` then calls `@portal.articles` on nil. The blast radius is wider than `show`: `fetch_portal` runs as a `before_action` for every portal action except `index`/`create`, so `update`, `destroy`, `archive`, `logo` and `send_instructions` hit the same nil crash (EE `ssl_status` too).

## Fix

One-token change: `find_by` -> `find_by!`. `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` then flows through the existing `handle_with_exception` rescue, which renders the standard 404 `"Resource could not be found"` - the same pattern sibling controllers already use (`labels_controller` uses `find`, and the public portals controllers use `find_by!(slug:)`). The lookup stays scoped to `Current.account.portals`, so a slug belonging to another account also returns 404, matching the reporter's expectation. Pundit authorization is class-level here and unchanged.

## Tests

Two request specs added to `portals_controller_spec.rb`: unknown slug -> 404 with the standard body, and cross-account slug -> 404.

**Test status (honest):** the specs are written but NOT executed - no Ruby toolchain was available in our environment. Verification was static: the nil path, the `handle_with_exception` RecordNotFound -> 404 rescue, and the sibling/public-controller `find_by!` precedent were all confirmed against current `develop` (`2f1ed80f89`). The one-token change mirrors the repo's own usage elsewhere.

> Built by breken, your AI support engineer - breken.ai - this one's on us.

title: fix: limit app, widget, and admin search indexing
body:
## Description

Prevent non-Cloud login and application pages, Super Admin, and installation setup pages from being indexed. Cloud application pages remain eligible for indexing. Widget pages always include `noindex`, and their existing crawl exclusion is preserved to avoid creating contacts from crawler requests. Public Help Center homepages and articles retain their existing indexing behavior, including when a widget is embedded.

A public Rails route replaces the static robots.txt file and retains `Disallow: /widget`. The application layout uses the existing Cloud detection helper to apply `noindex` conditionally; widget, Super Admin, and setup pages include it on every installation. Public Help Center layouts remain unchanged.

Because widget crawling remains blocked, crawlers cannot reliably read its `noindex` tag to remove already-indexed widget URLs. Allowing widget crawling safely requires a separate change to make widget GET requests create no records.

## Closes

Closes https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-8224/prevent-login-page-indexing-on-non-cloud-installations

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How Has This Been Tested?

1. On a self-hosted installation, open the page source for `/app/login`, `/app/login/sso`, `/app`, `/`, and `/widget?website_token=<valid-token>`. The HTML head includes `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">`, including when the manifest is disabled.
2. Set the installation's `DEPLOYMENT_ENV` to `cloud` with Enterprise enabled and reload. The application pages no longer include the directive, while the widget still includes it. Community installations retain the directive on application and widget pages.
3. Open `/super_admin/sign_in`, sign in, and inspect `/super_admin` and `/super_admin/accounts`. All include `noindex` on Cloud, self-hosted Enterprise, and Community installations.
4. On a fresh installation, open `/` and follow the redirect to `/installation/onboarding`. The setup page includes `noindex`.
5. Open a public Help Center homepage, article, and custom-domain homepage using either portal layout, including with a widget attached. None receives the directive. Plain article previews remain unaffected.
6. Open `/robots.txt` without signing in. It returns plain text with `User-agent: *` and `Disallow: /widget`, including in API-only deployments. Other paths remain crawlable.

title: docs(env): document WEB_CONCURRENCY in .env.example
body:
Closes #15819.

## Problem
`config/puma.rb` reads `WEB_CONCURRENCY` to run Puma in clustered mode:
```ruby
workers ENV.fetch("WEB_CONCURRENCY", 0)
preload_app!
```
But `WEB_CONCURRENCY` is absent from `.env.example`, so most self-hosted installs leave it unset and Puma defaults to `workers=0` (single process, only `RAILS_MAX_THREADS` threads). Under the GVL, CPU-bound requests then serialize and can queue/timeout even on multi-core servers.

## Change
Add a commented `WEB_CONCURRENCY` entry next to `RAILS_MAX_THREADS` in `.env.example`, explaining clustered mode and how to size it. 

The line is **commented out**, so default behavior is unchanged — this only documents and surfaces the knob to self-hosters, leaving the actual default value as a deployment choice. Docs-only, no code paths touched.

## Description

`Shopify::FeatureGate.globally_enabled?` resolved the flag through `GlobalConfigService.load`,
which is a write-capable helper. When the stored value is boolean `false` (the shipped default

installation config row instead, since the stubbed call no longer happens.

title: fix: trigger dashboard alerts on bot handoff
body:
Bot handoffs now play the dashboard sound and show a browser-tab badge, so agents know when a conversation needs human attention without waiting for another message.

Alerts use the agent's existing audio settings, including assignment filters and whether to alert while the dashboard is visible. Captain private notes remain visible in the conversation but no longer trigger alerts. The handoff itself is what requests attention.

## How it works

- A bot handoff starts a 2.5-second window, giving automatic assignment time to finish.
- At the end of the window, the dashboard checks the latest available assignment and status before applying the agent's alert settings.
- A human takeover or a conversation that is no longer open cancels the alert. Unrelated updates, such as an out-of-office message, do not cancel it.
- If the conversation is not stored locally, the dashboard uses the original handoff details.
- A bot handoff now only applies to pending conversations. On a conversation that is already open or resolved, it does nothing: no status change, no `waiting_since` update, and no handoff event. This affects agent-bot and API handoffs, handoff notifications, and handoff reporting, not just alerts.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Captain
    participant Conv as Conversation#bot_handoff!
    participant Listener as ActionCableListener
    participant Assign as Auto-assignment
    participant WS as actionCable.js
    participant Audio as DashboardAudioNotificationHelper

    Captain->>Conv: hand off
    Conv->>Conv: return false unless pending?
    Conv->>Listener: conversation.bot_handoff
    Listener->>WS: broadcast to inbox members
    WS->>WS: start 2.5s timer (key = account:id, duplicates ignored)
    Assign->>Listener: assignee_changed (performed_by Inbox/AssignmentPolicy)
    Listener->>WS: assignee.changed + assignment{automatic, assignee_id, type, updated_at}
    WS->>WS: store updates conversation
    Note over WS: timer fires
    WS->>WS: alertOnSettledHandoff()
    WS->>Audio: onConversationBotHandoff(conversation)
    Audio->>Audio: triggerAlert → filters → sound + badge + 30s repeat
```

The window is intentionally limited. If automatic assignment takes longer than 2.5 seconds, agents using assignment-based filters may miss that handoff alert. A late assignment does not restart it.

## Alert preferences

Agents control these alerts in **Profile Settings → Audio Alerts → Alert events for conversations**, using the same options as message audio alerts: my assigned conversations, unassigned conversations, and open conversations assigned to others.

Unchecking all three disables handoff sounds and their tab badges (`ui_settings.enable_audio_alerts = 'none'`). There is no separate bot-handoff toggle, so this also disables message audio alerts. The existing inactive-window and 30-second reminder settings apply to handoffs too.

## How to test

1. Enable dashboard audio alerts and switch to another browser tab.
2. Ask Captain to hand a pending conversation to a human. Confirm the sound and tab badge appear after about 2.5 seconds, without a second alert from the private note.
3. Try assignment filters, disabled alerts, and viewing the conversation in the active tab. Confirm the existing settings are respected.
4. With automatic assignment enabled, select "My assigned conversations" and confirm the selected agent is alerted when assignment finishes within the window.
5. Take over or resolve the conversation during the window and confirm the alert is cancelled. An out-of-office message alone should not cancel it.

title: fix: stop clearing the config cache on every read of falsy global configs
body:
## Description

`GlobalConfigService.load` returned early only when the cached value was `present?`. A stored
boolean `false` (any `type: boolean` config that is switched off) is not "present", so every
call fell through to the one-time ENV migration path: an `InstallationConfig.first_or_create`
plus an unconditional `GlobalConfig.clear_cache`. On a hot caller this means a DB roundtrip and
a full config cache wipe per call, and `clear_cache` itself ran a blocking Redis `KEYS` command
followed by one `EXPIRE` per key.

Three changes:

- `load` returns cached nonblank values and boolean `false`. Stored blank strings are still
  treated as unconfigured, preserving current behavior for installations that saved empty
  values (for example Firebase settings) from super admin.
- After a cached blank, the cache is cleared when the database lookup returns a configured
  value, including boolean `false`. This also handles a row created by a concurrent request;
  existing blank rows do not trigger a cache clear.
- `clear_cache` uses cursor-based `SCAN` followed by one multi-key `DEL` instead of `KEYS`,
  avoiding a single blocking keyspace scan.

The hot caller that surfaced this is fixed independently in
https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/pull/15899.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How Has This Been Tested?

New specs cover: a stored boolean false served from cache without clearing other cached
configs, an existing row with a blank value not clearing the cache, a stored empty string
still treated as unconfigured, and the create path clearing a stale cached nil. Existing
`GlobalConfig` cache specs pass unchanged. A deterministic two-reader probe also confirms
that concurrent configuration creation clears the stale cached nil and subsequent reads
are served from cache.

body:
# Pull Request Template

## Description

This PR adds table support to the email reply editor. Agents can insert tables from the editor menu, edit them in place, and send them as real HTML tables with inline styles that render reliably in Gmail and Outlook, in both light and dark mode.

It also fixes an issue where the reply editor stopped growing beyond 120px after visiting a Help Center article. `FullEditor.vue`'s global editor height cap was leaking into the reply editor, causing the message body to remain clipped when expanding or resizing the editor.

### https://github.com/chatwoot/prosemirror-schema/pull/60

### What changed

* `Channel::Email` formatting now enables the `table` node and `insertTable` menu item. Column resizing is disabled for messages.
* `ChatwootMarkdownRenderer` and `MarkdownRendererService` now enable CommonMarker's table extension.
* `BaseMarkdownRenderer` renders tables with inline styles and ensures empty cells retain their height.
* `MessageFormatter` fills empty markdown table cells so they render correctly in conversation bubbles and the quoted-reply preview.

title: feat(whatsapp): send campaigns in batches
body:
This MVP sends WhatsApp campaigns in batches of up to 100 contacts per background job, allowing other queued work to run between batches. Campaigns stay processing until the final batch finishes.

Batching lives in core and works in both Community and Enterprise editions. Enterprise continues recording recipient content and delivery status through its existing extension.

Related: https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-7891/batch-and-resume-large-campaign-sends

### Things to know

- Stacked on #15855; the base is `codex/paid-campaign-analytics`.
- Each job passes the last processed contact ID to the next job. No new table or migration is required.
- Audience labels are evaluated for each batch, so changing label membership while a campaign runs can change its remaining audience.
- This adds batching only. Manual resume and reliable recovery from an interrupted send remain separate work. Retrying a partially processed batch can resend messages, particularly in Community, which has no recipient tracking.
- Enterprise skips recipients already recorded as processed. A send accepted by WhatsApp before its result is saved can still be duplicated on retry.
- While sending, analytics explicitly labels counts, percentages, and delivery records as partial. Recipients appear as batches process them; this MVP does not prepare a frozen audience snapshot.
- Eligibility is checked when starting a campaign. An already queued batch chain can finish after a feature-flag change.

### How to test

1. Enable WhatsApp campaigns and create a campaign targeting a label with more than 100 contacts in a controlled test inbox.
2. Start the campaign with a worker consuming the low-priority queue. Confirm the first job processes at most 100 contacts and queues the next batch.
3. Confirm the campaign remains processing between batches and becomes completed after all eligible contacts have been processed.
4. In Enterprise, confirm analytics records sent, failed, and skipped recipients as batches run.
5. Repeat with Enterprise disabled to verify the same batching flow in Community.

title: fix: point to the emailed code in the device verification error
body:
## Description

Device verification returns its errors as server-rendered strings, and both the web login screen and the mobile app display them verbatim (inline on web, toast plus inline text on mobile). When a wrong code is submitted, the current message, "Invalid verification code", does not tell the user where the correct code actually is.

This matters most on mobile builds that predate [feat(auth): verify new devices with an emailed code on sign-in (chatwoot-mobile-app#1183)](https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot-mobile-app/pull/1183). Those builds reuse the MFA screen for the device verification challenge, so the on-screen copy points at an authenticator app. Device verification only triggers for users without MFA enabled, so those users have no authenticator code, and the emailed code is the only valid input. Since the error string comes from the server, updating it here reaches already-shipped app versions without an app update.

The message now reads: "Incorrect code. Enter the 6-digit code we sent to your email."

title: fix: rate-limit auth throttles read JSON request bodies
body:
## Description

The authentication rate-limit rules read request parameters with Rack's `req.params`, which only parses query strings and form bodies. The dashboard and mobile clients post JSON, so for those requests every key came back empty. Two consequences:

- The MFA/device-verification code submissions were not recognised as such (the `mfa_token` was invisible), so they were counted against the password-login throttles and the dedicated `mfa_login/*` throttles never fired.
- Code submissions carry no email, so the `login/email` discriminator resolved to an empty string. Because an empty string is a valid key, every code submission across the whole deployment shared a single bucket, effectively one global limit for all users.

This change adds a JSON-aware `auth_param` helper on the throttle request class that falls back to `ActionDispatch::Request` (which parses JSON) and returns nil for blank or non-string values, so a throttle keyed on a missing value skips instead of sharing one bucket. It is applied to the login, password-reset and resend-confirmation email throttles and to the MFA-login throttles. Parameter parsing is wrapped so a malformed body or an oversized/over-nested query can never raise out of a throttle. The blocked-event log line now records which rule matched.

Fixes https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-8264

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How Has This Been Tested?

Added `spec/initializers/rack_attack_spec.rb` covering the login, MFA-login, reset-password and resend-confirmation throttles for both JSON and form-encoded bodies: MFA submissions are exempted from the password throttles, a missing email skips instead of sharing a blank key, a non-string email and a malformed/over-nested body fail closed without raising, and the blocked-event log records the matched rule. Existing sessions and device-verification specs pass.
