title: fix(contacts): restore history ordering by recent activity
body:
Contact history can omit an older conversation even when it has recent activity. Ordering the limited history list by creation date puts newer, less recently active conversations ahead of it, affecting both the contact history UI and the contact conversations API.

This restores ordering by last activity, with ID as a stable tie-breaker, so recently active conversations appear in the history again.

Related: https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/pull/15427

### Things to know

The list remains limited to 25 conversations. Permission filtering and creation-date-based in-thread navigation are unchanged.

### How to reproduce

1. Use a contact with more than 25 conversations, including an older WhatsApp conversation outside the 25 newest by creation date.
2. Receive or send a message in that older conversation.
3. Open the contact's history. Before this fix, the conversation is omitted despite its recent activity.

### How to test

Repeat the steps above and confirm the older conversation appears near the top of the history. Confirm the contact conversations API returns it and that previous/next conversation navigation still follows creation order.

title: feat(whatsapp): restrict campaign analytics to paid plans
body:
WhatsApp campaign analytics uses the existing paid-feature and upgrade-message flow. Hacker accounts see a “View plans” message, while eligible paid accounts can open metrics and recipient details. Custom branding suppresses the upgrade message without granting access to a disabled feature.

## Closes

Fixes https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-7890/restrict-campaign-analytics-to-enterprice-plans-only

## What changed

- Adds `campaign_analytics` to the standard feature flags, all paid Cloud tiers, and self-hosted premium features.
- Mounts analytics only on Enterprise installations with the feature enabled and no applicable paywall. Uses the existing billing navigation and paywall components.
- Keeps the existing Enterprise analytics backend and its authorization unchanged. This PR adds no new backend plan enforcement or account-response entitlement fields.
- Stacked on #15854; merge that PR first.

## Rollout

Existing paid Cloud accounts need their plan features reconciled to enable the new flag. Adding the flag to the plan list does not backfill existing accounts by itself. Self-hosted installations use the normal premium-feature enablement flow; manually managed features keep their existing behavior.

## How to test

1. Open WhatsApp campaign analytics on a Hacker account: the upgrade message replaces analytics. “View plans” opens Billing settings.
2. Reconcile a Startups, Business, or Enterprise account and confirm an administrator can see analytics. Downgrade to Hacker and confirm the upgrade message returns.
3. On a custom-branded instance with the flag disabled, confirm neither analytics nor the Chatwoot upgrade message is shown. Enable the paid feature and confirm analytics loads.
4. Confirm the Community edition does not mount the Enterprise analytics content.


Shopify billing rollout: add `campaign_analytics` to every applicable paid plan in the deployment-managed `CHATWOOT_SHOPIFY_PLANS` catalog before reconciling those accounts. The repository intentionally ships an empty catalog; reconciliation uses each configured plan’s explicit feature list. This catalog update and the paid-account reconciliation are required deployment steps.

title: feat(api): support bearer authentication for existing API tokens
body:
Existing Chatwoot API tokens can now be sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on Application APIs, conversation direct uploads, and Platform APIs. The legacy `api_access_token` header remains supported, with the same token permissions and lifetime.

## Closes

Closes https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/issues/1615
Closes https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-2866/chore-standardise-the-access-token-based-authentication-in-chatwoot

## Why

A standard Authorization header works with common API clients and proxies that drop headers containing underscores. This provides the token transport needed for future OAuth support without adding OAuth issuance or changing authorization in this PR.

## What changed

- Accept existing user, agent bot, and platform app tokens through Bearer authentication.
- Preserve encoded dashboard Bearer authentication and existing account, bot, and platform resource restrictions.
- Give Bearer tokens precedence when both API headers are present; invalid Bearer tokens return 401.

## How to test

1. Call `/api/v1/profile` using an existing user token in `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; verify the same profile is returned using `api_access_token`.
2. Send different tokens in both headers and verify the Bearer token determines the authenticated identity. An invalid Bearer token returns 401 even when a valid legacy token is present.
3. Sign in to the dashboard and verify normal dashboard requests still work.
4. Use an agent bot token on an allowed conversation endpoint and for a conversation direct upload. Verify disallowed endpoints remain denied.
5. Use a platform app token on a permitted Platform API resource and verify an unpermitted resource remains denied.

title: fix: restore timezone-aware date filters without scan regression
body:
Date filters once again follow the user's local calendar day, without the performance regression that led to the rollback in #15815. A conversation created on September 7 at 9:49 PM in Brasília (September 8 at 00:49 UTC) now matches a `Created at < September 8` filter, the same way the day's report counts it.

Existing folders and contact segments keep their previous UTC behavior until they are opened and saved once, which records the browser's timezone on their date conditions.

### Closes

- Reintroduces #15784 after the rollback in #15815
- Support report: https://app.chatwoot.com/app/accounts/1/conversations/91709

### How to reproduce

1. Use a browser in `America/Sao_Paulo` and a conversation created at `2026-09-08 00:49 UTC`, which appears as September 7 at 9:49 PM locally.
2. Apply `Status = All`, `Created at > September 6`, and `Created at < September 8`, then save the folder.
3. Before this fix, the conversation is missing even though it appears in the September 7 report. With this fix, it appears in the folder and stays there after reloading.
4. Open an older folder with a date condition, save it once, and confirm it now uses local calendar days.

### What changed

- Local dates are converted to UTC boundaries before querying, so the timestamp column is compared directly and PostgreSQL can use its indexes. On 500,000 indexed timestamps, a selective filter went from a 150.57 ms sequential scan to a 0.95 ms index-only scan.
- `Days before` uses today's date in the saved timezone.
- Conversation lists compute the boundaries once per filter set instead of formatting every conversation.
- Invalid timezones return `422 Unprocessable Entity`.
- Automation rules and Captain audience conditions keep their existing behavior.

### Why not send UTC timestamps instead

Converting the local date to a UTC timestamp in the frontend fixes `is_less_than` and `is_greater_than`, but `Days before` needs today's date in the user's timezone at query time, so it would stay on UTC. Saved folders would also store timestamps that must be converted back to dates for editing. Saving the timezone fixes all three operators and keeps the stored value as the date the user picked.

title: fix: only apply HUMAN_AGENT tag to human replies outside the 24-hour window
body:
## Description

When `ENABLE_MESSENGER_CHANNEL_HUMAN_AGENT` or `ENABLE_INSTAGRAM_CHANNEL_HUMAN_AGENT` is enabled, every outgoing Meta message is currently sent with `messaging_type: MESSAGE_TAG` and `tag: HUMAN_AGENT` — regardless of who wrote it and whether the conversation is still inside the standard 24-hour window.

Meta only allows the HUMAN_AGENT tag on replies written by a human agent and sent after the 24-hour window has closed. Tagging automated replies (agent bots, Captain) violates the Messenger Platform policy, and tagging ordinary in-window replies is incorrect usage. Apps that enable the flag today are exposed to enforcement on the whole app.

This PR applies the tag only when both conditions hold:

- the sender is a human agent (`User`), and
- the last incoming message in the conversation is older than 24 hours.

Otherwise the message is sent exactly as it is today when the flag is off (`RESPONSE` for Facebook; no tag for Instagram).

The check lives in a small shared module, `Facebook::HumanAgentTagHelpers`, included by `Facebook::SendOnFacebookService` and `Instagram::BaseSendService`, so the three send paths — Messenger, Instagram Login and Instagram via a Facebook Page — share one rule. It reuses `Conversations::MessageWindowService::MESSAGING_WINDOW_24_HOURS` for the window length.

Automation rule messages have no sender, so they are never tagged. Macros run by an agent keep the agent as sender, so they are tagged outside the window, as a human-initiated reply should be.

Fixes #15887
Related: #14679

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How Has This Been Tested?

The existing HUMAN_AGENT specs were rewritten, because they encoded the behaviour being fixed or did not assert the payload at all:

- `send_on_facebook_service_spec` asserted that any message is tagged when the flag is on.
- `instagram/send_on_instagram_service_spec` enabled `ENABLE_MESSENGER_CHANNEL_HUMAN_AGENT` while the service reads `ENABLE_INSTAGRAM_CHANNEL_HUMAN_AGENT`, and only checked that `HTTParty.post` was called — so it passed whatever tag was sent.
- `instagram/messenger/send_on_instagram_service_spec` had the same `have_received(:post)` check without arguments.

Each of the three now covers:

- a human agent reply after the 24-hour window → tagged `HUMAN_AGENT`
- a human agent reply inside the window → not tagged
- an agent bot reply after the window → not tagged

Tests use `AgentBot` rather than `Captain::Assistant`, since the CE suite runs with `enterprise/` removed. Captain senders are covered by the same `User` check.

Run locally in CE mode, mirroring `run_foss_spec.yml` (`enterprise/` and `spec/enterprise/` removed, Ruby 3.4.4, `pgvector/pgvector:pg16`, Redis):

```
bundle exec rspec spec/services/facebook/send_on_facebook_service_spec.rb \
                  spec/services/instagram/send_on_instagram_service_spec.rb \
                  spec/services/instagram/messenger/send_on_instagram_service_spec.rb
```

- With this change: **37 examples, 0 failures**.
- Same specs against unmodified `develop` services: **37 examples, 6 failures** — exactly the six negative cases (in-window human reply, and agent bot reply after the window, for each of the three services). The new specs fail on the old behaviour and pass on the fix.
- `rubocop` on the eight changed files: no offenses.

title: fix: escape mention labels and sanitize the article diff panel

title: fix(voice): use Twilio API key credentials for recordings and outbound calls
body:
Call recordings and transcripts now work for Twilio voice inboxes set up with an API Key. Before this change, calls went through fine but the recording never showed up on the call and no transcript was created, because Chatwoot downloaded the recording with the wrong credential pair. Agent-initiated outbound calls had the same problem and now use the same credentials as the rest of the voice channel.

## How to reproduce

1. Create a Twilio inbox with voice enabled, using an API Key SID and API Key Secret.
2. Enable call recording and place a call, then end it.
3. The call works, but no recording is attached and no transcript appears. Logs show Twilio rejecting the recording download with a 401 (error 20003).

## What changed

- Added `basic_auth_credentials` on `Channel::TwilioSms`. OSS pairs `api_key_sid` (or `account_sid`) with `auth_token`; the enterprise override prefers `[api_key_sid, api_key_secret]` when both are set, mirroring the existing `client` override.
- The recording download and the Twilio media download now use `basic_auth_credentials`.
- The outbound voice adapter now uses `channel.client` instead of building its own client from `account_sid` and `auth_token`.

title: feat(reports): process durable monitor evaluations

body:

title: feat: account setting to enforce two-factor authentication
body:
# Pull Request Template

## Description

Adds an account-level setting, "Enforce two-factor authentication", that requires every member of the account to enrol in TOTP.

- New `enforce_mfa` key in account `settings`, editable by administrators from Account Settings. Available on all plans, and hidden when the installation has no Active Record encryption keys configured.
- A member without 2FA signing in with a password receives a `206` setup challenge and completes enrolment on the login page itself (QR or manual secret, verification, backup codes), then lands in the app authenticated. Nobody is ever locked out: the setup path is always completable.
- Sign-ins through Google or SAML are exempt, since the identity provider already applies a second factor. SAML members are also exempt from the token gate below.
- `api_access_token` requests from members who have not enrolled are rejected with `403` / `error_code: mfa_enrollment_required` for the enforcing account. Session-minting side doors are covered as well: account update, v1/v2 account creation, and conversation direct uploads. Profile MFA endpoints now require an interactive session, so an access token cannot enrol or manage 2FA by itself.
- Password reset and email confirmation no longer issue a session when the user still owes a second factor (enrolled or pending); they are redirected to sign in.
- While enforcement is on, members cannot disable their own 2FA (server-side `403`, and the profile UI shows a "required by your account" note). Backup code regeneration remains available.
- The setup challenge token is purpose-tagged and bound to the current password, the login MFA token now carries a typed claim, and new Rack::Attack buckets rate limit setup verification. As part of this, the auth throttles now parse JSON bodies; previously the `mfa_login/*` buckets never matched the web client's JSON sign-in requests.

Note for mobile clients: a password sign-in into an enforcing account returns `206` with `mfa_setup_required` and a readable `error` message. Un-enrolled users are intentionally hard-blocked on mobile until they enrol via the web app.

Ref: https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-8206

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

- Request/controller/model specs across sign-in, activation, token gates, reset/confirmation, and profile MFA endpoints, all guarded by the existing encryption-config skip and added to `run_mfa_spec.yml`.
- Component tests for the login enrolment wizard.
- Manual browser run on a local build: enable toggle as admin, forced enrolment with wrong and right codes, backup codes, subsequent sign-in challenge, API token gating, and blocked self-disable.

title: feat: add email delivery checks to the super admin panel
body: ## Description Adds an email delivery diagnostic to the super admin user page. When an address hard-bounces or gets a spam complaint, SES adds it to the account-level suppression list and silently drops every later email to it. The app still logs the send, so nobody sees a failure. This adds an **Email** menu on the super admin user page with: - **Check email delivery**: looks up the address on the SES suppression list and shows whether it is blocked, why (bounce or spam complaint) and since when. - **Unblock email**: removes a bounce entry after an in-app confirmation. Disabled for spam complaints, which need engineering. - **Send test email**: sends a plain-text email through the regular mailer path to confirm delivery end to end. - **Resend confirmation email**: the existing action, moved into the menu for unconfirmed users. Unblock and test email write a structured log line with the super admin and target user. Results show as a toast under the header actions on this page, so the page does not shift. The feature is inert unless `SES_SUPPRESSION_ROLE_ARN` is set: the actions return 404 and the page keeps the existing standalone resend confirmation button. SES calls assume that role from the instance profile, so the storage keys are never used. `SES_SUPPRESSION_REGION` overrides the default `us-east-1`. Adds the `aws-sdk-sesv2` gem. # Pull Request Template

## Description

This PR fixes the automation form crash when switching the event, for example from Conversation Created to Conversation Resolved.

Conversation Resolved rules can now use conversation and contact custom attributes as conditions, like the other conversation events.

title: chore: enable monitors and Captain Classifier for paid plans
body:
Conversation Monitors and Captain Classifier will be available to every paid Chatwoot Cloud account, including Stripe Startups, Business, and Enterprise customers and paid Shopify App Pricing customers. Existing accounts need the manual backfill below; future plan changes use billing reconciliation.

## Closes

- [CW-8305](https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-8305/enable-conversation-monitors-and-captain-classifier-for-all-paid-plans) — paid-plan entitlement rollout, child of [CW-8270](https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-8270/conversation-monitors-to-reports-with-jev)

## Type of change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

## What changed

- Grant `conversation_monitors` and `captain_classifier` from the Stripe Startups tier upward; Business and Enterprise inherit both. Downgrades to Hacker revoke plan-managed grants unless the account has a manual grant.
- Grant both flags to paid Shopify App Pricing accounts during billing reconciliation, alongside their catalog features. Shopify subscription loss removes the plan-managed flags; the catalog continues to manage other Shopify entitlements.
- Keep both flags available for manual grants in Super Admin.
- Restrict the minute-by-minute monitor dispatcher to accounts with active monitors so broader eligibility does not scan every paid account.

## Manual rollout

Run this one-off script in the **Chatwoot Cloud Rails console before deploying this PR**. It records existing pilot grants as manual overrides before the new reconciliation rules can remove them, then enables both flags for existing paid accounts. It is safe to rerun.

```ruby
raise 'Chatwoot Cloud only' unless ChatwootApp.chatwoot_cloud?

features = %w[conversation_monitors captain_classifier]
plans = %w[Startups Business Enterprise]

features.each do |feature|
  Account.public_send("feature_#{feature}").find_each(batch_size: 100) do |account|
    next if account.billing_provider == 'shopify' && Array(account.internal_attributes['shopify_managed_features']).include?(feature)

    manual = Array(account.internal_attributes['manually_managed_features'])
    next if manual.include?(feature)

    account.internal_attributes = account.internal_attributes.merge('manually_managed_features' => manual | [feature])
    account.save!(validate: false)
  end
end

stripe = Account.where("custom_attributes->>'plan_name' IN (?)", plans)
                .where("COALESCE(NULLIF(internal_attributes->>'billing_provider', ''), 'stripe') = 'stripe'")
shopify = Account.where("internal_attributes->>'billing_provider' = 'shopify'")
                 .where("custom_attributes->>'plan_name' <> ''")

[stripe, shopify].each do |scope|
  scope.find_each(batch_size: 100) do |account|
    next if account.billing_provider == 'shopify' && !Shopify::FeatureGate.enabled?(account: account)

    missing = features.reject { |feature| account.feature_enabled?(feature) }
    next if missing.empty?

    account.enable_features(*missing)
    account.save!(validate: false)
  end
end
```

After the backfill, deploy this PR. New upgrades and downgrades are handled by the billing reconciler. No database migration is included in the PR.

## Rollout notes

- Confirm `CAPTAIN_OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `CAPTAIN_OPENROUTER_DECISION_MODEL_ENDPOINT` are configured before enabling Captain Classifier for customers. The classifier calls OpenRouter directly and currently has no per-account credit metering or quota; monitor usage limits do not cover classifier requests. Check expected traffic and provider costs before rollout.

## How to test

1. On Chatwoot Cloud, confirm Hacker has neither feature without a manual grant. Upgrade a Stripe account to Startups, Business, and Enterprise; both features should be available at each paid tier.
2. Downgrade the Stripe account to Hacker; both plan-managed flags should become unavailable. A previously granted pilot account should retain its manual grants.
3. After the manual backfill, confirm existing paid accounts have both flags without waiting for another billing event. Open Reports → Monitors and check Captain Classifier suggestions in a conversation.
4. Confirm a paid Shopify Basic or Pro account receives both flags even if the Shopify catalog omits them, and loses them when its subscription ends. Other Shopify features continue to follow the catalog.
5. Confirm a self-hosted account is unchanged.

title: feat(whatsapp): add campaign history, batch sending, and paid-plan analytics
body:
Show sent WhatsApp campaigns in the conversation timeline so agents can see what the contact received. Send large campaigns in smaller batches, and make campaign analytics available on Business and Enterprise Cloud plans.

### What changed

- Display campaign content, title, timestamp, and delivery status in neutral message bubbles.
- Scope history to the contact, WhatsApp inbox, and conversation time window so saved campaign sends appear in the conversation active when they were sent, even when contact-inbox identities differ.
- Process campaign audiences in batches of 100.
- Keep live chat, SMS, and WhatsApp campaigns available on all paid Cloud plans through the shared campaigns feature flag.
- Show an analytics upgrade prompt on Startups; Hacker accounts do not have campaign access.
- Warn that deleting a campaign also removes its saved history and delivery details.

### Things to know

- History starts at the selected conversation’s creation time and ends before the next conversation for the same contact and inbox. Campaigns sent before the conversation started are excluded.
- The change does not backfill historical sends that have no saved campaign-recipient record.
- Replies are not explicitly attributed to campaigns.
- Analytics reflect progress so far while a campaign is sending.
- Durable resume and duplicate-send prevention remain follow-up work. Retried batches can resend messages on Community Edition; concurrent jobs or interruption between provider acceptance and saving delivery status can also cause duplicates.

### How to test

1. Open a WhatsApp conversation, then send a campaign to that contact. Reopen the conversation and confirm the campaign appears with its content, title, timestamp, and delivery status.
2. Repeat with a contact that has multiple WhatsApp identities in the same inbox. Confirm the campaign appears in the contact-and-inbox conversation active when it was sent.
3. Open two conversations for the same contact and inbox. Confirm each shows campaigns from its start time until the next conversation begins, and that earlier campaigns are excluded.
4. Load earlier campaign history and switch conversations; check ordering and scroll position.
5. Send a campaign to more than 100 contacts and confirm processing continues through subsequent batches.
6. Confirm Business and Enterprise accounts can access analytics. On Startups, confirm campaigns remain available and analytics shows an upgrade prompt. On Hacker, confirm campaign pages are unavailable.
7. Check the campaign deletion warning.

Related: https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-7891/batch-and-resume-large-campaign-sends

Related: https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-7825/persist-whatsapp-campaign-messages-and-attribute-replies-to-campaigns

title: fix: update rack-proxy for security advisory
body:
Updates `rack-proxy` to a patched release so the `bundle-audit` step in CI passes again. The refreshed advisory database flags the version in our lockfile, which currently fails the `security-scan` job on every open PR. `rack-proxy` is only used by the Vite dev server proxy, which is mounted in development and local test runs, so the app's request handling in production is not affected.

Fixes: GHSA-42qh-8mx8-7wqm

## How to reproduce

On `develop`, run:

```
bundle exec bundle-audit update
bundle exec bundle-audit check
```

It reports `rack-proxy 0.7.7` with the solution `upgrade to '>= 1.0.3'` and exits with a non-zero status.

## What changed

- Updates `rack-proxy` from 0.7.7 to 1.0.3, the patched version named in the advisory.
- Updates `vite_ruby` from 3.10.2 to 3.10.6. `rack-proxy` is a transitive dependency of `vite_ruby`, and 3.10.2 pins it to `~> 0.6`. Support for `rack-proxy` 1.0 landed in 3.10.5.
- Keeps `vite_ruby` on the 3.10 line on purpose. 3.11.0 detects the dev server by reading a `tmp/vite-ruby.json` file written by a newer `vite-plugin-ruby` than the 5.2.1 we use, so it needs to be taken together with a JS dependency update.
- Only `Gemfile.lock` changes. No other gems are updated.

title: feat(captain): trace Jev calls in Langfuse through a shared client
body: Captain label and priority suggestions and conversation monitors call Jev outside RubyLLM. Those requests were missing from Langfuse. ## What changed - Route both features through one System One HTTP client. - Record a Langfuse generation with the complete request and response, served model, reported token usage, cost, account, and conversation session. - Keep monitor credit accounting, response validation, scoring, and error mapping in its decision service. - Mark Jev's remote call as an OpenTelemetry client span and record its operation, returned model, conversation ID, and low-cardinality failure type. ## Langfuse v4 and OpenTelemetry review The existing exporter already uses OTLP/HTTP at `/api/public/otel/v1/traces`, Basic Auth, and `x-langfuse-ingestion-version: 4`. Each Jev call exports one completed generation span with its full request and response on the observation. The v4 migration does not require a new Langfuse API or SDK here. The new Jev fields follow the current OpenTelemetry GenAI client-span guidance while keeping the stable feature-specific span name. Jev's reported token counts are copied from its response. The full HTTP request body is captured, but Jev does not expose any internal representation it may build from that body. Higher token counts do not establish a specific hidden prompt or overhead. ## Verification - 103 focused RSpec examples passed for the shared Jev implementation; the four Jev client examples pass after the OpenTelemetry follow-up. RuboCop passes on the changed Ruby files. - Synthetic classifier and monitor calls succeeded locally. Langfuse returned one `GENERATION` observation for each call, with the request, response, model, usage, and cost. References: [Langfuse v4 custom ingestion](https://langfuse.com/integrations/native/opentelemetry/migration-to-v4), [Langfuse OTEL mapping](https://langfuse.com/integrations/native/opentelemetry), [OpenTelemetry GenAI client spans](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/main/docs/gen-ai/gen-ai-spans.md).

title: feat: add Captain conditions to automation rules
body:
# Pull Request Template

## Description

This PR adds a new automation condition, Captain detects / does not detect. Admins can describe what they want to check in plain English instead of matching keywords. Captain reads the message in context and checks whether the description applies, so rules can match the meaning of a message. For example, "I want my money back" can match a refund rule even when the word "refund" is not used.

It works with all automation events and can be combined with existing conditions using AND/OR. The condition is available for accounts with the `captain_classifier` feature enabled.

## How to test

1. Enable `captain_classifier` for the account and set `CAPTAIN_OPENROUTER_API_KEY` / `CAPTAIN_OPENROUTER_DECISION_MODEL_ENDPOINT`.
2. Go to Settings → Automations → Create. Select Message Created and add: Message Type = Incoming AND Captain detects "the customer is asking for a refund". Set the action to add a label.
3. As a customer, send "You charged me twice, I want my money back" → the label is applied.
4. Send "Thanks, all working now" → no label.
5. Send "I do NOT want a refund, just fix the bug" → no label, since Captain checks the meaning and not just keywords.
6. Switch the operator to does not detect and repeat steps 3–4 → the condition is inverted.
7. Edit the rule → the Captain condition should reopen with its text. Disable the feature → the Captain option disappears from the picker and saving an existing rule with the condition returns 422.

title: fix: drop the contact_inboxes foreign key on campaign_recipients
body:
## Description

`20260922090000_add_contact_inbox_to_campaign_recipients` added the `contact_inbox_id` column together with a database foreign key to `contact_inboxes`, in a single transaction. The column add takes an `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock on `campaign_recipients`, and the foreign key then needs a lock on `contact_inboxes`. Any in-flight transaction that has written to `contact_inboxes` and then reads `campaign_recipients` ends up waiting on the migration while the migration waits on it, so Postgres aborts the migration with `PG::TRDeadlockDetected`. On a busy install this happens on every attempt.

We manage associations in Rails rather than with database foreign keys (see https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/pull/8602#discussion_r1461694017), so this drops the foreign key:

- `20260922090000` now only adds the column and index. It touches a single table, so it cannot deadlock.
- `CampaignRecipient` already declares `belongs_to :contact_inbox, optional: true`, so no model change is needed.
- `AGENTS.md` documents the foreign key convention.

Follow-up to https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/pull/15854

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How Has This Been Tested?

- Fresh database: rolled the migration back and ran it again. The column and index exist and there is no foreign key to `contact_inboxes`.
- Reproduced the original deadlock in plain SQL with a concurrent transaction that writes `contact_inboxes` and then reads `campaign_recipients`; the column-only migration does not lock `contact_inboxes` at all.

title: feat(tools-manifest): add toolset manifest install service [PR-2]
body:
Adds the backend for installing Captain toolsets from the [chatwoot/tools](https://github.com/chatwoot/tools) repository. A toolset is addressed as `chatwoot/tools/<folder>` and pinned to a commit, either one passed in or the latest on the default branch. Installing the same commit again is a no-op, and a new commit updates the existing tools in place while keeping their slugs and the admin's enabled or disabled choice. Nothing calls these services yet; the API and UI come in the next PRs.

This is part 2 of a series of PRs that bring toolset manifest import to Captain, following #15995 (merged).

## Changes

- Custom tools record their source (repository, folder, tool id, commit, version).
- Install service that fetches a toolset from chatwoot/tools and installs it onto an assistant.
- Toolsets are validated before they are merged into chatwoot/tools, so Chatwoot only parses the manifest and fills in defaults. Every installed tool still goes through the custom tool model's validations (headers, endpoint safety, auth config), and the admin's install values are checked for type and required fields.
- Optional internal GitHub token for commit lookups, with fallback when it's rejected.

title: feat(tools-manifest): install Captain toolsets from GitHub [PR-3]
body:
Adds the API and install dialog for installing Captain toolsets from the [chatwoot/tools](https://github.com/chatwoot/tools) repository. The dialog takes `chatwoot/tools/<folder>`, previews the toolset and its tools, asks for the inputs and secrets it declares, and installs the latest commit from the default branch. If an older version is installed, it offers to update it. Installed tools show where they came from and are read-only, apart from enabling or disabling them. The dialog has no entry point on its own; the Tools Catalog in the next PR opens it.

Installs require the `custom_tools` plan and a new Super Admin switch, "Captain Tools Manifest", which is off by default.

This is part 3 of a series of PRs that bring toolset manifest import to Captain, following #15996 (merged).

## Changes

- Preview and install API for toolsets in chatwoot/tools, for administrators.
- Short, translated error messages for bad sources and configuration issues.
- Install dialog, opened by the Tools Catalog in the next PR.
- Installed tools show their source, open read-only, and can only be enabled or disabled.
- Tool titles open the side panel: editable for admins' own tools, read-only otherwise.

title: fix(whatsapp): restore contact info requests for bsuid conversations
body:
Agents can request a phone number again from eligible WhatsApp Cloud conversations identified by a BSUID. The action now checks availability when an agent opens a conversation whose contact has no phone number, and refreshes as the contact or request state changes.

Eligibility is fetched separately from conversation rendering, keeping pending-request history queries out of conversation lists. Existing checks still prevent duplicate pending requests and require an approved Request Contact Info template outside the messaging window.

Related: https://linear.app/chatwoot/project/whatsapp-bsuid-4df5614db3f9/issues

### Background: previous approach

[PR #15826](https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/pull/15826) temporarily hid the dedicated Request Contact Info action to remove pending-request message-history lookups from routine conversation rendering, including inbox lists, filtered lists, contact conversation lists, and individual conversation responses. These eligibility checks added database work to ordinary browsing. Checking only the messages loaded in the UI would also miss pending requests in older history, potentially showing an action that the backend would then reject.

This PR restores the action through a separate availability request for the selected WhatsApp Cloud conversation when the contact has no phone number. The endpoint retains the full pending-request check across conversations sharing the contact-inbox identity, while keeping history lookups out of conversation rendering as in #15826. History lookups still occur for the selected conversation's eligibility check; they are no longer part of routine list rendering.

### Things to know

- No database migrations or feature flags are required. The unused static `contact_info_request` field is removed from conversation responses; the dashboard reads availability from the dedicated endpoint. External clients consuming that field must use the endpoint instead.
- Availability requests are cancelled when switching conversations, and a pending request remains disabled even when its message is outside the loaded message history.
- The interactive request and customer phone-sharing response were manually verified end to end. The template flow outside the messaging window has not been tested live.
- Existing targeted validation passed: 29 Ruby service examples, 155 frontend tests, Ruby and JavaScript linting, and focused endpoint, authorization, and concurrent-request checks.

### How to reproduce

Open a WhatsApp Cloud conversation with a BSUID contact, no phone number, and an active messaging window. Before this fix, the Request Contact Info action is hidden because the conversation payload reports the capability as unavailable.

### How to test

1. Open an eligible WhatsApp Cloud conversation whose contact has no phone number. Confirm Request Contact Info appears in the composer.
2. Send the request. Confirm the action is disabled while a request is pending, including after reopening the conversation.
3. Share the phone number from WhatsApp. Confirm the contact is updated and the action disappears.
4. Switch between conversations while availability is loading. Confirm the action reflects the selected conversation.
5. Open a conversation outside the messaging window. With an approved Request Contact Info template, confirm the action opens the template picker; without one, confirm the action is hidden.

title: fix(voice): cancel the Twilio call leg when an agent ends a call before pickup
body:
Fixes a bug with outbound Twilio calls. If an agent hung up before the callee answered, the callee's phone kept ringing. If they then picked up, they heard hold music with nobody on the line. Now hanging up in the dashboard also hangs up the callee's Twilio call leg. A leg that still gets answered after the call has ended is sent `<Hangup/>` instead of an empty conference.

In production, 38 of 289 agent-ended outbound Twilio calls (13.1%) kept the callee's leg alive after teardown. 22 of them were answered into hold music, 12 rang on to `no-answer`, and 4 ended `busy`. That comes to about 49 minutes a month of billed Twilio audio with nobody on our side.

## Closes

-

## How to reproduce

1. Place an outbound call from a Twilio voice inbox to a phone you have with you.
2. While it is still ringing, hang up in the dashboard.
3. Before this fix, the phone keeps ringing, and answering it plays hold music. After this fix, it stops ringing right away.

## What changed

- `ConferenceService#terminate_call` hangs up `provider_call_id`, and also `parent_call_sid` when it is set and different, with `Status=completed`. It uses `call.inbox.channel.client`, so api-key mode works. `ConferenceController#destroy` calls it before `end_conference`, and both run before the call is finalized, so a failure still leaves the call repairable. `end_conference` stays as it was, because it handles the agent's leg and any other participants already in a live conference.
- Why `completed` in every state: Twilio documents that "Specifying `canceled` will attempt to hang up calls that are queued or ringing; however, it will not affect calls already in progress. Specifying `completed` will attempt to hang up a call even if it's already in progress." Sending `canceled` would silently do nothing if the callee answers while the request is in flight, and that is exactly this bug.
- For a leg that has already ended (the normal case, 251 of 289 calls), Twilio returns HTTP 200 and leaves the status unchanged. We tested this against a real account for both status values, on both `completed` and `no-answer` legs. So no rescue is needed.
- In `Twilio::VoiceController#call_twiml`, if the resolved call is already terminal, it now renders `<Hangup/>` instead of the conference TwiML. This covers the race where the callee answers while the hang-up request is in flight. The `reject_inbound?` path is unchanged.
- This also fixes the August bug where an inbound caller was stuck in hold music. When the conference was still in `init`, `end_conference`'s `status: 'in-progress'` query found nothing. `terminate_call` acts on the Call resource instead, so the conference state no longer matters.

## Out of scope (follow-ups)

- `useCallSession.js#endCall` has no in-flight lock (unlike `joinCall`'s `globalIsJoining`), so 18% of call_sids get duplicate `destroy` calls. Those are harmless now, because a hang-up on an ended leg returns 200.
- Outbound calls are marked `in_progress` when the agent joins the conference, not when the callee answers. So calls nobody answered still get a "completed" bubble.
- `Voice::Provider::Twilio::Adapter#twilio_client` pairs `account_sid` with `auth_token`, which is broken in api-key mode.

title: feat: forward emails from email conversations
body:
## Description

This PR adds support for forwarding emails from email conversations to any email address.

Agents can open the context menu on an email message and select **Forward email**. This opens a forward panel where they can add To, Cc and Bcc recipients, add an optional note, edit the forwarded content, manage attachments, and send the email.

The forwarded email is sent as a new email thread. The original contact is not included unless explicitly added as a recipient.

The outgoing message shows the To and Cc recipients along with a note that the contact cannot see the forwarded email. Bcc recipients are not shown.

Forwards without a recipient are rejected by the API. Retrying a failed forward also keeps the original recipients, forwarded content and edits instead of falling back to the contact.

Fixes https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-5011/feat-ability-to-forward-email-messages, https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/issues/6013, https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/issues/12691, https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/issues/14941, https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/issues/6673

## Type of change

* [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

## How Has This Been Tested?

### How to test

1. Open a conversation in an email inbox and hover over an email message. Open the three-dot menu and select **Forward email**.
2. Verify the forward panel is pre-filled with:
   * The current inbox as **Via**
   * Empty **To** and **Cc** fields, with a **Bcc** button to reveal the Bcc field
   * An optional note editor
   * A `---------- Forwarded message ---------` header with From, Date, Subject and To
   * The original email body
   * Original attachments as attachment chips
3. Add a recipient by searching for a contact or entering an email address. Verify **Send** stays disabled until at least one To recipient is added.
4. Add Cc and Bcc recipients. Verify the contact dropdown only opens for the field being edited.
5. Edit the forwarded body, add a note, remove an existing attachment and add a new one.
6. Use Cmd/Ctrl+Z while editing the forwarded body and verify the changes can be undone.
7. Send the forward and verify the outgoing message shows:
   `Forwarded to <to>, <cc> | <contact> cannot see this`
   Bcc recipients should not be shown. The outgoing bubble should contain the forwarded header, edited body, note and attachments.
8. Check the recipients' mailboxes and verify:
   * The subject starts with `Fwd: <original subject>`
   * The email starts a new thread without `In-Reply-To` or `References`
   * To, Cc and Bcc are delivered as entered
   * The note, edited content and attachments are included
9. Reply to the contact from the same conversation and verify the reply still targets the contact, not the forward recipients.
10. On a **seeded inbox with SMTP disabled**, send a forward so it fails. Retry it from the failed bubble and verify it still uses the forward recipients, forwarded content and edited body.
11. Via the API, create a message with `content_attributes[forwarded_message_id]` and no `to_emails`. Verify it returns `422`.
12. Regression test **New conversation** in an email inbox and verify Cc and Bcc still work as expected.

title: fix(imap): skip blank Reply-To addresses before normalizing sender
body:
Fixes #16019

`MailPresenter#from` previously chose a present `reply_to` array before checking its entries, then called `downcase` on every entry. `[nil]` is present in Rails, so a malformed Reply-To address list raises `NoMethodError`. The IMAP fetch job counts the exception and skips the message for six hours after three failures.

This removes nil/blank entries before downcasing. A Reply-To with no usable addresses falls back to From. If neither list has an address, the presenter returns `[]`, leaving the existing IMAP sender-validity check to ignore the mail. No changes to the fetch cache or unrelated sender parsing.

Regression specs cover mixed and empty address lists in the presenter, plus a synthetic raw-email fixture whose `Reply-To: <"">` parses as `[nil]`. The IMAP mailbox regression uses that fixture without stubbing `reply_to` and creates a conversation and message from the valid From address.

### Related issues

- Linear: [CW-8301](https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-8301/imap-mailpresenterfrom-calls-downcase-on-nil-and-the-message-is)
- Sentry: [CHATWOOT-FAZ](https://chatwoot-p3.sentry.io/issues/7696163347/)
- Sentry: [CHATWOOT-FEY](https://chatwoot-p3.sentry.io/issues/7708063382/)

title: feat(contacts): classify contacts as leads when they are created or updated
body:
Contacts now get the right type as they are created and updated. A contact becomes a lead when it has an email, a phone number or an identifier, when it has a conversation (clicking a campaign message counts, since that opens one), or when it was created on purpose through the contacts API, the dashboard or an import. Everyone else stays a visitor, and a lead never goes back to being a visitor.

This is the first phase of making `contact_type` the source of truth for contacts. Nothing reads the type differently yet, so the contact list, search, filters and exports behave as before on accounts without `crm_v2`. Existing contacts are not touched; the backfill is the next PR.

## Closes

Part of [CW-8316](https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-8316/contacts-contact-type-stale-contact-cleanup-and-opensearch-migration). This is phase 1 of 5, so the issue stays open.

## How to test

There is no UI for the type yet. Read it from the console with `Contact.find(id).contact_type`.

- Open a site with the widget and do nothing: the contact is a visitor.
- Send a first message from the widget: the contact becomes a lead.
- Click a campaign message in the widget without typing anything: the contact becomes a lead.
- Call `setUser` with only an identifier: lead.
- Create a contact with only a name, from the dashboard or with `POST /api/v1/accounts/:id/contacts`: lead.
- Import a CSV whose rows have only a name: every row is a lead.
- Create a contact on an API inbox with only a name: visitor, until its first conversation.
- Start a conversation from the dashboard with a contact that has no email, phone or identifier: lead.
- Merge a lead into a visitor: the surviving contact is a lead.
- Remove the email, phone and identifier from a lead: it stays a lead.

## What changed

- `Contacts::SyncAttributes` also promotes a visitor when it has an `identifier`.
- `Conversation` gets an `after_create` that marks a visitor contact as a lead. It runs inside the insert's transaction instead of after commit. The app runs `load_defaults 7.0`, so commit callbacks run in reverse declaration order, and one that raises skips the remaining commit callbacks of every record in the transaction, which would drop `conversation_created` and the first message's callbacks.
- `Api::V1::Accounts::ContactsController#create` builds the contact as a lead.
- `DataImport::ContactManager` builds new CSV rows as leads. `Contact.import` does not run save callbacks, so until now every new CSV contact was stored as a visitor, even with an email.
- `DataImports::Importer` (Freshdesk, Intercom) always imports contacts as leads and promotes a matched visitor.
- `ContactMergeAction` keeps the higher of the two types.
- No write reads the `crm_v2` flag, and the `contacts` table is unchanged.

## Things to know

- A contact's first conversation sends one extra `contact_updated` event to webhooks, the dashboard and the LeadSquared hook. Its `changed_attributes` names `contact_type`, which the payload itself does not carry.
- The contact row is updated inside the conversation's transaction, so it stays locked until that transaction commits. On Facebook that includes the attachment download.
- Conversations created by the Freshdesk and Intercom importers are inserted in bulk and do not run the new callback. The importer marks its contacts as leads directly.
- Accounts with `crm_v2` on already read `contact_type = lead` for the contact list, so they will see the newly promoted contacts.
- Captain prompts print the contact type. Anyone in a conversation now reads as a lead there.

title: feat: trigger automations from monitor matches
body:
## Description

Administrators can use an active conversation monitor as an automation event. They can create a rule from the automation screen or from the monitor list and report, then see linked rules on the monitor report. A rule fires when a live public message first makes the conversation match, whether that message is incoming or outgoing. Replies generated by another automation remain visible in monitor reporting but cannot trigger a linked rule; historical scans do not run actions. Pausing or deleting a monitor disables its linked rules, and resuming the monitor leaves them disabled until an administrator re-enables them.

## Type of change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

## Closes

- [CW-8304](https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-8304/trigger-automations-from-conversation-monitor-matches)

## How to test

1. Use an account with Reports, Conversation Monitors, and Automations enabled and a configured monitor provider.
2. Create a monitor, then create an automation with **Monitor matched** as its event and select that monitor. Confirm only active monitors are offered.
3. From the monitor list or report, create another automation and confirm the selected monitor is prefilled. After saving, confirm the monitor report shows the linked rule.
4. Send a new public incoming or outgoing message that first makes the monitor match. Confirm the rule's action runs. Send an automation-generated reply that alone matches the monitor, including immediately after a customer message, and confirm it records the match without running the linked rule. Confirm historical scans do not run actions and the same recorded match is not replayed.
5. Pause the monitor and confirm its linked rules become disabled. Resume it and confirm the rules stay disabled until explicitly re-enabled. Deleting a monitor should also disable its linked rules.

## What changed

- Added monitor event validation, account scoping, live activity attribution, durable delivery records, and action dispatch in Enterprise.
- Kept automation-generated replies in monitor reporting while excluding them from the action-eligible message context.
- Preserved live eligibility when a new message is updated before commit, and isolated delivery inserts so deleting a linked rule cannot discard the monitor match.
- Added the monitor event picker, rule status and search, monitor shortcuts, and linked rule list in the dashboard.
- Added coverage for API validation, delivery behavior, lifecycle changes, and frontend selection and navigation.

title: feat(companies): add Context.dev enrichment and redesign company pages
body:
Companies now fill in their own profile. When a company with a domain is added, Chatwoot looks it up on Context.dev and fills in the description, industry, employee count, location, phone and social profiles; admins can refresh a profile any time from the company page. The company page is also rebuilt so agents can see what's going on with an account at a glance: a profile card with key facts, then tabs for the company's conversations, notes and people.

Enrichment is part of the Business and Enterprise plans on Chatwoot Cloud. Startups accounts see an upgrade prompt when they try to refresh a profile, and Hacker accounts see an upgrade page for Companies. Self-hosted installs keep Companies free as before.

## Closes

- N/A

## How to test

**Enrichment (Business / Enterprise on Cloud, with `CONTEXT_DEV_API_KEY` set)**
1. Create a company with a real domain (e.g. `stripe.com`). After a few seconds its description, industry, employees, location and social links appear.
2. On the company page, click the refresh icon to re-fetch the profile. Manual edits to enriched fields are replaced by fresh data.

**Plan gating on Cloud**
1. On a Startups account, open a company and click refresh: an upgrade modal appears with a link to billing.
2. On a Hacker account, open Companies: an upgrade page is shown instead of the list, and company URLs show the same prompt.

**Company page**
1. Open a company with several contacts, conversations and notes.
2. Conversations: rows use the expanded conversation card grouped by date; use **Filter** (top right) to filter by status, assignee, inbox, team, priority or label; use **Load more** at the bottom.
3. Notes: search from the top bar; matches are highlighted. Long notes expand with **Show more**; the contact name links to the contact.
4. People: search and paginate; **Add** links an existing contact; the unlink icon removes one.
5. Open a conversation or contact and press back: the tab, filters and search are restored.
6. Click the pencil icon to edit company details, social profiles and custom attributes in the side panel.

**Custom attributes**
1. Settings → Custom Attributes now has a **Company** tab. Create an attribute, set it on a company from the edit panel, and it shows in the facts strip.

**Companies list**
1. The list shows each company's description, domain, industry, employees and location, 50 per page.

## What changed

- **Enrichment (Enterprise):** `Companies::EnrichmentService` (Context.dev by-domain lookup), `Companies::EnrichJob` on create, and `POST /companies/:id/enrichment` (admins only). Enriched data lives in `additional_attributes`.
- **Plans:** new `company_enrichment` feature flag added to the Business plan (Enterprise inherits it). A Cloud-only paywall list (`CLOUD_PAYWALLED_FEATURES`) in `usePolicy` shows the Companies paywall on Cloud without affecting self-hosted installs.
- **Conversations:** `Companies::ConversationFilterService` reuses `Conversations::FilterService`, scoped to the company's contacts (`POST /companies/:id/conversations/filter`). `ConversationCardExpanded` gets opt-in `selectable` and `conversationFirst` props; the main conversation list is unchanged.
- **APIs:** company conversations and notes are paginated with totals; people and notes accept a search query.
- **UI:** new detail page components (header, facts, conversation list and filters, notes feed, people list, edit panel). `TabBar` accepts an optional icon per tab.
- **Existing Business/Enterprise accounts** get `company_enrichment` on their next billing sync; a data migration to backfill it is not included yet.

title: feat(shopify): complete merchant onboarding from the app store
body:
Merchants installing Chatwoot from Shopify can create an account or sign in to an eligible existing workspace, then continue to Shopify billing setup. The installation destination follows them through email confirmation, invitation acceptance, password reset, Google sign-in, SAML, and MFA.

This is the final Shopify onboarding PR. Dashboard connections and the installation foundation have already merged in #16084 and #16085; this PR targets `develop` and completes the App Store signup and authentication flows.

### Closes

- Fixes https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-6500/support-shopify-app-store-install-flow-for-merchant-initiated
- Fixes https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/PLA-170/resolve-shopify-app-store-billing-rejection

### Things to know

- Shopify remains behind its feature flag. Shared signup, login, confirmation, password-reset, and account-routing code changes in this PR still require regression coverage with Shopify disabled.
- App Store onboarding uses Shopify billing. Existing Stripe customers continue connecting through the dashboard flow.
- Google signup rejection preserves the target workspace. Invalid or claimed installation tokens return a recoverable error, and invitation password-setup links preserve the installation continuation.
- Account membership creates notification settings within its transaction and reuses existing settings when an agent is re-added. Unrelated agent-cleanup, IMAP entitlement, and shared-plan lookup changes are excluded.
- No Shopify lookup-index migration is included; those indexes are deferred.
- Shop-scoped locking and database uniqueness enforcement are deferred. Concurrent signups using separate pending tokens for the same shop can create duplicate connections and block later App Store launches. Database transactions and model validation do not prevent this race. The installation/uninstall race is also deferred. Both are accepted risks, not fixed issues: https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/pull/13550#discussion_r4154926009 and https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/pull/13550#discussion_r4152556108.
- Configure the Shopify app URLs for the target environment. Webhook testing requires a reachable callback host.

### How to test

1. With Shopify enabled, install from a development store, create an account, confirm the email, and complete billing setup with a test plan. Verify the store is connected to the new workspace.
2. Repeat while signed out of an eligible existing workspace. Verify workspace selection and the installation destination survive email/password login, Google, SAML, and MFA.
3. Start with an unconfirmed invited administrator, resend confirmation, accept the invitation, and set a password. Verify onboarding resumes in the intended workspace.
4. Exercise password reset and confirmation resends from a Shopify continuation. Verify the installation token or billing destination and workspace are preserved.
5. Reject a personal Google signup and retry with the correct identity. Verify the target workspace is retained. Retry with an expired or claimed installation token and verify a recoverable error appears instead of a server error.
6. With Shopify disabled, verify ordinary signup, confirmation, invitation acceptance, login/logout, password reset/change, Google, SAML, and MFA. Check existing Stripe billing and account access.

title: fix(monitors): raise call limits and preserve quota retry holds
body:
Conversation monitors now allow **10,000,000 calls per UTC month** and **500,000 calls per UTC day**, per account. Allowances count attempted provider requests, including preview calls, and no longer depend on estimated token lengths. Pending evaluations retain their quota holds when new messages arrive and resume after the applicable reset without retrying ahead of a provider cooldown.

## What changed

- Enforce both call limits using persisted daily usage under the account lock, so concurrent workers cannot exceed the remaining allowance. Each attempted provider batch consumes one call, even when it evaluates multiple monitors or returns a provider error.
- Remove the daily token reservation and reconciliation, which mixed JSON request bytes with provider input tokens. Keep request-size limits and provider token/cost telemetry.
- Preserve daily and monthly quota holds across new conversation input. Spread retries over up to four hours after the later of the quota reset and the longest provider cooldown recorded across failed batches.
- Report when the current monthly allowance was reached, ignoring timestamps from the previous 100,000-call allowance.
- Document the RubyLLM bundle-audit exceptions for the pinned Ruby 3.4.4 runtime, with reassessment required when the runtime or supported dependency versions change.

## Quota logging

When a committed call reaches the daily or monthly account cap, emit one structured `conversation_monitor_limit_reached` log event for that period. It includes `account_id`, `period` (`daily` or `monthly`), `used`, `limit`, and the UTC reset timestamp `resets_at`. Rolled-back calls and subsequent blocked retries do not emit events. Reaching both caps in the same call emits one event for each period.

The event uses the existing Rails log forwarding path. In New Relic, group events by account and period with:

```sql
FROM Log
WITH aparse(message, '%"account_id":*,%') AS account_id,
     aparse(message, '%"period":"*"%') AS period
SELECT count(*)
WHERE message LIKE '%conversation_monitor_limit_reached%'
FACET account_id, period
SINCE 7 days ago
LIMIT MAX
```

## Closes

Fixes https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/INF-117

## How to reproduce

1. Exhaust an account's daily allowance, then receive additional conversation messages before the next UTC midnight. Previously, each message could pull the held work into an early retry and accumulate another job at the reset. The work now retains its saved retry time while recording the new input.
2. Have an earlier provider batch return a long `Retry-After`, then exhaust the daily or monthly allowance before the next batch. The saved retry now honors both the allowance reset and the longer provider cooldown before adding jitter.

## Rollout

Existing quota holds retain their saved retry times; the increased allowances apply when work next reserves a call. Already-scheduled jobs from before deployment will still run once.

title: refactor(slack): extract webhook signature verification into a shared verifier
body:
Moves Slack request signature verification out of the events webhook controller into `Integrations::Slack::SignatureVerifier`, so other Slack endpoints can reuse it. There is no change in behaviour for the events webhook.

This is split out of #16129, which adds a second Slack endpoint (interactive button clicks) that needs the same check.

## What changed

- New `Integrations::Slack::SignatureVerifier` with the signing secret lookup and the signature check, moved as they were from `Api::V1::Integrations::WebhooksController`.
- The events webhook controller calls the verifier. It still skips verification with a warning when no signing secret is configured, and still returns `401` for a missing, stale or invalid signature.
- `SignatureVerifier.valid?` returns `false` when no signing secret is configured. The events webhook never reaches that case because it checks for the secret first; it is there so a caller that requires a secret can use `valid?` alone.

title: feat(slack): refresh thread avatars and label Captain and super admin senders
body:
Messages Chatwoot posts into a Slack thread now show who sent them more clearly:

- Captain's replies are labelled **(Captain)** and use the Captain logo instead of the generic bot one.
- Contact, agent, bot and system messages get new, sharper avatars in one consistent style.
- Agents who are also super admins are now labelled **(Agent)**; they were shown as **(Bot)**.

This is split out of #16129. The borders for private notes and activity messages are in #16142; the two can merge in either order.

## How to test

1. Connect the Slack integration and start a conversation so a thread is created in the channel.
2. Let Captain reply in the conversation: in Slack the message shows as `<assistant name> (Captain)` with the Captain logo. A reply from another agent bot shows as `(Bot)` with the bot avatar.
3. From the dashboard, reply as an agent without a profile picture, and send a message as a contact: each shows its new default avatar in the thread. An agent with a profile picture still shows their own.
4. Reply from the dashboard as an agent who is also a super admin: the message is labelled `(Agent)`.
5. Resolve or reassign the conversation: the activity message appears in the thread under **System** with the new system avatar.

Slack caches avatars per message, so only messages posted after this change show the new ones.

## What changed

- `SendOnSlackService` maps each sender label to an avatar file explicitly. The avatars live under new file names in `public/integrations/slack/` so Slack fetches them fresh; `user.png` stays (redrawn) because the Dyte integration uses it as its default avatar.
- Agents without a profile picture now get the agent avatar. They were pointed at `agent.png`, which does not exist.

title: feat(tools-manifest): add a Tools Catalog to browse and install toolsets [PR-4]
body:
Admins can now browse the Captain tools catalog and install toolsets from it. A new "Tools Catalog" button on the tools page opens a page listing the toolsets published in [chatwoot/tools](https://github.com/chatwoot/tools), filterable by category. Clicking a toolset opens a side panel with its tools, the configuration it needs, and its README, with an Install button that opens the install preview from #15997. Toolsets the assistant already has are marked "Installed", or "Update available" when the catalog has a newer version. Each toolset shows its author, and toolsets authored by Chatwoot are listed first.

Toolsets can also be installed from a shareable link, `/captain/toolsets/install?source=chatwoot/tools/<folder>`. It opens the dashboard in the user's current account, asks which assistant to install to when there is more than one, and opens the install preview over that assistant's tools page.

This is part 4 of a series of PRs that bring toolset manifest import to Captain, stacked on #15997.

## How to test

1. In Super Admin, enable "Captain Tools Manifest". The Captain Tools Catalog URL defaults to `https://www.chatwoot.com/captain/tools`; locally, point it at a deployment that serves the catalog, for example `https://deploy-preview-322--chatwoot.netlify.app/captain/tools`.
2. On an account with the custom tools plan, open Captain > Tools and click "Tools Catalog".
3. Switch between category pills and check the cards filter.
4. Click a card, review the tools, configuration and README in the side panel, then click Install and complete the install.
5. Check you land back on the tools page with the new tools listed, and that the catalog now marks that toolset as installed.
6. Open `/captain/toolsets/install?source=chatwoot/tools/better-stack` as an admin. With more than one assistant, pick one, then complete or cancel the install and check you end up on that assistant's tools page.
7. Turn "Captain Tools Manifest" off and check the Tools Catalog button is hidden on the tools page.

## Changes

- `CAPTAIN_TOOLS_CATALOG_URL` installation config, exposed to the dashboard through the global config.
- Tools Catalog page at `/captain/:assistantId/tools/explore` with category pills and a three column card grid.
- Toolset details side panel with tools, configuration fields, README, and an Install button for admins.
- Installed and update available badges, backed by a new `GET captain/tools_manifest/installed` endpoint.
- Shareable install link at `/captain/toolsets/install?source=...`, with an assistant picker when the account has more than one.
- The "Captain Tools Manifest" setting only hides the Tools Catalog button; the preview and install APIs still enforce it. The catalog, its install actions and the install link stay behind the custom tools paywall.
- Custom tool templates no longer render with `strict_variables`, so `{% if response.error %}` and `| default:` work on optional fields. Liquid syntax errors still fail the call.
- Custom tool endpoint URLs may contain Liquid tags (`{% %}`); the save-time URL check ignores them, and SafeFetch still checks the real host on every call.
- The catalog is fetched from the browser without credentials, so the catalog host must allow cross-origin requests.

## Known limitations

- An install link opened while logged out, or in an account with no assistants yet, does not resume after login or assistant creation. Opening the link again works.

title: feat(stripe): view customer billing details in conversations
body:
Adds a read-only Stripe integration so support agents can view customer details, subscriptions, and recent invoices directly in the conversation sidebar without asking a teammate to look them up in Stripe.

Account administrators connect through OAuth and manage the connection from Settings → Integrations. Super Admin controls the Stripe app configuration. Sandbox and live connections are supported; Chatwoot's own subscription billing is unchanged.

### Things to know

- This is an initial read-only integration. Refunds, payment actions, and webhook-driven updates are not included.
- Customer lookup uses the conversation contact's email. When multiple Stripe customers match, the agent selects one. Billing data is scoped to conversations the agent can access.
- Customer matching uses Stripe Search with an exact case-insensitive email check. Newly created or edited customers may not appear immediately because of indexing delays. Stripe Search is unavailable to businesses in India; this integration currently shares that limitation. See [Stripe Search limitations](https://docs.stripe.com/search#limitations).
- Connections reuse integration hooks, with encrypted OAuth credentials and token refresh. No new database table is required. Active Record encryption must be configured.
- Configure the matching OAuth installation link and developer secret in Super Admin → Settings → Stripe. The Stripe app must allow the installation's `/stripe/callback` URL. Each installation uses one credential pair; changing environments requires reconnecting accounts.
- Disconnecting removes the local credentials. Uninstall the app in Stripe to revoke provider-side access.
- The sandbox flow has been exercised locally. Live-mode behavior has automated coverage, but live credentials, an internal live pilot, deployment, and Marketplace publishing are deferred.

### How to test

1. Configure a sandbox OAuth link and matching developer key in Super Admin → Settings → Stripe, with Active Record encryption enabled.
2. As an account administrator, open Settings → Integrations → Stripe and connect a sandbox. Confirm the connected account, environment, date, and dashboard link.
3. Create a Stripe customer whose email matches a Chatwoot contact, with a subscription and invoices. Open that contact's conversation and expand Stripe to see the customer, subscription status, and recent invoice amounts, dates, and statuses.
4. Check a contact with no email, no matching customer, and multiple matching customers. The sidebar should show the appropriate empty state or customer selector.
   Use a mixed-case email in Stripe to verify case-insensitive matching, and edit the contact email with the sidebar open to verify it reloads and clears the old customer selection. Allow time for Stripe's search index to update.
5. Confirm agents cannot manage the connection or retrieve Stripe data through an inaccessible conversation.
6. Disconnect and confirm the sidebar is no longer available. Live-account verification is a separate rollout step and has not been performed.

title: fix(stripe): log safe details for customer fetch failures
body:
Stripe customer lookups currently return `stripe_unavailable` without enough information to identify the underlying provider failure. This adds minimal server-side diagnostics for Stripe API and network errors while keeping the customer-facing response unchanged.

### What changed

Log the error class and, for Stripe API errors, the error code, HTTP status, and Stripe request ID. Raw response bodies, exception messages, credentials, and customer data are excluded.

### Things to know

Authentication and OAuth error handling remain unchanged. No migrations, configuration changes, or feature-flag changes are required.

### How to reproduce

With Stripe connected, a customer lookup that encounters a Stripe API or network error returns `stripe_unavailable`, but previously did not log the provider details.

### How to test

In a test environment, trigger a customer lookup with a simulated Stripe API failure. Confirm the response remains `422` with `stripe_unavailable` and the server log contains only the safe error details. Confirm successful customer lookups still display billing information normally.

title: fix(companies): attach logo on enrichment and label authorless notes as System
body:
Enriching a company now also sets its logo. Previously enrichment filled in the profile (industry, size, location, socials) but left the avatar untouched, so companies kept a low-resolution favicon or no logo at all, even after "Company profile refreshed." In the company notes feed, notes without an author now show as **System** with a gear icon instead of "Someone".

## How to reproduce

1. Open a company that has a domain but no logo (or only a blurry favicon), on an account with company enrichment enabled.
2. Click **Enrich**. The profile fields refresh, but the logo does not change.
3. Open the **Notes** tab for a company that has a note created without an agent (for example via automation or the API). The author shows as "Someone" with initials.

## What changed

- `Companies::EnrichmentService` attaches the Context.dev logo as the company avatar, preferring the square `icon` variant and falling back to the first logo.
- Automatic enrichment on company creation only fills a missing avatar. The manual **Enrich** action replaces the existing avatar, matching how it already overwrites other fields.
- Logos in formats avatars do not accept (such as SVG) are skipped and the existing avatar is kept.
- Authorless notes in the company notes feed render with the name "System" and a gear icon.

## Notes

- Companies created before favicon fetching existed still have no avatar until they are enriched or `rake companies:fetch_missing_avatars` is run.
- For newly created companies, the favicon job can attach before automatic enrichment finishes, in which case the favicon stays until someone clicks **Enrich**.
