title: perf: skip the account lookup when reading online users
body:
Presence pings from the dashboard, mobile app, and widget now run one less Postgres query each. Agents and visitors see no change in behavior.

## What changed

- `OnlineStatusTracker.get_available_user_ids` loaded the `Account` row only to reach `account_users`. It now queries `AccountUser` by `account_id` and plucks the user ids.
- `OnlineStatusTracker.get_availability_from_db` gets the same change. Its account lookup was served by the query cache until now, and would have become a real query once the first lookup was gone.

## Why

`RoomChannel#update_presence` calls `get_available_user_ids` on every ping. On Chatwoot Cloud that was one `Account` query per ping, about 367M a week, averaging 2.9 ms each as measured from the app. The method was written for auto-assignment, where one extra query per assignment costs little.

Auto-assignment and inbox agent availability call the same method and return the same results as before.

<details>
<summary>Benchmark</summary>

Based on local benchmarking of 40,000 pings over 5 threads, the change cuts Postgres queries from 2 per ping to 1. Throughput rose from about 1,050 pings a second to between 1,460 and 1,600. Median ping time fell from 4.1 ms to 2.8 ms.

The run used the production traffic mix of 7% agent pings and 93% widget pings. It ran against a local database and Redis in development mode, so absolute times in production will differ.

### Script

Save it as `presence_concurrent.rb` and run it with `bundle exec rails runner presence_concurrent.rb`. `TOTAL` and `THREADS` set the number of pings and threads. It reads Postgres only, and it writes presence heartbeats to the local Redis. The `Before` module is a copy of the method on `develop`, so both versions run in one process.

```ruby
# Runs presence pings from several threads at once, before and after the change.
# Reads Postgres only. Writes presence heartbeats to the local Redis, as a real ping does.
TOTAL = (ENV['TOTAL'] || 40_000).to_i
THREADS = (ENV['THREADS'] || 5).to_i
AGENT_SHARE = 7 # percent of pings that come from agents, as measured in production

# The method as it is on develop
module Before
  def self.get_available_users(account_id)
    user_ids = get_available_user_ids(account_id)
    return {} if user_ids.blank?

    user_availabilities = ::Redis::Alfred.hmget(OnlineStatusTracker.status_key(account_id), user_ids)
    user_ids.map.with_index { |id, index| [id, (user_availabilities[index] || OnlineStatusTracker.get_availability_from_db(account_id, id))] }.to_h
  end

  def self.get_available_user_ids(account_id)
    account = Account.find(account_id)
    range_start = (Time.zone.now - OnlineStatusTracker::PRESENCE_DURATION).to_i
    user_ids = ::Redis::Alfred.zrangebyscore(OnlineStatusTracker.presence_key(account_id, 'User'), range_start, '+inf')
    user_ids += account.account_users.where(auto_offline: false)&.map(&:user_id)&.map(&:to_s)
    user_ids.uniq
  end
end

PG_QUERIES = Concurrent::AtomicFixnum.new
ActiveSupport::Notifications.subscribe('sql.active_record') do |*, payload|
  PG_QUERIES.increment if !payload[:cached] && payload[:name] != 'SCHEMA' && payload[:name].present?
end

accounts = Account.where(id: Conversation.distinct.pluck(:account_id)).to_a
users = accounts.flat_map { |a| a.account_users.pluck(:user_id).map { |id| [a.id, 'User', id] } }
contacts = accounts.flat_map { |a| a.contacts.limit(3000).pluck(:id).map { |id| [a.id, 'Contact', id] } }
random = Random.new(42)
work = Array.new(TOTAL) { random.rand(100) < AGENT_SHARE ? users.sample(random: random) : contacts.sample(random: random) }
puts "accounts=#{accounts.size} users=#{users.size} contacts=#{contacts.size} threads=#{THREADS} db_pool=#{ActiveRecord::Base.connection_pool.size} env=#{Rails.env}"

# One ping, as RoomChannel#update_presence runs it inside the Rails executor
ping = lambda do |tracker, account_id, type, id|
  Rails.application.executor.wrap do
    OnlineStatusTracker.update_presence(account_id, type, id)
    data = { account_id: account_id, users: tracker.get_available_users(account_id) }
    data[:contacts] = OnlineStatusTracker.get_available_contacts(account_id) if type == 'User'
    data
  end
end

run = lambda do |tracker|
  queue = Queue.new
  work.each { |item| queue << item }
  latencies = Array.new(THREADS) { [] }
  PG_QUERIES.value = 0
  started = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
  THREADS.times.map do |index|
    Thread.new do
      loop do
        item = begin
          queue.pop(true)
        rescue ThreadError
          break
        end
        t0 = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
        ping.call(tracker, *item)
        latencies[index] << (Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) - t0) * 1000
      end
    end
  end.each(&:join)
  elapsed = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) - started
  all = latencies.flatten.sort
  { elapsed: elapsed, rate: TOTAL / elapsed, avg: all.sum / all.size, p50: all[all.size / 2], p95: all[(all.size * 0.95).to_i],
    p99: all[(all.size * 0.99).to_i], pg: PG_QUERIES.value }
end

work.first(500).each { |item| ping.call(Before, *item) && ping.call(OnlineStatusTracker, *item) }

[['before', Before], ['after', OnlineStatusTracker], ['before', Before], ['after', OnlineStatusTracker]].each do |label, tracker|
  r = run.call(tracker)
  puts format('%-7s %6.1f s  %6.0f pings/s  avg %.2f ms  p50 %.2f  p95 %.2f  p99 %.2f  postgres queries %d (%.2f per ping)',
              label, r[:elapsed], r[:rate], r[:avg], r[:p50], r[:p95], r[:p99], r[:pg], r[:pg] / TOTAL.to_f)
end
```

</details>

title: chore: guard against migration version collisions
body:
## Description

Migrations with hand-written, rounded versions (e.g. `20260925000000`) keep colliding across branches. Git merges two such files cleanly because the filenames differ, and spec CI stays green because it loads the schema instead of running migrations. The failure only shows up on a real `db:migrate`: a `DuplicateMigrationVersionError`, or a database that already recorded one branch's migration silently skipping the other.

This adds:
- A `Migration Version Check` workflow on PRs that touch `db/migrate`. It fails when a migration added or renamed in the PR has a version ending in `0000`, and when two files in `db/migrate` share a version. Existing migrations are not flagged.
- An `AGENTS.md` rule to create migrations with `rails g migration` instead of writing the version by hand.

Linear: https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/INF-118

## Type of change

CI and contributor guidelines only, no app code changes.

## How Has This Been Tested?

Ran both steps locally against simulated PR merge commits on top of develop: a generated timestamp passes, `...000000` and `...090000` versions fail, renaming a migration to a rounded version fails, and a duplicate of an existing version fails. Develop as-is passes both checks.

title: perf: count assignment rate limits with a sorted set instead of scanning the keyspace
body:
## Description

`AutoAssignment::RateLimiter` counted an agent's recent assignments with `Redis::Alfred.keys_count`, which runs `SCAN` over the whole keyspace once per candidate agent per conversation on every assignment run. On a large keyspace that is thousands of round trips per check, and the cost scales with keyspace size rather than with assignments.

This stores assignments in one sorted set per inbox and agent (member: conversation id, score: assignment time), trims entries older than the window on write, expires the key with the window, and counts with `ZCOUNT`. Limits, windows and defaults are unchanged.

Existing per-assignment keys are not migrated: windows in progress at deploy time reset, and the old keys expire on their own.

Fixes https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/INF-116

## Type of change

## How Has This Been Tested?

`bundle exec rspec spec/services/auto_assignment spec/jobs/auto_assignment` (62 examples, 0 failures). The rate limiter spec now asserts Redis state directly, including trimming and the sliding window via `travel_to`.

title: fix: send post from super admin post_to buttons

The "Unblock" button on the Super Admin user page returned a 404, so support could not unblock a bounced email address. The button now works again. The "Resend confirmation email" button on installs without SES suppression configured had the same problem and is fixed too.

## How to reproduce

2. Click **More** → **Check email delivery**.

title: fix: scale message bubble text with the font size setting
body:
List items in a message bubble now render at the same font size as the paragraphs around them. Before this change, a user who picked a non-default font size in profile settings saw list items at a different size from the rest of the message.

## How to reproduce

1. Go to Profile settings and set the font size to Small.
2. Open a conversation that has a message with a paragraph followed by a numbered or bulleted list.
3. Inspect the paragraph and a list item. The paragraph is 13.125px and the list item is 14px.

## What changed

The bubble prose style set its base font size to `14px`. Paragraphs take their size from the global `p` rule, which uses `0.875rem`. The font size setting changes the root font size, so paragraphs scaled and list items did not. The bubble base size is now `0.875rem`. At the default setting the text is still 14px.

Email bubbles and the forward editor use the same prose style, so they get the same change.

title: fix(auto-assignment): enqueue Assignment V2 job after the creating transaction commits
body:
With Assignment V2 enabled, a newly created conversation could stay unassigned even with an online agent available: the `AssignmentJob` was enqueued from `after_save`, inside the transaction creating the conversation, so a fast worker scanned the inbox before the row committed, assigned 0 conversations, and nothing ever retried for inboxes without an assignment policy.

#### Closes

Closes https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/issues/16134

#### How to reproduce

1. Enable Assignment V2 and inbox auto-assignment (no assignment policy needed).
2. Create a conversation from an incoming message (conversation creation runs inside a surrounding transaction).
3. Watch the logs: `AssignmentJob` starts within a few ms and logs `Assigned 0 conversations for inbox <id>`; the conversation stays unassigned until some other conversation in the inbox changes status.

#### What changed

- `AutoAssignmentHandler#run_auto_assignment` now defers the V2 enqueue with `ActiveRecord.after_all_transactions_commit`, so the job is only queued once the creating/status-changing transaction has committed and its scan can actually see the conversation. On rollback nothing is enqueued. The legacy V1 paths (inline `before_save` assignment and the post-save service call for new conversations) are unchanged, as is the per-inbox coalescing in `enqueue_for_inbox`.
- Verified with a standalone ActiveRecord 7.2.3.1 harness that loads the real concern and gives the job's scan its own connection (a separate worker can only see committed rows): unpatched, a create inside a transaction enqueues while still inside it and the scan sees 0 unassigned conversations (the reported symptom); patched, nothing is enqueued inside the transaction, the post-commit scan sees 1, and a rolled-back create enqueues nothing. Full RSpec was not run locally (needs Postgres/Redis and the full bundle in this environment) — CI is authoritative.

title: perf: load widget request context in fewer queries
body:
Widget requests run fewer database queries. The widget gets the same responses as before.

## What changed

- `WebsiteTokenHelper#set_web_widget` loads the web widget, its inbox, and the account in one joined query. It ran one query for each.
- `WebsiteTokenHelper#set_contact` loads the contact inbox and the contact in one joined query. It ran one query for each.
- `Api::V1::Widget::InboxMembersController#index` preloads `account_users` for the inbox members.
- The inbox members view picks the account user from the preloaded rows. It called `find_by` on the association, which queries once per member.

## Why

Every widget request runs the setup in `WebsiteTokenHelper` before its action. On Chatwoot Cloud over 7 days, the widget endpoints below ran about 230M times, and each ran these five setup queries at about 2 ms each as measured from the app.

| Endpoint | Calls | Average |
|---|---|---|
| `widget/messages#index` | 65.0M | 40.0 ms |
| `widget/conversations#index` | 64.7M | 34.9 ms |
| `widget/contacts#show` | 48.7M | 27.6 ms |
| `widget/campaigns#index` | 18.9M | 24.1 ms |
| `widget/inbox_members#index` | 15.9M | 65.6 ms |
| `widget/contacts#update` | 14.9M | 48.6 ms |

`widget/contacts#show` runs the five setup queries and nothing else.

`widget/inbox_members#index` also averaged 8.5 `AccountUser` queries per request, one per inbox member.

## Results

Local replay of one average production minute of widget GET traffic. The request counts are the 7-day production totals divided by 10,080 minutes, 21,138 requests in all. 16% of the visitors have a conversation, which matches the share of message requests that load messages in production. Both runs replay the same shuffled sequence through the full Rails stack.

| | Before | After | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Postgres queries | 141,129 | 67,995 | 52% fewer |
| Total time | 306.4 s | 234.5 s | 23% less |

| Endpoint | Queries per request before | after | Average time before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `messages` | 7.10 | 4.26 | 15.1 ms | 12.6 ms |
| `conversations` | 6.00 | 3.00 | 12.4 ms | 10.1 ms |
| `contact` | 5.00 | 2.00 | 10.9 ms | 8.7 ms |
| `campaigns` | 4.00 | 2.00 | 9.2 ms | 7.5 ms |
| `inbox_members` | 16.00 | 5.00 | 37.7 ms | 20.7 ms |

The JSON response is identical before and after for all five endpoints. The inbox used for the replay has 10 members.

`messages` drops by 2 queries when messages are rendered, not 3. Rendering a message loads the account again. The query cache answered that from the first lookup before. The account now arrives through a join, so the later lookup is a real query.

## Not changed

`WidgetsController` and `Api::V1::Widget::ConfigsController` have their own versions of these lookups. They are left as they are.

Release notes

Sourced from axios's releases.

v1.20.0 — August 19, 2026

This release hardens runtime option handling, adds RFC 9110 status-code aliases, fixes Node.js and XHR reliability issues, and refreshes project tooling and documentation.

⚠️ Breaking Changes & Deprecations

  • HTTP Status Naming: Added ContentTooLarge (413) and UnprocessableContent (422), while retaining PayloadTooLarge and UnprocessableEntity as backward-compatible deprecated aliases. (#11082)

🔒 Security Fixes

  • Runtime Option Handling: Hardened behavioral configuration reads against shared and foreign prototype pollution and normalized unsafe interceptor replacement objects. This also clarifies Fetch redirect and custom implementation behavior, HTTP/2 DNS and proxy handling, CIDR-based NO_PROXY matching, and malformed data URI rejection; see the PR for documented compatibility effects. (#11141)

🐛 Bug Fixes

  • Interceptor Lifecycle: Prevented unbounded handler-array growth by trimming trailing ejected interceptors without changing iteration semantics, and kept interceptor operations safe when the public handlers field is nullish. (#11087, #11118)
  • Request Error Preservation: Prevented custom Error.prepareStackTrace implementations that return non-string values from replacing the original request failure with an unrelated TypeError. (#11109)
  • XHR Reliability: Navigation-canceled requests now reject with ECONNABORTED instead of resolving with status 0, while successful downloads flush their final progress callback during the live loadend dispatch. (#11094, #11121)
  • Node.js Socket Memory: Removed request-context retention from per-socket error listeners, preventing completed response data from being pinned for the lifetime of pooled keep-alive sockets. (#11091)
  • Core Methods and HTTP Errors: Prevented structural method-header buckets from leaking into outgoing headers, standardized invalid DNS lookup and httpVersion failures as AxiosError.ERR_BAD_OPTION_VALUE, and corrected the timeoutErrorMessage merge strategy. (#11096)

title: feat(contacts): use company selector for enabled accounts
body:
Contacts use the company selector when Companies is enabled, including contacts that still have a legacy free-text company name.

## Why
Legacy contacts could not choose a company record while their free-text name was present. Automatically resolving that name on every contact save also affected API and import paths outside this UI change.

## What this change does
- Shows the existing selector in the contact detail and conversation edit forms; Companies-disabled accounts keep the free-text field.
- On dashboard contact saves, links an unlinked legacy name to the first exact-name company or creates one if none exists. Users can clear the legacy name directly in the selector.
- Keeps the linked company name mirrored in `additional_attributes.company_name` for existing readers.
- Leaves CSV import association for a follow-up. Imports continue to write the free-text company-name attribute without creating or linking company records.

## Validation
- In a Companies-enabled account, open a contact with a legacy company name and no linked company. Save it and confirm the company record is linked; repeat with an existing same-name company to confirm it is reused.
- Use the selector's clear option and save to confirm the legacy name is removed without a company link.
- Import a contact with a company name and confirm the free-text attribute is preserved without an automatic link.
- In a Companies-disabled account, confirm the original free-text company field remains.

title: feat: add user diagnostics page to super admin
body: ## Description Support can't see which build of the mobile app a user is on, or why their push notifications aren't arriving, without log access. A recent ticket had an agent reporting an iOS freeze while insisting they were on the latest build — their sessions showed 4.8.5 against a shipped 4.9.1, and nobody on the thread could check that. The console already had a Push Diagnostics page with its own user lookup, identity card and subscription table. Rather than add a second page repeating all three, this renames it **User Diagnostics**, moves it under **Monitor** in the redesigned Super Admin, and adds the mobile and web session data to it. One lookup, three tabs. The user card at the top matches the user details page header: avatar, name, ID, email and the accounts the user belongs to, with a link through to the full user page. **Push delivery** — notification settings, registered devices, test send. Settings come first because `Notification::PushNotificationService` checks them once before the subscription loop: every type off means no push on any device, however healthy the registrations look. An account with every type off is called out in an amber notice. **Mobile app** — app version, platform, OS, device and activity per session, from the `X-Chatwoot-*` headers the app sends on every request. Sessions predating app 4.8.0 show as legacy builds. **Web** — browser, version, operating system and activity per browser session, read from the user agent. Both session tabs list only sessions whose auth token is still valid, the same filter the profile sessions endpoint uses. A `user_sessions` row outlives its token, so without it a device that was signed out or whose token expired would still be presented as a currently installed build. Tabs with nothing to show render an empty state. The page is reachable from the Monitor section and from the dashboard shortcuts. Read-only apart from the test-send and delete actions Push Diagnostics already shipped. Device attributes render from an allowlist, tokens are cut to a six-character tail for log correlation, and no conversation, contact, IP or location data is shown. ## Closes Fixes [CW-8030](https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-8030/add-mobile-app-diagnostics-page-to-super-admin) ## How to test 1. Open `/super_admin` → **Monitor** → **User Diagnostics** (or the **User Diagnostics** dashboard shortcut) and look up a user by email or numeric ID. 2. **Push delivery**: one column per account, SLA rows only for SLA-enabled accounts, and an account with every type off called out under the table. Select devices to send a test push or delete stale registrations. 3. **Mobile app**: sessions list app version, OS and device. Sign the user out of a device (or let its token expire) and the session drops off the list. 4. **Web**: browser sessions list browser, version and operating system; mobile sessions don't appear here. 5. Look up a user with no sessions or registrations: each tab shows an empty state. 6. `/super_admin/push_diagnostics` redirects to the push tab with the lookup preserved. ## Type of change - [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) ## What changed - `PushDiagnosticsController` becomes `UserDiagnosticsController` at `/super_admin/user_diagnostics`; the old path redirects to `?tab=push`. The Monitor navigation and dashboard shortcut point at the new page. - Sessions are filtered to client IDs with an unexpired token before being split into mobile and web. - Views use the redesigned Super Admin partials (`section`, `card`, `table`, `badge`, `button`). `card` takes an optional `count:` that renders as a badge beside the title. - The subscription table renders once, with allowlisted attributes and truncated identifiers, replacing the previous raw `subscription_attributes` dump. - `update_activity!` refreshes client metadata through `RequestDeviceInfo`, so a user who upgrades without signing in again no longer reports their old version. - Push Diagnostics copy moves into `en.yml` alongside the new strings. - No `chatwoot_cloud?` gate: `user_sessions` are populated on every install and the app supports self-hosted. ## Checklist: - [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project - [x] I have performed a self-review of my code - [x] I have commented on my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas - [x] My changes generate no new warnings - [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works - [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

title: feat: encrypt Captain custom tool credentials
body:
Captain custom tools stored `auth_config` and `headers` as plain JSON. This encrypts both with Active Record encryption when encryption keys are configured. Installs without keys keep the current behaviour.

Existing plaintext rows still read correctly. A row becomes encrypted the next time it is saved. A follow-up PR backfills the remaining rows and should ship in a later release, because code without this change cannot read encrypted rows.

Rails also adds both params to the request log filters, so header values no longer appear in logs.

Ad-hoc smoke tests ran locally with encryption enabled and disabled. They covered old plaintext rows, new encrypted rows, empty and `NULL` values, 5 MB values, updates, all three auth types, validations, and the API for admins and agents. The existing custom tool specs pass with and without keys.

title: chore: backfill encryption for Captain custom tool credentials
body:
Encrypts `auth_config` and `headers` on existing Captain custom tools. It follows the PR that added encryption to the model, and is stacked on that branch.

Merge this only after the model change has been released. Code without that change reads encrypted rows as ciphertext, so running this during the same rolling deploy would break tool credentials.

The migration does nothing when encryption keys are not configured. It does not change `updated_at`. `down` decrypts the rows again.

Ad-hoc smoke tests ran locally. Old plaintext rows read the same values after the migration, including `NULL`, empty, and 5 MB values. Running it twice changed nothing, and `down` restored plaintext.

title: fix: quote professional email sender names per RFC 5322
body:
Outgoing emails failed on inboxes that use the professional sender name and have a comma in the inbox or business name. The sender name is now quoted, so these emails are delivered.

## The bug

A comma separates addresses in an email header. An inbox named `Care Team, Billing` produced a From header that could not be parsed into one mailbox. The SMTP envelope sender then fell back to the whole raw string, and the provider rejected the email.

| | From header | SMTP envelope |
|---|---|---|
| Before | `Care Team, Billing <care@example.com>` | `MAIL FROM:<Care Team, Billing <care@example.com>>`, rejected by Gmail with `555 5.5.2 Syntax error` |
| After | `"Care Team, Billing" <care@example.com>` | `MAIL FROM:<care@example.com>`, accepted |

Recipients see the same sender name. Mail clients remove the quotes on display. A name without special characters, such as `Care Team`, produces the same header as before.

## How to reproduce

1. Open an email inbox that sends through SMTP.
2. Set the sender name to the professional format.
3. Set the inbox name or business name to `Care Team, Billing`.
4. Send a reply from a conversation in that inbox.
5. Before this change, the message fails to send. After it, the message is delivered.

## What changed

- The professional sender name is built with `Mail::Address`, which quotes the display name when it needs quoting.
- If `Mail::Address` cannot parse the email address, the code keeps the old plain string. `Email::SenderNameBuilder` does the same for the friendly name.
- Removed the `professional_name` locale key from `en.yml`. Nothing reads it now.

## Related

Replaces #15278. That PR fixed both the friendly and the professional sender name. #15459 has since fixed the friendly name on `develop`, so only the professional name remained.

title: refactor: use Responses for OpenAI text inference
body:
Captain and Copilot text requests use OpenAI's Responses API on the standard OpenAI endpoint, including the editor, FAQ and help-center services, PDF FAQ generation, and inactive-conversation completion. Tool calls and structured replies retain their existing contracts. Langfuse records the API protocol, requested reasoning effort, and actual reasoning token usage.

Super Admin model additions and saved effort controls are handled separately in #16178 (CW-8336). Existing feature models and routing defaults are preserved. Custom OpenAI endpoints retain their existing protocol behavior. Audio transcription and embeddings keep their dedicated APIs.

## Closes

https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-8335/move-assistant-and-copilot-to-responses-endpoint

## How to test

1. Select an existing OpenAI model for Assistant, Copilot, editor and FAQ features through Super Admin. Send a Playground message that uses a tool, retrieve a test contact through Copilot, and rewrite a message.
2. Generate FAQs from document text and a PDF. Check valid structured results and FAQ matching. Responses JSON input must contain the JSON instruction even when the system prompt already specifies it.
3. Test inactive pending conversations with evaluated inactivity resolution enabled. Confirm that an answered question resolves and a promised human follow-up hands off, with saved private notes.
4. Check Langfuse for the expected model and `api_protocol=responses`. Requested effort is separate from actual reasoning token usage, which can be zero.
5. Continue an existing conversation and check saved replies, tools and session history. With a custom endpoint, verify existing protocol and supported temperature behavior.

## What changed

- Uses shared Responses request configuration across OpenAI text services and retains provider-specific behavior for other models.
- Preserves schema contracts, JSON mode, and PDF file input while parsing Responses output after reasoning items.
- Records protocol, requested effort, effective temperature and reasoning token usage in generation instrumentation.

title: feat(copilot): add chat history
body: ## Summary - Add Past chats and New chat actions to the existing Copilot sidebar. - List the current agent's chats newest first and load older pages on demand. - Restore every message from a selected chat while preserving the assistant saved on that chat. ## Scope This is intentionally the smallest base for the Copilot stack. It does not add Copilot settings, a model selector, or a new account-level assistant override. New chats continue to use the existing preferred assistant, inbox assistant, then first assistant behavior. ## Verification - Focused request specs: 17 examples passed. - Relevant frontend lint passed. - Verified new chat, past-chat ordering, and restored messages directly in the local Cook environment on desktop and at the mobile breakpoint. - The local Vitest runner is blocked before collection by the shared worktree `fake-indexeddb` path; CI will run the frontend suite in its normal environment.

title: feat(voice): ring agents' phones for inbound calls
body: Rings agents' phones for inbound calls so a call reaches the mobile app when it is killed or the screen is locked. The web learns about calls over the socket; a locked phone has no socket, and a VoIP push is the only way iOS lets an app wake into CallKit. Linear: [CW-8226](https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-8226/voice-call-support-in-app) - iPhones register their PushKit token as an `apns_voip` notification subscription, keyed on the same device id as the FCM row. - When an inbound call starts ringing, `Voice::VoipPushJob` sends an APNs VoIP push to each iPhone and a high-priority FCM data message to each Android phone. Dead tokens (APNs 410, FCM `UNREGISTERED`) are deleted. A platform whose client cannot be set up, such as when Google's token request fails, is skipped without stopping the other. - The push carries the caller, the inbox name, and the conversation's display id and account id, which the app uses to open and join the right conversation before its socket is up. - When the call stops ringing, rung Android devices get a `voice_call.cancel` message. iOS gets no cancel; the woken app reads the outcome from the socket. Behind the `mobile_voice_push` account feature. Needs `APNS_VOIP_KEY`, `APNS_VOIP_KEY_ID`, `APNS_VOIP_TEAM_ID`, `APNS_VOIP_BUNDLE_ID`, `APNS_VOIP_ENVIRONMENT` in installation config; FCM reuses the existing Firebase credentials. The agents rung are the conversation's assignee when there is one, otherwise everyone who could be assigned the inbox, in both cases only agents whose status is online, as on the web. They are recorded on the call as the ring starts, so a later cancel or missed-call notice goes to the same agents. The WhatsApp call payload also carries `answer_digest`, a SHA-256 of the SDP answer the server accepted, so a device whose accept response was lost can tell whether its own answer was taken without the answer itself being exposed. ## Super Admin Super Admin user diagnostics show the `apns_voip` rows on the Push tab (a test push skips them, since a VoIP push would ring a call), and the Mobile tab gains an Incoming calls section: whether the installation can push to iPhones and Android phones, how many of the user's devices are registered for calls, and per account the two features, the voice inboxes the agent is rung for, their status, and whether a call rings their phone. An `APNS_VOIP_ENVIRONMENT` the push would reject shows as not configured. ## Verify ``` bundle exec rspec spec/enterprise/jobs/voice/voip_push_job_spec.rb \ spec/enterprise/services/voice/voip_push_service_spec.rb \ spec/builders/notification_subscription_builder_spec.rb \ spec/services/notification/fcm_service_spec.rb \ spec/enterprise/controllers/api/v1/accounts/whatsapp_calls_controller_spec.rb \ spec/enterprise/services/voice/ring_readiness_spec.rb \ spec/controllers/super_admin/user_diagnostics_controller_spec.rb ```

title: feat(voice): ring timeout, ringing-calls query and missed-call notification
body: Makes a ring finish cleanly whether or not anyone answers. Stacked on #16007. Linear: [CW-8226](https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-8226/voice-call-support-in-app) - **Ring timeout.** `Voice::RingingTimeoutJob` runs every 30 s on Enterprise and moves inbound WhatsApp calls that have rung for over 60 s with no agent claiming them to `no_answer`; Meta's own ring ends at about the same time. Twilio callers are left waiting on hold music until they hang up or an agent joins, as on the web. Only calls that rang phones are swept. Without it a WhatsApp call whose end-of-ring never arrives stays ringing forever. - **Ringing calls query.** `GET …/calls?status=ringing` returns the unanswered inbound calls that rang the agent, as recorded when the ring started, while the agent is online. A phone whose socket dropped while locked asks for these when it comes back. - **Missed-call notification.** New `voice_call_missed` type, created for the agents a call rang when it ends with nobody answering: timed out, or the caller hung up, whatever status the provider reported. - **New-message notification for call messages.** Held back only for agents whose phone a ring push actually reached and who get missed calls by push or email; anyone else, a failed or rejected push included, still gets it. Existing users have the new push flag off until they enable it. ## Super Admin User diagnostics label the missed-call type on the Push tab and list it only for accounts with both call features, marking it unavailable elsewhere. ## Verify ``` bundle exec rspec spec/enterprise/services/voice/ringing_timeout_service_spec.rb \ spec/enterprise/finders/call_finder_spec.rb \ spec/enterprise/jobs/voice/missed_call_notification_job_spec.rb \ spec/services/messages/new_message_notification_service_spec.rb \ spec/enterprise/services/enterprise/messages/new_message_notification_service_spec.rb \ spec/enterprise/services/voice/voip_push_service_spec.rb \ spec/enterprise/models/call_spec.rb \ spec/controllers/super_admin/user_diagnostics_controller_spec.rb ```

title: feat(voice): end the Twilio conference when the last agent leaves; keep the provider status
body:
Twilio fixes for calls carried by a phone, whose legs come and go in ways a browser's do not. Stacked on #16008.

Linear: [CW-8226](https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-8226/voice-call-support-in-app)

- **End the conference when the last agent leaves.** A phone can drop its leg without ever sending `DELETE conference` (app killed, network gone, OS ended the call), leaving the contact in a silent conference until Twilio's own timeout. When Twilio reports the last agent participant leaving, the conference is ended and the call marked completed.
  The leave is decided under the call's row lock. A leave from the agent who claimed the call before their join callback arrived ends the live call; a leg Twilio could not add releases its claim, and any conversation assignment that claim made (to an agent who claimed the call since, if one did), so an inbound call rings on for the other agents, while an outbound call is marked unanswered with its conference ended, or failed when the contact had already answered.
  Each agent connection is recorded in `call.meta['agent_legs']` as joining when Twilio asks for its TwiML, then joined or gone. A failure or leave is left alone while another of the agent's connections is on the call or still joining (for 30 s), so a reconnect is not cut off by a late callback for the connection it replaced, whatever order the callbacks arrive in. An accepted `POST /conference` holds a place for the agent's connection until Twilio asks for its TwiML. Whether any connection is still joining is checked under the row lock that recording a connection takes, and the call is completed before its conference is ended, so a connection that opens afterwards is hung up; `Voice::EndConferenceJob` makes the same check, and a failure set aside for a joining connection is decided again by `Voice::FailedAddRecheckJob` once that connection's time is up. A contact leaving a call their own status callback already ended still ends the conference. When Twilio cannot be reached, `Voice::EndConferenceJob` retries, rechecks for a remaining agent before every attempt, and tries again in later rounds.
- **Keep Twilio's status beside ours.** `queued`, `initiated` and `ringing` all map to our `ringing`, so an outbound call screen could not tell when the far handset actually rang. The provider status is now kept in `call.meta['provider_status']` and the call message is rebroadcast when it changes. An outbound call is dialled before its row commits, so `Voice::SyncProviderStatusJob` applies Twilio's current status and times once it does, and a late `ringing` never moves an answered call back.

```
bundle exec rspec spec/enterprise/services/voice/conference/manager_spec.rb \
  spec/enterprise/services/voice/provider/twilio/conference_service_spec.rb \
  spec/enterprise/services/voice/status_update_service_spec.rb \
  spec/enterprise/services/voice/call_status/manager_spec.rb \
  spec/enterprise/jobs/voice/end_conference_job_spec.rb \
  spec/enterprise/jobs/voice/sync_provider_status_job_spec.rb \
  spec/enterprise/controllers/twilio/voice_controller_spec.rb \
  spec/enterprise/models/call_spec.rb \
  spec/enterprise/jobs/voice/failed_add_recheck_job_spec.rb
```

title: feat: add email verification by one-time code for Captain [PR-1]
body:
Adds the building blocks for verifying a customer's email in a Captain conversation. Captain emails a 6-digit code, and the customer types it back.

This is part 1 of 3. **Nothing in this PR is reachable yet.** No agent has the tools, and nothing calls the service. Part 3 turns it on.

## What is added

- **`Captain::EmailVerification`:** sends a code, checks a code, and reports the verified email. State is in Redis.
- **`Captain::EmailVerificationMailer`:** the code email, sent with the inbox name as the sender name.
- **Two Captain tools:** `SendEmailVerificationCodeTool` and `VerifyEmailCodeTool`. The code is compared in the tool, so the model cannot mark an email as verified.

## Rules

- A verification lasts 24 hours, and is tied to the contact inbox and the exact email address.
- Codes are 6 digits, expire in 30 minutes, allow 5 attempts, and are stored hashed.
- Sends are limited to 5 per hour, per contact inbox and per email address.
- An address that is already verified gets no further codes.
- The plain code never appears in the mail job's arguments or in the subject.

## Series

1. **This PR:** email verification building blocks.
2. #16229: tool settings and the `session.verified_email` template value.
3. #16230: activation, with the gate, the agent wiring, the prompt, and the dashboard toggle.

Replaces #16202.

title: fix(captain): stop sending tool call text as replies
body:
Captain sometimes sent customers raw text like `{"commentary":null}` or `{"query":"..."}` instead of a reply. On the Responses API, gpt-5.2 occasionally writes the tool call it meant to make as reply text instead of calling the tool. Captain now catches these replies before they're sent, retries once when it's safe to, and hands the conversation to a human if the reply is still bad. No credit is charged for a handoff.

## Closes

- https://app.chatwoot.com/app/accounts/1/conversations/98035

## How to reproduce

Hard to trigger on demand. Replaying the affected production prompt on gpt-5.2 over Responses leaked in 5 of 16 runs and in 0 of 24 runs over Chat Completions. The leaked text arrives as ordinary reply text, with no `phase` field and no native function call. In production it appears either as the whole reply or as a first part followed by the real answer.

## What changed

- `ResponseParts#leaked_tool_call?` flags a reply when any part is a JSON object or contains `to=functions.`. JSON inside a sentence or a fenced code block is not flagged. Over 1,537 production replies, it flagged 0 normal replies and caught both leaks in the sample.
- `AgentRunnerService#generate_response` retries once when the reply leaks, unless a tool already ran (a retry would repeat it, e.g. a custom HTTP POST) or a newer customer message discarded the turn. If the reply still leaks, it raises `LeakedToolCallError`, which goes through the existing error response: customer conversations get the normal failure handoff with no credit charged, and Copilot reply suggestions raise their existing `GenerationError`.
- A rejected reply is never saved, so it can't end up in the conversation history used for the next turn.
- Langfuse traces for rejected runs record `credit_used: false`, using the same check.

## Known tradeoffs

- A reply part made only of a bare JSON object, with no code fence, is treated as a leak and leads to a retry or handoff.
- Copilot's job already retries `GenerationError` up to 3 times, so a model that keeps leaking can use up to 6 runs for one suggestion.
- No retry after any tool runs, including read-only ones like `faq_lookup`. The turn hands off to a human instead.

title: feat: add settings and a session email value to Captain custom tools [PR-2]
body:
Adds the data model that lets a custom tool require a verified customer. Stacked on #16228.

This is part 2 of 3. **Existing tools run as before.** The setting is stored and nothing enforces it. Part 3 turns it on. One API change is listed below.

## What is added

- **`settings` on custom tools:** a `jsonb` column with one option, `requires_email_verification`. Only known keys with `true` or `false` values are accepted.
- **API:** `settings` is accepted, merged on update, and returned. An unknown key or a value that is not `true` or `false` returns 422, so a malformed setting cannot look saved.
- **Parameter validation:** a parameter in a create or update request may only have `name`, `type`, `description`, `required` and `source`, each with a plain value. Anything else returns 422.
- **Manifests:** a flat `requires_email_verification` key per tool, default `false`, stored in `settings`.
- **Verified parameters:** a parameter can declare a `source`. Chatwoot fills it from what the customer verified, and the model does not see it in customer conversations.

```yaml
param_schema:
  - name: email
    type: string
    description: Customer email
    source: verified.email        # one-time code
```

## Rules

- `source` accepts only `verified.email` for now, and the parameter must be a string.
- A tool with a `verified.email` parameter counts as requiring email verification, with no setting needed.
- In part 3, Chatwoot sets the verified email after the model's parameters, so the model cannot replace it.
- Where an admin or an agent is the user, a `source` parameter is shown to the model as a required parameter. Nothing builds tools that way yet.

## Behaviour changes

- **Stricter parameters in the API.** Before, `permit` dropped an unknown field or a nested value in a parameter, and the save succeeded. Now the request returns 422 with "Param schema must list parameters with known fields and plain values". The dashboard form sends only the known fields, so it is not affected. An API client that sends extra fields, such as `enum` or `example`, would start getting 422. A dropped field could have turned a verified parameter into one the model fills, which is why the request now fails instead.
- **Accepted before enforced.** The API accepts `requires_email_verification` and `source` before anything enforces them. A `source` parameter renders empty until part 3. Parts 2 and 3 should ship in the same release.

## Migration

Adds `settings` (`jsonb`, default `{}`, not null) to `captain_custom_tools`.

## Series

1. #16228: email verification building blocks. Merged.
2. **This PR:** tool settings and verified parameters.
3. #16230: activation, with the gate, the agent wiring, the prompt, and the dashboard options.

title: fix: normalize .oga filenames for audio transcription
body:
Telegram audio attachments with `.oga` filenames fail transcription because OpenAI rejects the upload with `Unsupported file format oga`. Normalize the temporary transcription filename to `.ogg` in the shared speech service. The stored filename and audio bytes stay unchanged.

Replayed an affected original Ogg/Opus recording against `gpt-4o-mini-transcribe`: `.oga` returned HTTP 400, while the identical bytes uploaded as `.ogg` returned a transcript. The regression spec checks the upload extension, byte preservation, and stored filename. All 21 focused speech/message/job examples passed, and RuboCop reported no offenses. The existing call-recording cases passed after running the search-specific case with OpenSearch configured.

title: fix(voice): restrict authenticated twilio recording downloads
body:
Prevents Twilio recording downloads from sending inbox credentials to an untrusted server. This is a scoped security stopgap that can be deployed without waiting for customers to update their Account Auth Tokens.

Recording URLs must use HTTPS on a trusted Twilio API hostname and match the inbox's account and recording. Existing SafeFetch behavior already strips authentication on cross-origin redirects, so this PR does not change the shared downloader.

Related: https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-8443

### Things to know

- This addresses the reported recording credential-theft path. It does not authenticate voice callbacks; forged call events remain possible until signature verification is deployed through [#16247](https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/pull/16247).
- It can be deployed independently of the token-update flow in [#16244](https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/pull/16244). No customer credential update is required for this PR.
- The URL check supports the default and regional/edge Twilio API hosts, with the default, WAV, or MP3 recording path. Userinfo, query strings, fragments, nonstandard ports, and non-HTTPS URLs are rejected before downloading.
- Fifty-eight existing recording, SafeFetch, and Twilio media-download tests passed, and changed files passed lint. Live recording playback should be confirmed after deployment.

### How to test

1. Complete a recorded Twilio call and confirm the recording appears and plays in Chatwoot.
2. Confirm a recording URL pointing to another host, account, or recording is rejected before an authenticated request is sent.
3. Confirm redirects to a different origin do not receive the original download credentials.

title: feat(voice): ring agents' phones by default on Voice Channel accounts
body:
Ringing agents' phones only does anything with Voice Channel on, so a separate Super Admin switch for it was one more thing to find. It is now on for every account by default and kept out of the feature grid, so turning on Voice Channel is the only step.

- `mobile_voice_push` ("Calls on mobile") is enabled by default and marked `hidden: true` in `config/features.yml`.
- Super Admin leaves hidden features out of the account feature lists, and saving the account form keeps their current state instead of clearing them.
- Migration runs outside a transaction: it saves the enabled `ACCOUNT_LEVEL_FEATURE_DEFAULTS` entry first (adding it, or the row, when missing), so accounts created during the deploy start with the flag, then sets the bit on every account that lacks it in batches of 1,000 that each commit.
- On deploy, every Voice Channel account takes part in the ring flow for new inbound calls: phones are pushed where APNs/Firebase are configured, unanswered WhatsApp calls are ended as no-answer after about 60 s, rung agents get missed-call notifications per their preferences, and ringing calls are returned to the app for recovery. Accounts without Voice Channel see no change.
- It can still be turned off for an account from the console (`account.disable_features!('mobile_voice_push')`) or the Platform API; that applies to calls arriving afterwards. User Diagnostics shows its state.

```
bundle exec rspec spec/controllers/super_admin/accounts_controller_spec.rb spec/enterprise/controllers/super_admin/user_diagnostics_controller_spec.rb spec/models/account_spec.rb spec/lib/config_loader_spec.rb
```

title: fix(super-admin): show why a call does not ring an agent's phone in user diagnostics
body:
User Diagnostics showed "Only with the app open" for every account whose calls don't ring the agent's phone, including accounts that take no calls at all and agents who have never signed in to the app.

- `Voice::RingReadiness#blocker` returns the first reason a call doesn't ring: Voice Channel off, Calls on mobile off, no voice inboxes, not online, no phone registered, or push not configured
- The Phone rings cell shows that reason; "Only with the app open" stays only for a registered phone the installation can't push to

| Reason | Phone rings |
|---|---|
| Voice Channel off | No, Voice Channel is off |
| Calls on mobile off | No, Calls on mobile is off |
| No voice inbox rings the user | No, no voice inboxes |
| User not online | No, not online |
| No phone registered for calls | No, no phone registered |
| Phone registered, push not configured | Only with the app open |

```
bundle exec rspec spec/enterprise/services/voice/ring_readiness_spec.rb spec/enterprise/controllers/super_admin/user_diagnostics_controller_spec.rb
```

title: feat: notify administrators when Captain credits run low
body:
Chatwoot Cloud now emails account administrators when Captain response credit use exceeds 80% of the current total. The alert uses the same total shown in Billing, including purchased credits and account quota overrides, and sends once per billing period.

## What changed

The shared response counter now queues an alert check after persisted usage crosses the fixed threshold. The job rechecks Cloud and Captain eligibility under an account lock, records a persistent alert marker, and sends the administrator email with consumed and remaining credits.

Billing renewal clears the usage count and alert marker together. Top ups and plan changes keep the marker, so they do not send another alert in the same period.

## How to test

1. Use a Chatwoot Cloud account with Captain enabled and a response limit of 300.
2. Confirm that consuming credit 240 does not send an email.
3. Consume credit 241 and confirm every account administrator receives one email with 241 consumed, 59 remaining, and a working Billing link.
4. Run the alert job again and confirm no second email is sent.
5. Add top up credits and confirm the alert does not rearm.
6. Reset usage for a billing renewal and confirm a later threshold crossing can send one new alert.

title: fix(stripe): disconnect accounts when the app is uninstalled
body:
This draft makes Chatwoot disconnect a Stripe integration when an administrator uninstalls the app from Stripe. Today the saved connection remains active until someone disconnects it in Chatwoot, leaving the integration marked Connected after uninstall.

Signed `account.application.deauthorized` events remove the matching integration and its saved access and refresh tokens. Returning to the Stripe settings tab refreshes the connection status. Outstanding refreshes are invalidated when connecting or disconnecting, so outdated responses and errors cannot overwrite the newer state.

Related: https://app.chatwoot.com/app/accounts/1/conversations/101148

### Things to know

- After deployment, register `https://<chatwoot-host>/webhooks/stripe_app` on the Stripe app publisher account, listening to events on Connected accounts and subscribing to `account.application.deauthorized`.
- Save that endpoint's signing secret in Super Admin → Stripe → Stripe App Webhook Signing Secret. This is separate from Chatwoot subscription-billing webhooks.
- Cleanup is scoped to the Stripe account and live/sandbox environment, including every matching Chatwoot account. Duplicate events are harmless, and events at or before the saved connection timestamp are ignored. Equal-second timestamps are ambiguous: this preserves a possible reconnection but also skips a genuine uninstall within the installation second.
- Local verification: signed webhook requests passed for valid/invalid signatures, duplicate delivery, credential cleanup, environment/account isolation, and delayed-event protection. All 11 existing Stripe UI tests passed with a focused setup excluding an unrelated missing IndexedDB dependency. The Ruby regression run had 52 passing examples, one asset-manifest rendering failure in the Super Admin page, and one encryption check pending because local encryption keys were unset.
- Follow-up race coverage passes: 3 backend examples and all 14 Stripe component tests, including delayed list/detail responses and stale errors after disconnect. Ruby and JavaScript lint checks pass. Frontend tests use the focused setup excluding the unrelated missing IndexedDB dependency.
- No Marketplace version update is required. Production webhook registration and reviewer validation remain pending.

### How to test

1. Configure the webhook signing secret and connect a Stripe account in Chatwoot.
2. Uninstall Chatwoot from that account's Stripe Dashboard.
3. Verify Stripe reports a successful webhook delivery. Return to Chatwoot's Stripe settings and confirm it offers Connect; the saved integration credentials should be gone.
4. Redeliver the same event and verify it succeeds without affecting another account or environment.
5. Reconnect, then deliver an uninstall event with an older or equal timestamp and verify the new connection remains active.
6. Delay a focus-refresh response, disconnect, and then release the delayed response. Confirm the page still offers Connect and does not restore the Connected card.

title: chore: add testing tools to the widget test page
body:
Adds a tools column to the widget test page at `/widget_tests`, so common widget checks no longer need URL edits or the browser console. The page is not routed in production. ## Tools - **Verify contact with HMAC:** Enter an identifier, email, and name, and the page calls `setUser` with a hash signed by the inbox's HMAC token. A Randomize button fills the fields with a random contact. - **Invalid hash test:** Switch to "Invalid hash" to send a hash signed with a wrong key on a fresh session. The status line reports whether the server rejected it. - **Reset session:** Runs `$chatwoot.reset()` and reloads as an anonymous visitor. - **Event log:** Lists widget events on the page, newest first, and fills the remaining height of the column. The widget also opens on load. The column sits on the side opposite the bubble, and each tool is one `
`, so more can be added. Tested locally in the browser on a web widget inbox, including the invalid hash rejection shown in the screenshot.

title: fix(voice): collect account auth tokens before security rollout
body:
Lets existing Twilio inboxes collect the Account Auth Token separately from their API key credentials before webhook signature verification is deployed.

API-key inboxes without a recorded account token can save it from Voice settings. SMS-to-voice upgrades collect the missing credentials, and the saved token state survives turning voice off and on again.

Related: https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-8443
Rollout: https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-8452/update-remaining-twilio-voice-account-tokens-before-signature

### Things to know

- Deploy this token-update flow first, then ask affected customers to update their credentials and re-run validation.

Signature verification remains in [#16247](https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/pull/16247) and deploys after credential updates are complete.

- Twenty-five existing inbox and voice-model tests passed. The credential-upgrade checks also passed.

### How to test

1. Open an existing API-key voice inbox without a recorded Account Auth Token. Confirm Voice settings shows the token field and Update button, and save the correct token.
2. Upgrade an API-key SMS inbox to voice. Confirm it collects the Account Auth Token separately and preserves API credentials.
3. Turn voice off and on again. Confirm the saved account token is reused without another prompt, and calls still work.

title: fix(campaigns): show campaigns sent before the first reply
body:
WhatsApp campaigns sent before a customer's first reply were missing from the conversation timeline. The first conversation now includes saved campaigns sent before it was created, so agents can see the offer the customer received.

Later conversations keep their existing history boundaries, so earlier campaigns do not appear again in each new conversation. Unsent campaign records remain excluded.

### Related

Related: https://app.chatwoot.com/app/accounts/1/conversations/101569

### Things to know

This displays existing saved campaign-recipient records; it does not reconstruct missing historical records or attribute replies to campaigns.

### How to test

1. Send a WhatsApp campaign to a contact with no conversation, then have the contact reply. Open their first conversation and confirm the campaign appears before the reply.
2. Send another campaign during that conversation and confirm both campaign messages appear in chronological order.
3. Create a later conversation for the same contact and inbox, then send another campaign. Confirm the later conversation shows its own campaign without repeating the first conversation's campaigns.

Verified locally with two conversations and three saved campaigns in the browser and API. All 27 campaign-history request examples pass, and the controller passes Ruby lint.

title: fix: skip IMAP emails that another fetch job already saved
body:
IMAP inboxes no longer save the same email more than once when two fetch jobs for that inbox run at the same time. Before this change, each copy of a new email thread became its own conversation. In one customer inbox, 12 emails were saved up to 7 times each within 20 minutes.

## Closes

[CW-8275](https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-8275/email-duplication-issue)

## How to reproduce

1. Connect an email inbox to an IMAP server that is slow to respond, so that one fetch runs longer than 5 minutes.
2. Send a new email to that inbox while the fetch is running.
3. The inbox lock expires after 5 minutes, and the scheduler starts another fetch every minute. Each new fetch downloads the same unsaved email.
4. Before this change, every one of those fetches saved the email, and each copy opened a new conversation. After this change, only one conversation is created.

## Why duplicates happened

- `Inboxes::FetchImapEmailsJob` takes a Redis lock per inbox with a 5-minute TTL. A fetch against a slow mail server can run longer than that. On Sep 21, one fetch ran for 43 minutes.
- When the lock expires, the next job starts while the first is still running. The unlock is also not owner-checked, so a finishing job can delete the next job's lock.
- Each job checks for duplicates when it downloads the headers. It saves the emails only after it has downloaded every body, which can be minutes later.
- At the save, `create_message` only looks for the Message-ID inside the matched conversation. A new thread has no conversation yet, so every copy passes.

That leaves two windows where a second job can save the same email:

1. **Between the header check and the save.** Another job may save the email during the minutes in between.
2. **During the save.** The save runs in one transaction. A second job cannot see the first job's row until it commits.

## What changed

`Imap::ImapMailbox#process` now runs a duplicate check as the first step inside its transaction:

1. It takes a Postgres advisory lock with `pg_advisory_xact_lock`, keyed on the inbox ID and a hash of the Message-ID. If another job holds the lock, that job is saving the same email right now, and this job waits until it commits.
2. It then checks `@inbox.messages.exists?(source_id:)` inside `Message.uncached`. If another job has already saved the email, this job skips it.

The job waits instead of skipping so that a reply later in its batch can find the first email's conversation. The check bypasses the query cache because the fetch-stage check runs the same query, and Rails can return that cached result. The lock call uses `select_value`, because `execute` clears the query cache and would hide a missing `uncached`.

The lock closes the second window. The check closes the first. Postgres releases the lock when the transaction commits, rolls back, or loses its connection.

`spec/fixtures/files/malformed_reply_to.eml` gets a `Message-ID` header. The fetch service drops any email without a Message-ID before it reaches the mailbox, so the mailbox now assumes one is present. That fixture was the only mailbox spec input without one.

## Options we considered

- **Advisory lock plus `exists?` at the save (this PR).** Closes both windows in about 10 lines. Needs no Redis key, TTL, or migration.
- **Time out stalled body fetches (the earlier version of this PR).** Reverted. It shortens one cause of long fetch jobs, but two jobs can still save the same email. It can come back as its own PR for the delay a stalled email causes.
- **`exists?` at the save with no lock.** Closes the first window only. Jobs stalled on the same mail server may be released together and save at the same moment.
- **Redis lock per email.** Same coverage, but the lock has a TTL. Attachments upload inside the transaction, so a slow save may outlive it.
- **Unique index on `(inbox_id, source_id)`.** `messages` is a very large table, other channels also write `source_id`, and existing duplicate rows would block the index build.
- **Stop fetch jobs from overlapping.** An owner-checked unlock or a Postgres session lock per inbox would address the overlap itself. Both are larger changes and are left as follow-ups.

We ran four threads, each on its own DB connection, saving the same email at the same moment. With the check, every round produced 1 conversation. Without it, a round produced 4. The specs cannot cover this case because they share one DB connection.

## Trade-offs

- Fetch jobs still overlap. The extra jobs still download the same headers and bodies, and that work is wasted.
- The header scan is still slow. Every fetch downloads all headers since yesterday and runs one query per header.
- A stalled body fetch still delays new emails for that inbox.
- If a job finds the lock taken, it waits for the other job's transaction. If that job fails, the waiting job saves the email.
- `statement_timeout` is 14 seconds. If the other job's save takes longer, the waiting job raises and logs the error. The email is saved by the other job or by the next sync. A reply in the waiting job's batch can still start a second conversation in that case.
- The check relies on the READ COMMITTED isolation level, which is the Postgres default. The repo does not override it. The production setting has not been verified.
- Two different emails in one inbox may hash to the same lock key. If both are saved at the same moment, one job waits for the other.
- The lock uses the two-integer advisory key form. Postgres keeps it separate from the single-bigint keys that the importer and `ConversationMonitors::RetryJob` use.
- Emails that arrive through forwarding do not go through this mailbox. An email that arrives through both forwarding and IMAP can still be saved twice.

title: fix(conversations): render a conversation with a deleted assignee as unassigned
body:
## Description

The conversation list no longer returns 500 when one conversation is assigned to a user that no longer exists. That conversation renders as unassigned and the rest of the page loads, which is what happened before v4.18.0.

`Conversation#assignee_type` answers `'User'` whenever `assignee_id` is set, and `assignee_id` has no foreign key, so an id left behind by a removed user resolves to `nil`. title: feat: verify customer email before Captain uses sensitive tools [PR-3]
body:
Turns on email verification for Captain custom tools. A tool can now require a verified email before it runs, and a parameter can take the verified email from Chatwoot, so the model never chooses it. Builds on #16228 and #16229, both merged.

Before this, a visitor could type any email into the chat or the pre-chat form, and Captain would use it to look up that person's account with custom tools.

This is part 3 of 3. **Every behaviour change in the series is in this PR.**

## 1. Two kinds of custom tool

`HttpTool` is split by who the user is. The runner picks the class once per run.

- **`PublicHttpTool`:** a customer is the user. This is the default, so any code that builds a tool without choosing gets the gate.
- **`CopilotHttpTool`:** an admin or an agent is the user. This covers the playground and reply suggestions.
- `HttpTool` keeps only the shared request code.
- The unused V1 wrapper `CustomHttpTool` is removed.

## 2. The gate, for customers

- A tool is gated if `requires_email_verification` is on, or a parameter has `source: verified.email`.
- A gated tool makes no request until the customer has verified an email with a one-time code. Captain gets a message telling it to verify first.
- HMAC does not count. It verifies an identifier, not the email.
- The verified email is read from stored data on every call, never from the run state.
- A verification lasts for the conversation it happened in, for up to 1 hour. In email conversations it lasts up to 3 hours, because replies arrive slowly. A new conversation from the same contact starts unverified. The limit on sending codes stays per contact, so opening new conversations does not give more codes.
- A parameter with a `source` is hidden from the model. Chatwoot fills it in, and a value the model sends under that name is replaced.
- The setting on its own only requires a verified customer. It does not bind which email the request uses. A tool that takes the email as a plain parameter still sends whatever email Captain passes. To bind the email, add a verified email parameter.

## 3. Playground and reply suggestions

- Verified parameters are shown to the model, which fills them. The tool sends the value it was given, because a team member is the user.
- When that value is not the email the customer verified, the result says so.

## 4. Request headers

- Every custom tool request carries `X-Chatwoot-Verified-Email` when the customer has verified an email by one-time code. It is left out otherwise.
- `X-Chatwoot-Contact-Email` is unchanged. It holds the contact record's email, which is not verified.

## 5. Agents

- Every Captain agent in a customer conversation gets the two verification tools, on every channel including email. This happens only when an enabled custom tool requires a verified email.
- The assistant and scenario agents get a "Customer Identity" section under the same condition, on every channel. The section also shows when the customer has already verified, even if the tool was turned off later. It states whether the customer verified an email by one-time code, what that proves, and how to verify. It does not mention HMAC.
- Reply suggestions and Copilot chat do not get that section.

## 6. Dashboard

- An "Add verified email" button next to "Add parameter". It adds a parameter that Chatwoot fills from the verified email, shown as a compact row. A tool can have one.
- A "Require email verification" switch. It shows on and locked when a parameter takes the verified email.
- Tools that cannot be edited open as a details view instead of a disabled form. This covers installed tools, and any tool an agent opens. The view shows the description, email verification, authentication type and parameters. The endpoint, headers and templates are in a collapsed "Request and response" section. Installed tools show a note that they are read-only.
- On an installed tool, admins can change the email verification switch in that view. It saves as soon as it changes. Agents see it read-only.
- A warning before saving. The form scores a tool for signs that it handles customer data: a write method, credentials, a parameter that looks like an email or an ID, money or personal data words, and known private API hosts such as Stripe and Attio. If the tool is not gated and the score is high enough, saving asks "Save without email verification?" with **Go back** and **Save anyway**. It never blocks the save.
- A hint on email parameters. A parameter Captain fills that looks like an email shows "This email is not verified. A customer could type someone else's.", with a **Use verified email** link that turns it into the verified email parameter.

## Behaviour by channel

| Where Captain runs | Who is the user | Verification tools | Gated tools | Verified email parameter | How long a verification lasts |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Web widget | Customer | Yes, when a tool needs it | Refuse until verified | Filled by Chatwoot, hidden from Captain | This conversation, up to 1 hour |
| API inbox | Customer | Yes, when a tool needs it | Refuse until verified | Filled by Chatwoot, hidden from Captain | This conversation, up to 1 hour |
| WhatsApp, SMS, Facebook, Instagram, Telegram, Line | Customer | Yes, when a tool needs it | Refuse until verified | Filled by Chatwoot, hidden from Captain | This conversation, up to 1 hour |
| Email | Customer | Yes, when a tool needs it. The code goes out as a separate email | Refuse until verified | Filled by Chatwoot, hidden from Captain | This conversation (email thread), up to 3 hours |
| Playground and `rake captain:chat` | Admin | No | Run | Filled by Captain, result says "not verified" | Not applicable |
| Reply suggestions | Agent | No | Run. Only GET tools, which is an existing rule so a draft cannot change data | Filled by Captain, result says "not verified" unless it matches the customer's verified email | Uses the conversation's verification, if any |
| Copilot chat | Agent | No | Not available, no custom tools | Not applicable | Not applicable |

- HMAC does not count as verification. It verifies an identifier, not an email.
- Sending codes is limited to 5 an hour per contact and 5 an hour per email address. A new conversation does not reset that.
- On email, Captain replies only to the contact, and that contact is the address replies go to.

## Things to know

- **No feature flag.** An assistant gets the two verification tools and the identity section in customer conversations once any of its enabled custom tools requires a verified email. Assistants without such a tool see no change.
- **Tools are open unless marked.** Existing tools and installed toolsets are not gated until the setting is on or a parameter has a `source`. The manifests in `chatwoot/tools` and the manifest validator need updating separately.
- **Installed tools keep their setting.** A tool takes `requires_email_verification` from the manifest when it is first installed. After that the setting belongs to the admin, like the enabled flag, and toolset updates do not change it. A toolset update that turns the setting on reaches only new installs. A verified email parameter still gates the tool, because updates do change parameters.
- **Older versions reject `source`.** A manifest that uses it cannot be installed on a version before this series.
- **IDs are not bound.** A verified customer can pass any ID they know to a gated tool that takes an ID from the model, such as a customer ID or an order number. The gate checks who the customer is, not which records they ask for. Binding IDs to what an earlier verified tool returned is a follow-up.
- **Email conversations.** The code is sent as a separate email, not as a reply in the thread. Captain replies only to the contact, and on email inboxes the contact is the address replies go to, so a sender who only claims an address cannot receive another person's data.

## Testing

Specs cover both tool classes, the runner's choice of class, verified parameters, the verified email header, and the agent wiring.

The one-time code flow was tested locally with ad-hoc chats on a web widget inbox, using Stripe and Attio toolsets. Covered: sending a code, wrong codes, resending, and a successful verification.

The gate with verified parameters has not been run in a live chat yet. The "Add verified email" button and its row have not been clicked through in a browser.

## Series

1. #16228: email verification building blocks. Merged.
2. #16229: tool settings and verified parameters. Merged.
3. **This PR:** activation.

title: feat: auto translate conversations with Captain [3]
body:
# Pull Request Template

## Description

This PR adds the backend for auto translation with Captain. It builds on #16279, which has the feature flag and the account setting. The dashboard that shows the translations is in #16276, on top of this one.

**Incoming messages**
- A new `auto_translate` endpoint translates up to 20 messages of a conversation into the agent's language in one Captain call and stores the result on each message. Contact messages and bot replies are covered. Private notes, messages without text and emails with an HTML body are not.
- The language of every incoming message is detected with Captain and stored on the message. The conversation follows the contact's latest language, so a contact who switches languages gets replies in the new one.
- Messages already in the agent's language are stored as such and are never sent to the model again.

**Replies**
- Agent replies are sent in the contact's language, and the agent's own text is kept so the dashboard can show it. The language the agent wrote in is detected from the text, so a reply already in the contact's language goes out as typed.
- Private notes, WhatsApp and content templates, interactive messages, bot replies and forwarded emails are not translated. If the translation fails, the reply is still sent as written and flagged for the agent.

**Templates**
- Greeting, out-of-office, email collect and CSAT messages are sent in the contact's language once it is known. The original text is kept for agents.

Language detection runs on a small model and does not count towards Captain response usage; translations do.

Fixes https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/AI-5/chore-auto-translate-incoming-and-outgoing-messages-using-ai

## Type of change

title: feat: show auto translations in the dashboard and widget [3]
body:
# Pull Request Template

## Description

This PR adds the dashboard and widget side of auto translation with Captain. Agents read every conversation in their own dashboard language and reply in it; contacts read the replies in theirs. It builds on #16279 (feature flag and account setting) and #16292 (the translation backend). Auto translate stays off until an account switches it on in Settings.

**Dashboard**
- Contact messages and bot replies are shown in the agent's dashboard language, with `View original (language)` to read what was written. Agent replies show `View translated (language)` to see what the contact received.
- When a conversation is opened, older messages load or a new message arrives, the dashboard asks for every message that has no translation in the agent's language yet. Each message is translated in the background and the translation arrives through the message updated event. Until then the message shows `Translating…` with a subtle shimmer, and the space is reserved so the layout does not shift.
- The server picks the target language from the agent's dashboard language, so the dashboard no longer sends it.
- Messages already in the agent's language show `Already in (language)`, once per group of messages. A reply that could not be translated shows `Could not translate, sent as typed`; a contact message that could not be translated shows `Could not translate`.
- Only text messages and plain-text emails are translated. Call bubbles, cards, forms, emails with an HTML body and forwarded emails are left as they are.
- Captain replies get the same treatment, with the toggle in the `Generated by Captain` row.
- The manual Translate action is hidden for auto translated messages. Copy and Add to canned response use the text that is currently shown.

**Widget**
- An agent reply shows `Translating…` while it is translated, then arrives in the contact's language.
- `View original` is offered only on replies that auto translate translated before sending, so the contact can read the agent's own text. Bot replies and translations agents made for themselves are never shown to the contact.

**Email**
- Only the agent's new text above the quoted thread is translated. The quoted thread is kept as it was, and the email the contact receives is built from the translated text.
- Translated email replies are sent once and show up in the dashboard immediately. Previously the rendered email html could not be broadcast, so the reply only went out on retry.

When auto translate is off nothing changes: no translation requests are made and the existing Translate action keeps working.

**Known follow-ups**
- Webhooks receive the agent's untranslated reply on `message_created` before the translated update (AI-230).
- The widget SDK `chatwoot:on-message` event carries the untranslated reply (AI-226).
- Translations can use the informal form of "you" when the contact wrote formally (AI-227).
- HTML emails, quote trimming for contact emails and line breaks in translated emails are handled in #16291 (AI-228).
- The conversation list preview shows the contact's language (AI-229).

Part of https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/AI-5/chore-auto-translate-incoming-and-outgoing-messages-using-ai

Fixes https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/AI-24/feature-machine-translation-of-chat-via-google-translate


## Type of change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

## How Has This Been Tested?

### How to test

1. Enable the Auto Translate feature for the account in Super Admin, configure a Captain API key, and switch Auto Translate on in Settings.
2. Set your profile language to one the contact does not write in.
3. From the live chat widget, write in another language. The message shows `Translating…` and then appears in your language, with `View original` to switch back.
4. Reply from the dashboard. The reply shows `Translating to (language)…`, then the widget receives it in the contact's language, with `View original` showing your text.
5. On an email inbox, reply to a plain-text email with the earlier thread quoted below. The contact receives your reply in their language with the quoted thread unchanged, and the reply shows up in the dashboard straight away.
