title: fix: preserve automation labels on unrelated conversation saves
body:
Prevents labels added by automation from disappearing when message processing later saves unrelated conversation fields. SLA and priority can remain intact while the label disappears without a removal activity entry.

## Why this happens

`acts-as-taggable-on` persists a tag list once it has been read, even if the record is being saved for an unrelated change. A message worker can read an empty label list, automation can add a label through a different instance, and the original worker can then overwrite the label while saving first-reply fields. The label was not explicitly changed on that instance, so the removal can bypass label-change activity logging.

This mechanism also reproduces with the unmodified gem, ActiveRecord, and an in-memory SQLite database, without Chatwoot models or callbacks.

## Solution options

### 1. Persist only lists that changed locally (implemented)

Keep a snapshot of the original in-memory tag list. Allow the gem's tagging and cache callbacks to write only when the current list differs from that snapshot. Refresh the snapshot after saving and clear it on reload.

This protects conversations and contacts from unrelated stale saves while preserving explicit assignments and in-place `label_list.add/remove` edits. The comparison does not require additional database queries or row locks.

The tradeoff is that this is an application-level compatibility patch around gem internals. Ideally, the gem would own mutation tracking and conditional persistence, allowing this concern to be removed after an upstream fix. It does not serialize two workers intentionally editing labels at the same time.

### 2. Lock and reload around the relevant updates (not selected)

Take a conversation row lock, reload its current state, and hold the lock through the reply-state update. Label read-modify-write operations can also use the lock so competing edits take turns. Reloading without a lock leaves a window for another writer between the reload and save.

We do not recommend this approach for this fix:

- It adds database reads and row-lock contention to message processing. Busy conversations can make competing workers wait.
- The local trial needed an explicit reload before `with_lock`, which reloads again under the lock, because newly created conversations carry a trigger-populated `display_id` marked as an unsaved change.
- Protecting only the automation is insufficient. Every relevant stale-save path must acquire the lock and reload before saving.
- It leaves the underlying behavior in place: an unrelated save still attempts to persist labels that were merely read.

These are architectural costs, not measured production latency results. The locking trial is not included in this PR.

## Legacy label-cache backfill job

`Migration::ConversationBatchCacheLabelJob` filled `cached_label_list` by reading `label_list` and calling `save!`. That relied on the gem writing the cache after a read, which this PR stops. The job now builds the cache from the taggings and writes it directly, under a row lock.

This change is largely inert. The job runs only from the December 2023 migration `20231219000743_re_run_cache_label_job`, which first shipped in v3.4.0. Only instances upgrading from before v3.4.0 run it. Every other instance has already run that migration and never reaches this code.

## How to reproduce

1. Create a record with no labels and load it into two instances.
2. Read the empty label list on the first instance.
3. Add a label through the second instance.
4. Save an unrelated field through the first instance.
5. Without the fix, the tagging can disappear; with an initially NULL cache, the cached list also becomes empty. With the fix, both remain intact.

The corresponding product path is a new conversation receiving an outgoing native-channel message while a conversation-created automation adds its label. Explicit label additions and removals should continue working.

No backfill or historical data repair is included.

title: perf: skip loading contact inboxes when dispatching contact merged event
body:
# Pull Request Template

## Description

`ContactMergeAction` dispatches `CONTACT_MERGED` with a `tokens` list built from every contact inbox of the base contact:

```ruby
tokens: [@base_contact.contact_inboxes.filter_map(&:pubsub_token)]
```

No listener reads `tokens`. `ActionCableListener#contact_merged` is the only handler for this event, and it has broadcast to the account token since #11082. This drops the unused argument.

Why it matters for performance: the list is built synchronously inside the merge, so every merge loads all contact inboxes of the base contact and instantiates a record for each one. The same list then goes into the `EventDispatcherJob` payload for the async dispatcher. A web widget contact gains one contact inbox for every new browser session that identifies as that contact, so long-lived contacts can collect a very large number of them. For those contacts every widget `set_user` call that merges into them got slower over time, with the cost growing linearly with the number of contact inboxes.

After this change the merge cost no longer depends on how many contact inboxes the base contact has. The broadcast and its payload are unchanged.

Fixes https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/INF-123

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

Existing specs for the contact merge action and the action cable listener pass.

title: fix: send auto-translated templates in email inboxes
body:
## Description When Auto Translate is on, automatic messages in email inboxes were never sent to the customer. This covers the greeting, out-of-office, CSAT survey and auto-resolve messages. The job that sends them crashed while translating them, and Sidekiq kept retrying it and failing every time. These messages are now translated and sent. The dashboard also shows their original text as plain text, instead of raw HTML like `

Help us improve!

`. Fixes https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-8502/nomethoderror-undefined-method-merge-for-nil-nomethoderror Sentry: https://chatwoot-p3.sentry.io/issues/7801028324/ ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) ## Why it happened - When an agent replies in an email inbox, the reply goes through `Messages::MessageBuilder`. The builder saves the email that will be sent (HTML and text) in `content_attributes['email']`. - Automatic messages do not go through the builder. They are created directly with `conversation.messages.create!`, so they have no `content_attributes['email']`. The mailer sends them from their plain content instead, and that has always worked. - After translating, `AgentMessageTranslationService` updates the saved email with the translated text. It did this for every message in an email inbox. For an automatic message there is no saved email to update, so it called `merge` on `nil` and crashed. - Other channels were not affected, because this step only runs for email inboxes. ## How to reproduce 1. Enable Auto Translate for the account and turn on the CSAT survey (or the greeting message) on an email inbox. 2. Send an email to the inbox in another language, for example Malayalam or French. The message is translated for the agent. 3. Resolve the conversation. 4. The survey never reaches the customer, and `SendReplyJob` fails on every retry with `undefined method 'merge' for nil`.
Log sample ~~~ # Incoming email detected as Malayalam and translated for the agent "conversation_language" => "ml" message 27920607 (incoming_email): "source_language" => "ml", "translations" => {"en" => "…"} # Agent resolves → CSAT message created with no email attributes, flagged for translation POST /api/v1/accounts/1/conversations/31838/toggle_status {"status" => "resolved"} "message.created", {id: 27920608, content: "Help us improve!", message_type: 3, content_type: "input_csat", content_attributes: {"display_type" => "star", "translation_pending" => true}} Enqueued SendReplyJob … with arguments: 27920608 # SendReplyJob crashes while translating the message ERROR: Error performing SendReplyJob … NoMethodError (undefined method 'merge' for nil): enterprise/app/services/captain/conversation/agent_message_translation_service.rb:93:in '…#email_content' enterprise/app/services/captain/conversation/agent_message_translation_service.rb:39:in '…#use_translation' enterprise/app/services/captain/conversation/agent_message_translation_service.rb:28:in '…#translate_reply' app/jobs/send_reply_job.rb:22:in 'SendReplyJob#perform' # Every retry fails the same way, so the survey is never sent Performing SendReplyJob … with arguments: 27920608 ERROR: … NoMethodError (undefined method 'merge' for nil) "retry_count":0 ~~~
With this fix, the same steps send the message. The pending job from the log above went through on its next retry: `Email message 27920608 sent`. ## What changed - Added `email_reply?` to `AgentMessageTranslationService`. It is true only for replies built by the message builder, which have a saved email. - The service updates the saved email, and keeps the original as HTML, only when `email_reply?` is true. Automatic messages keep their plain text and are sent through the mailer's existing fallback. - Agent replies in email inboxes and messages on other channels work exactly as before. ## Checklist: - [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project - [x] I have performed a self-review of my code - [ ] I have commented on my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas - [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation - [x] My changes generate no new warnings - [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works - [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes - [ ] Any dependent changes have been merged and published in downstream modules

title: fix: fall back to SQL search on OpenSearch errors
body:
Message search keeps returning SQL results when OpenSearch times out or fails, and reports the original error through `ChatwootExceptionTracker` with account and user context.

The rescue uses the Faraday and OpenSearch error classes provided by the installed client, fixing the `NameError` caused by the unloaded Elasticsearch constant. Existing search specs now exercise those failures at the query layer and verify reporting, successful results, SQL filtering, and GIN precedence.

Closes https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-8401

1. Configure OpenSearch and enable advanced search for an account with GIN search disabled.
2. Make OpenSearch unavailable or simulate a request timeout, then search for messages.
3. Confirm the search returns matching SQL results and the original error is logged and reported to Sentry when configured.

title: feat: preserve help center context across locale switches
body:

## Closes

## Why

The language switcher currently discards the page being viewed and always redirects to the selected locale's Help Center home. This interrupts visitors who are reading content that already has a translated equivalent.

## What this change does

- Resolves translated articles through their associated article mapping.
- Resolves translated categories through their associated category mapping.
- Uses the translated content's own slug and locale when building the destination.
- Falls back to the selected locale's Help Center home when no matching translation exists.
- Applies the behavior to the classic desktop, classic mobile, and documentation layouts.

## How to test

1. Open a public Help Center article that has a published translation and switch languages. Confirm the matching translated article opens.
2. Open a translated category and switch languages. Confirm the matching translated category opens.
3. Switch to a locale where the current article or category has no translation. Confirm the selected locale's Help Center home opens.

1. Reconcile a Startups, Business, or Enterprise account. Confirm Stripe is enabled and available under Settings → Integrations when OAuth is configured.
2. Downgrade to Hacker and reconcile. Confirm Stripe is disabled unless granted through a manually managed override.

title: fix: clarify self-hosted assignment policy enablement
body:
Community self-hosted inbox settings show “Custom assignment policies are available on the Premium plan” and link “Upgrade to Premium” to self-hosted pricing. Licensed self-hosted accounts with Advanced Assignment disabled show “Custom assignment policies are not enabled for this account.” without an upgrade button. Cloud keeps the Business plan prompt and account billing link.

## Why

The assignment prompt used Cloud upgrade guidance for self-hosted installations. Community installations need self-hosted pricing, while licensed installations should not be asked to upgrade for a disabled account feature.

Reported in [Discord](https://discord.com/channels/647412545203994635/1557776827353792602).

## How to reproduce

Open inbox collaborators settings with Assignment V2 enabled and Advanced Assignment disabled, then enable automatic assignment:

- On Community self-hosted, confirm the Premium plan prompt and self-hosted pricing link.
- On licensed self-hosted, confirm the account feature message with no upgrade button.
- On Cloud, confirm the Business plan prompt and account billing link.

Assignment behavior and feature eligibility are unchanged.

title: fix(voice): accept incoming twilio calls with withheld caller IDs

These calls now appear as “Unknown caller,” with a separate contact and conversation for each call. Retries reuse the existing records. Anonymous call conversations allow private notes but block SMS replies and callbacks. Normal numbered calls retain their existing behavior. **Unknown caller call** **Messaging restriction** Fixes https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/PLA-255 ### Things to know Covers incoming Twilio calls, including documented numeric placeholders for withheld caller IDs. Local webhook checks passed; real-call audio and browser verification remain pending. ### How to test 1. Call a voice-enabled Twilio inbox with caller ID withheld. Confirm agents receive the call as “Unknown caller.” 2. Call anonymously again. Confirm a separate contact and conversation are created. 3. Confirm callback is hidden, SMS replies are blocked, and private notes work. 4. Replay the same webhook with the same CallSid. Confirm no duplicate records are created. 5. Call with a visible number. Confirm normal calling and messaging behavior remains unchanged.

title: fix(whatsapp): recover stalled campaigns without repeating sends
body:
Tracked WhatsApp campaigns can remain in Processing when a worker stops during startup, while sending, or between batches. This change lets newly started campaigns recover from their saved progress after 15 minutes without progress, continuing with untouched contacts while excluding recipients already attempted.

If a send was interrupted and its outcome is uncertain, the recipient is left for review rather than automatically retried. This avoids risking a duplicate message while allowing the rest of the campaign to continue.

### Closes

Fixes https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-8478/recover-interrupted-whatsapp-campaigns-without-duplicate-sends

### What changed

- Save recovery eligibility atomically when a supported campaign enters Processing, and persist completed batch checkpoints.
- Create a unique recipient record before contacting WhatsApp. Only the execution that creates the record sends; existing recipients, including failed and historical queued recipients, are excluded from replay.
- Recover stale campaigns through the existing scheduler, using the saved checkpoint rather than stale job arguments.
- Reuse the existing Redis lock manager with a 15-minute campaign lock. Recipient claims prevent repeat sends if workers overlap, and checkpoints cannot move backward after lock expiry. The shared lock manager and mutex job are unchanged; no custom SQL is added.
- Cover startup interruption, lost responses, lost batch handoffs, expired-lock overlap, checkpoint ordering, and legacy recipient exclusion with regression tests discovered by the existing CircleCI Enterprise backend suite. No campaign tests are added to the MFA workflow.

### Things to know

- Automatic recovery applies to newly started campaigns using Enterprise delivery tracking. Existing Processing campaigns without a checkpoint need manual recovery; untracked OSS campaigns do not gain durable recovery.
- Apply the additive migration, then drain/restart all campaign workers before starting campaigns on this version. Old and new sender code must not process recovery-enabled campaigns concurrently.
- A worker stopping before a claimed send reaches WhatsApp cannot reliably be distinguished from WhatsApp accepting it before the response is saved. Neither case is automatically retried; uncertain recipients require reconciliation.
- Completion means send processing has finished. Delivery updates and uncertain-send review may remain pending. Audience membership continues to follow the existing live-label behavior.
- Before the workflow cleanup, CI passed on `b6a293ca2c`: all 16 backend shards, the Enterprise campaign regressions, lint, frontend tests, security checks, and both Docker builds. The workflow cleanup also passes all 33 focused campaign examples locally. Hosted checks for the updated commit are pending. This change has not been deployed.

### How to reproduce

Interrupt a worker after a tracked WhatsApp campaign enters Processing but before its first job is enqueued, during a batch, or before the next batch is enqueued. The campaign could previously remain in Processing indefinitely. Replaying a queued recipient whose provider response was lost could also repeat a send.

### How to test

1. In a test environment, start a tracked WhatsApp campaign spanning multiple batches and interrupt its worker during startup or sending.
2. Restart the worker and allow scheduled recovery after 15 minutes without progress. Untouched contacts should continue and the campaign should finish processing.
3. Confirm previously recorded recipients are excluded from repeat sends and uncertain outcomes remain available for review.
4. Replay an old batch or allow competing workers after a lock expires. Recipients must not be sent again, and saved progress must not move backward.
5. Confirm historical campaigns without a checkpoint are not automatically restarted. Replaying an existing legacy batch must exclude its queued, sent, and failed recipients.

title: feat: support an IdP metadata URL for SAML
body: SAML settings stored one static IdP certificate. If the identity provider rotated its signing certificate, SSO logins failed until an admin pasted the new certificate into each account. An admin can now enter the IdP metadata URL instead. Chatwoot reads the SSO URL, entity ID and signing certificates from it, refreshes them when the certificate is about to expire, and lets the admin refresh them on demand. Closes #16232 ## How it works - The SAML settings form has two tabs, "Metadata URL" and "Manual". Manual is the existing form. - When the metadata URL is saved or changed, Chatwoot fetches it and stores the SSO URL, entity ID and certificates. If the fetch fails or the values are invalid, the save fails with an error. - If the fetch fails, the error says why: the URL is not HTTPS, the host is blocked or unreachable, the IdP returned an error, or the response is not SAML metadata. Admins see a fixed message, not the raw fetch error, which can include host names and IP addresses. - The metadata URL must use HTTPS. The fetch goes through `SafeFetch`. - During a SAML login, Chatwoot fetches the metadata again only if the newest stored certificate expires within 15 minutes, at most once every 5 minutes. Only one request fetches, and concurrent logins use the stored values. - If that fetch fails, Chatwoot logs a warning with the same reason and keeps the stored values. - A "Refresh metadata" button on the Metadata URL tab fetches the metadata right away. - If the metadata lists several signing certificates, Chatwoot stores and trusts all of them. Each certificate is validated on save. - When several certificates are stored, the settings form shows the fingerprint of the one that expires last. The expiry check uses the same certificate. Logins still accept any stored certificate. - Accounts without a metadata URL behave as before. - The SAML settings error messages were defined under the wrong i18n key and showed "Translation missing". They now show the English text. ## Limits - An IdP that rotates its certificate well before expiry is not picked up at login. Logins fail until an admin clicks "Refresh metadata". A scheduled refresh job can cover this later. - After a rotation with no overlap, such as ZITADEL's, logins can fail for up to 5 minutes. - The HTTPS rule applies to the entered URL. `SafeFetch` follows redirects, including redirects to HTTP. - Self-hosted installs with an IdP on a private network must set `SAFE_FETCH_ALLOW_PRIVATE_NETWORK`. - Chatwoot does not check the metadata signature, `validUntil` or `cacheDuration`. ## How to test 1. Open Settings, Security, SAML SSO. 2. On the "Metadata URL" tab, enter the IdP metadata URL and save. 3. Open the "Manual" tab. It shows the fetched SSO URL, entity ID and certificate. 4. Log in through SSO. 5. Rotate the signing certificate in the IdP, then click "Refresh metadata" on the Metadata URL tab. The fingerprint changes. 6. Log in through SSO again.

## Description

The website widget, CSAT survey and help center pages set a `_chatwoot_session` cookie on every load (including inside the widget iframe on customer websites), even though they never use the session. title: feat(voice): apply business hours to incoming calls
body: This change lets admins apply an inbox’s business hours and timezone to incoming Twilio calls. Outside those hours, callers hear a configurable announcement and the call ends without ringing agents. The conversation records the missed call as “Outside business hours.” Admins can edit the announcement, save to generate its audio, and listen to the saved recording. If generation fails, the existing announcement stays active. ### Closes Fixes https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/PLA-137/business-hours ### Screenshots **Business hours enabled with saved announcement playback** **Warning when the inbox’s business hours are turned off** **Missed call logged as “Outside business hours”** ### Things to know - Applying business hours to calls is optional and off by default. Both the inbox’s business hours and the call-hours toggle must be enabled. - Audio generation uses Captain and one response credit. If Captain or credits are unavailable, Twilio reads the saved text instead. - Calls during business hours, and calls with the call-hours toggle off, continue through normal routing. Outbound calls are unaffected. - This version covers Twilio calls. WhatsApp follow-up messaging, voicemail, and reusable Voice Profiles are outside this scope. ### How to test 1. In a Twilio voice inbox, configure business hours and timezone. Enable “Apply business hours to calls,” enter an announcement, and save. Confirm the saved audio plays and remains available after reloading. 2. Call outside business hours. Confirm the announcement plays, no agents ring, the call ends, and the conversation shows “Outside business hours.” 3. Call during business hours with an eligible agent available. Confirm the call rings and can be answered. 4. Turn off “Apply business hours to calls,” then call outside business hours. Confirm normal ringing resumes. 5. Turn off the inbox’s business hours. Confirm the Voice settings explain that calls continue ringing.

title: feat(captain): move GPT-4 series and legacy transcription to GPT-6 Luna and gpt-transcribe
body:
OpenAI will shut down the GPT-4 series in the API. Captain features that still use these models will stop working on these dates unless we move them. This PR moves every Captain feature that runs on a GPT-4 model today to GPT-6 Luna, except Copilot, which moves to GPT-5.2. Audio transcription moves to gpt-transcribe. Features that run on GPT-5.2 stay as they are.

| Model | Shutdown date | Replacement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| gpt-4.1-nano | October 23, 2026 | gpt-6-luna |
| gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini, gpt-4.1, gpt-4.1-mini | January 14, 2027 | gpt-6-luna |
| gpt-4o-mini-transcribe, whisper-1 | February 26, 2027 | gpt-transcribe |

We replayed about 1,000 production calls from the last week on GPT-6 Luna and read every pair of outputs. Luna was equal or better on most features. Where it was worse, this PR fixes the prompt or the setting, and we re-ran the same calls to confirm each fix. The results are in the Evaluation section below.

## Main changes

1. Every Captain feature on GPT-4 moves to gpt-6-luna with reasoning effort none. Copilot moves to gpt-5.2. Audio transcription moves to gpt-transcribe. Features already on GPT-5.2 do not change.
2. `Captain::BaseTaskService` now sends the reasoning effort. Before this, it never sent the effort, so Luna would have used its default of medium on every editor request.
3. Document FAQ generation, a background job, uses reasoning effort medium so it keeps code samples and full coverage.
4. Prompt fixes from the evaluation: follow-up, widget tagline, overview summary length, completion reason language, tone rewrites, and PDF FAQ chunks.
5. A data migration moves saved GPT-4 model choices, and a GPT-4 `CAPTAIN_OPEN_AI_MODEL` on the standard OpenAI endpoint, to the new models. It runs during `db:migrate`, so the switch happens at deploy time.

## Closes

- OpenAI GPT-4 series retirement notice from October 14, 2026: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations

## Why GPT-6 Luna

OpenAI recommends GPT-6 Luna as the replacement for all of the retiring GPT-4 models. Its migration guide says to start with reasoning effort set to none.

Luna with reasoning off scores higher than every retiring model on the same version (v4.3.2) of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, and it costs less per token.

| Model | Index score | Price per 1M tokens (input / output) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| gpt-6-luna, reasoning off | 18 | $0.10 / $0.50 |
| gpt-4.1 | 13 | $2.00 / $8.00 |
| gpt-4.1-mini | 10 | $0.40 / $1.60 |
| gpt-4o | 8 | $2.50 / $10.00 |
| gpt-4.1-nano | not listed | $0.10 / $0.40 |

gpt-transcribe costs $0.0045 per minute. gpt-4o-mini-transcribe costs $0.003 per minute. OpenAI does not offer a cheaper replacement.

## How to test

1. With no Captain model overrides on the account, use the reply editor (improve, fix grammar, change tone, follow-up), reply suggestion, and summarize. Check that each gives a normal answer quickly. In Langfuse, check that the generation uses gpt-6-luna with reasoning effort none. Use Copilot and check that it uses gpt-5.2.
2. Upload a document and a short PDF (one or two pages) to a Captain assistant. Check that FAQs are generated, that the PDF finishes quickly, and that its FAQs are not repeated. In Langfuse, document FAQ generation should show reasoning effort medium.
3. Resolve a conversation that matches an existing FAQ. Check that FAQ matching still finds the duplicate.
4. Search the help center in another language. Check that the query is translated.
5. Run help center onboarding. Check the curated categories, and check that the widget tagline is short and not cut off.
6. Send voice notes from WhatsApp (OGG), Telegram (OGA), and the web widget. Check that each is transcribed.
7. Before running migrations, save editor = gpt-4.1 and audio transcription = whisper-1 on an account, and set `CAPTAIN_OPEN_AI_MODEL` to gpt-4.1. Run migrations. The account should show gpt-6-luna and gpt-transcribe, and the installation config should show gpt-6-luna. With a custom OpenAI endpoint, the installation config should stay unchanged.
8. Check that Captain V2, conversation FAQ generation, and article writer requests for GPT-5.2 accounts are unchanged.

## What changed

- `config/llm.yml`: GPT-4.1 models and the old transcription models are removed. gpt-6-luna takes the place of gpt-4.1-mini in every text feature list, so it is also available for features that default to GPT-5.2. Every former GPT-4 default is now gpt-6-luna, and audio transcription uses gpt-transcribe.
- gpt-6-luna has a model-level reasoning effort of none in `config/llm.yml`. `Llm::FeatureRouter` uses it when the feature does not set an effort, so requests to GPT-5.x models are unchanged.
- gpt-6-luna also has `temperature: true` in `config/llm.yml`, and `Llm::Models.temperature_for` reads it before the RubyLLM registry. The registry comes from models.dev, which lists Luna without temperature support, but Luna accepts temperature at reasoning effort none. Keeping the value in `config/llm.yml` means a registry refresh cannot undo it. `config/llm_models.json` is unchanged from develop.
- Hard-coded GPT-4 fallbacks now use gpt-6-luna. This covers `LlmConstants::DEFAULT_MODEL`, `Llm::Config::DEFAULT_MODEL`, the legacy OpenAI service, and the article search-term request, which used gpt-4o. Help center curation pinned gpt-4.1 and now uses the onboarding feature default. The unused `PDF_PROCESSING_MODEL` constant is removed.
- The `ReplaceRetiredCaptainModels` migration runs `Migration::ReplaceRetiredCaptainModelsJob` inline. The job remaps saved account model choices that are no longer allowed, and a GPT-4 `CAPTAIN_OPEN_AI_MODEL` on the standard OpenAI endpoint. It logs any account that fails other validations and moves on. The migration runs the job inline because on staging a queued copy reached Sidekiq workers that were still on the previous release and did not have the job class yet.
- `CaptainFeaturable` now validates Captain models only when they change. A saved model that `config/llm.yml` no longer allows no longer blocks unrelated account saves, such as billing credit updates. `Llm::FeatureRouter` already ignores such a value and uses the feature default.
- Copilot defaults to gpt-5.2 instead of Luna. Copilot passes its default as `fallback_model`, so the remapped `CAPTAIN_OPEN_AI_MODEL` does not move it to Luna.
- Document FAQ generation runs at reasoning effort medium. With effort none, Luna dropped code samples and some topics from long documents.
- Prompt fixes found by the evaluation:
  - Follow-up: change only what the agent asks for, and keep the signature.
  - Widget tagline: keep it under 45 characters and specific to the company.
  - Assistant overview summary: the 220-character limit per point is now firm.
  - Conversation completion: write the reason in English. The reason is posted as an agent-visible private note.
  - Tone rewrites: apply the requested tone clearly.
  - PDF FAQ generation: create FAQs for content in a short final range and stop there.
- `Captain::BaseTaskService` now sends the configured reasoning effort. Before this, it worked out the effort but never set it on the request, so every request built there used the model's default. With gpt-6-luna that default is medium, which would have made the editor actions, conversation completion, the widget tagline, curation, and the overview summary reason on every call. With the fix they use effort none, and conversation completion takes about 1.5 seconds instead of 3 to 11.
- `rake ruby_llm:refresh_models` works again. RubyLLM 2.0 points the model registry at a `ruby_llm_models` table that Chatwoot does not have, so the task now writes `config/llm_models.json` directly. The task file is renamed to `lib/tasks/llm_models.rake`, because RubyLLM loads `tasks/ruby_llm.rake` and was picking up our file, which defined the task twice. The cache file the refresh writes is ignored.

## Evaluation

We sampled up to 50 production calls per feature from October 8 to 14, replayed them on Luna with the original prompts, and read each pair.

- Equal or better: FAQ matching, improve, fix spelling and grammar, query translation, article translation, summarize, confident tone, reply suggestion, and the two overview summaries. Reply suggestion had fewer invented facts and used the right language more often.
- GPT-4.1-mini returned an empty `{}` for 6 of 346 editor requests (1.7%) in production. Luna returned none.
- Conversation completion made the same decision in 44 or 45 of 50 cases, and none of the differences was clearly wrong.
- Fixed by this PR and re-checked on the same calls:
  - Widget tagline: taglines cut off at the 60-character limit went from 16 of 50 to 1 of 50.
  - Overview summary: points over 220 characters went from 40 of 130 to 5 of 132.
  - Completion reasons in English went from 28 of 50 to 49 of 50.
  - Follow-up now keeps the agent's signature.
  - Tone rewrites improved, but casual and friendly are still milder than GPT-4.1-mini.
- PDF FAQ generation: on two test PDFs, the old prompt made GPT-4.1-mini keep asking for pages past the end of a 2-page PDF. It produced 174 FAQs in 135 seconds. Luna returned none. With the fix, GPT-4.1-mini made 21 FAQs in 12 seconds and Luna made 13 with no repeats.
- Message translation already ran on Luna, at its default effort of medium, because `BaseTaskService` never sent an effort. With this PR it runs at effort none. On 30 production messages, 25 translations were equal, medium was slightly better on 4 and none on 1, and none was about 0.3 seconds faster at the median.
- Audio transcription: on 9 real recordings (2 Opus, 7 MP3), gpt-transcribe gave the same text on 6 and better text on 3.
- Editor speed on the real services (median of 5 runs, reasoning effort none): improve about 1.4 s, against 1.2 s on GPT-4.1-mini. Reply suggestion took 7 to 9 s, against 4.6 s on GPT-4.1-mini, because its search tool adds two more Luna calls.
- Responses API and JSON: we ran the real services on Luna through the Responses API. Schema output (tagline, curation, overview summary, conversation completion), JSON mode (FAQ generator at effort medium, FAQ matching), the hand-built PDF FAQ request, and reply suggestion with its search tool all returned valid, parsed results with no errors.
- Not fully tested: Copilot turns that call tools. Copilot now uses gpt-5.2, which already serves some Copilot traffic in production.

## Known issues

- Custom OpenAI endpoints are not supported. Copilot always sends gpt-5.2, and article search-term generation always sends gpt-6-luna with reasoning effort none. Both ignore `CAPTAIN_OPEN_AI_MODEL`. The migration leaves `CAPTAIN_OPEN_AI_MODEL` unchanged on custom endpoints. Captain only supports OpenAI today.
- Document FAQ generation sends reasoning effort medium to whichever OpenAI model runs it, not only Luna.
- A Copilot model set to GPT-4.1 in Super Admin is remapped to Luna, not GPT-5.2. One Cloud account has this, and we will set it back to the default before deploying.

## Deferred to follow-up PRs

- A global default model and reasoning effort for each feature on the Super Admin Captain settings page, with the per-account override on top. `Llm::FeatureRouter` would then be the only reader of `CAPTAIN_OPEN_AI_MODEL`, which replaces Copilot's `fallback_model` and the other direct reads.
- Per-account reasoning effort controls in Super Admin, with one shared helper that applies the reasoning effort to every request.
- More providers, and searching for or typing in any model that RubyLLM supports.
- Out-of-hours call announcements use gpt-4o-mini-tts-2025-12-15, which OpenAI shuts down on January 6, 2027. The replacement works only through the Realtime API, so it needs its own change.
- The article search-term request raises `NoMethodError` instead of showing the provider's error. This bug was there before this PR.
- Replays of Copilot and reply suggestion turns that call tools. The recorded traces drop the tool calls, so we could not replay them.

## Notes for reviewers

- In the last 7 days of production, GPT-4 models handled about 33,000 text generations and 6,944 audio transcriptions. The largest was the document FAQ generator on gpt-4.1, with 10,228 calls costing $200.
- gpt-transcribe was tested against the live API with OGG, M4A, and MP3 files and `temperature: 0.0`. It rejects `.oga` file names in the same way as the old model, and #16184 already handles that.

title: feat(copilot): add durable read-only workflow building blocks
body:
Copilot can now work through many records in one request and answer when it is done, e.g. "find the customers who asked about refunds last week and summarize what the agents told them". It selects conversations, contacts or messages with filters, reviews the matching conversations one at a time in the background, and answers in the same chat turn. A turn reviews up to 100 conversations. When more remain, Copilot says how many it covered and reviews the next 100 when the agent asks it to continue. The agent can ask follow-up questions about the saved results later. Copilot only reads data in this PR. Everything is behind the internal `copilot_workflows` flag.

Changes with approval are in #16208.

## Closes

https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-8071/copilot-long-running-tasks

## How to test

1. Enable `copilot_workflows` for a test account and open Copilot.
2. Ask "Go through the conversations from the last 90 days, find the billing related ones and tell me which were the most troubled." Copilot shows each step, waits while the review runs, and then answers in the same turn with linked conversations, the filters it used and how many it checked.
3. Ask about a period with more than 100 conversations, e.g. "Review all conversations from this year and find the ones about refunds." Copilot reviews the newest 100, says how many are left and offers to continue. Reply "continue". Copilot reviews the next 100, and the results stay in the same review.
4. Ask "Which conversations are the most urgent?" Copilot reads the conversations to judge urgency instead of filtering on the priority field.
5. Ask "Find the customers who asked about pricing and give me their names and emails." Copilot reviews the conversations and then lists the matching contacts.
6. Ask "Which conversations mention order <an order number from a test conversation>, and who are those customers?" Copilot searches the message text and lists the conversation and its customer.
7. Ask a follow-up about the results, e.g. "which of those are still open?". Copilot answers from the saved results without starting a new review.
8. Stop Sidekiq while a review is running and start it again. The review continues after about 2.5 minutes, and Copilot still answers.
9. Use an agent whose custom role does not include contact management and ask for contacts. Copilot says it cannot view contacts.
10. Disable the flag while a review is running. The review stops before its next model call, and Copilot says workflows are turned off. New messages use the existing response path.

## What changed

- **Saved runs.** Each Copilot turn, selection and review is saved in `copilot_runs`, each tool call in `copilot_tool_calls`, and each reviewed conversation in `copilot_review_findings`. A worker that crashes or restarts during a deploy picks up where it stopped.
- **get_data.** Selects conversations, contacts or messages with typed filters and saves the IDs. With `from`, it selects the records linked to an earlier saved set, or to the matched conversations of a finished review, e.g. messages, then their conversations, then their contacts. Each record type is one class in `Captain::Copilot::Resources` that defines who can see it, its filters, its display columns and how to reach it from the other types. Contacts need the `contact_manage` permission. Messages are limited to conversations the user can open, and the text filter uses the existing trigram index. The model cannot set a limit, so a selection always covers everything that matches, up to 5,000 records.
- **review_conversations.** Jev scores every conversation against an optional yes or no question and drops the ones that clearly do not match. It reads the same messages GPT reads, private notes included. Conversations longer than 20 messages skip Jev, so evidence in older messages is not dropped unseen. GPT then reviews each remaining conversation in its own call and saves whether it matched, a category, a reason and the IDs of the messages it used as evidence.
- **Reviewing in batches.** A review finishes at most 100 conversations per turn, newest first, and reports how many remain. `continue_review` reviews the next 100 on the same review ID. It refuses to run twice in one turn, so the agent decides each time whether to continue.
- **Chatwoot context in the prompt.** The prompt explains what open, pending, snoozed and resolved mean, which fields agents and automations set, and what incoming, outgoing and private messages are. It tells the model not to add filters the agent did not ask for, and to judge topic, urgency, sentiment or intent by reviewing conversations, not by status or priority.
- **Waiting for a review.** The Copilot turn pauses while the review runs in the background and continues when it finishes, so the model reads the results and answers in the same turn. A message sent while a review runs is answered after that turn.
- **Recovery.** A job on the existing 5-minute enterprise schedule wakes a turn whose review finished without waking it, and requeues runs whose next job was never queued.
- **Turning the feature off.** Disabling `copilot_workflows` stops turns and reviews that are already running, at the same check as the credit limit.
- **display.** Shows any saved set or review as a linked table with counts of what was checked and how many conversations are left to review.
- **Tracing.** Each Copilot turn is one Langfuse trace, even though it runs across several jobs, and each Copilot thread is one Langfuse session. Review generations record the model, tokens and cost. Each tool call is its own span, and a tool call that fails is marked as an error.
- **Cost tracking.** Each user turn stores its total provider cost in USD, including Copilot orchestration, conversation reviews and Jev screening. `cost_complete` is false when any provider call does not report a cost, so account-level Metabase reporting does not silently treat a partial total as complete.
- **Smaller fixes.** `get_conversation` returns the contact ID, so Copilot looks up the right contact instead of guessing. Copilot replies stay readable in dark mode. Workflows use their own model setting, `copilot_workflows`, which defaults to GPT-5.2 with reasoning off. The old `search_conversation` tool is hidden on this path, because it put full transcripts into the model's context.

## Decisions

- **The durable design stays for this beta.** Each turn, selection and review is saved, each run holds a lease, and a turn waits for its review without holding a worker. We restarted Sidekiq in the middle of a review batch on a local copy of 2024 production data. The review resumed at 114 of 200 conversations after about 2.5 minutes and ended with 200 findings and no duplicates. If production shows that restarts during a turn are rare, a later PR can replace this with a simpler design.
- **Some changes reach every Copilot account, not only accounts with the flag:**
  - Answers use the chat bubble text style with blue underlined links, so they stay readable in dark mode.
  - Conversation links in answers open inside the dashboard instead of a new tab.
  - `get_conversation` adds the contact ID to its result.
- **The cost columns stay.** `total_cost_usd` and `cost_complete` on `copilot_runs` feed a Metabase dashboard of Copilot cost per account.
- **Known gap.** When Copilot builds a selection from a review that stopped early, the selection is not marked as incomplete, so its totals can look complete. A follow-up PR will fix this.

## Notes for reviewers

- The screening threshold is 0.1, because Jev gives low scores to conversations that are only partly about a topic. In a test with 45 conversations, 0.3 kept 3 of the 6 matches GPT found, and 0.1 kept 5.
- One selection holds at most 5,000 records (`MAX_SELECTION`), and a review covers at most 100 conversations per turn (`CONVERSATIONS_PER_TURN`).
- The batches and the recovery job came out of an end-to-end test where the model capped "review all" at 50 conversations and added a status filter nobody asked for, while its answer read as complete.

title: feat(copilot): propose changes behind an approval card
body:
Copilot can now change conversations after the agent approves. When an agent asks, e.g. "find the conversations about pricing from the last 90 days and label them billing", Copilot finds them as in #16093 and then shows a card with the change, the number of conversations and links to the first ten. Nothing is written until the agent clicks Approve. Copilot then applies the change and reports how many conversations it changed, skipped or could not change. Rejecting, sending another message, or leaving the card for five minutes cancels the change, and the agent can ask Copilot to propose it again.

Stacked on #16093. Retarget to `develop` after #16078 and #16093 merge. Everything is behind the internal `copilot_workflows` flag.

## Closes

No linked issue.

## How to test

1. Enable `copilot_workflows` for a test account and open Copilot.
2. Ask "Find conversations from the last 90 days where a customer asked about pricing, and label them billing." After the review, a card shows the label, the number of conversations and links to the first ten, and the loading indicator stops. The links open the conversations.
3. Click Approve. The conversation list shows the new label, each conversation gets an activity message with your name, and Copilot reports how many conversations it changed, skipped or could not change.
4. Ask again with another label and click Reject. No labels change, the card shows Rejected, and Copilot says nothing was changed.
5. Ask again and send a new message instead of deciding. The card shows Rejected, and Copilot answers the new message.
6. Ask again and wait five minutes. The card shows Expired, and Copilot says nothing was changed. Reply "yes, continue". A new card appears for the same conversations, and approving it applies the label.
7. Ask again, then disable `copilot_workflows` before deciding and click Approve. The card shows Rejected with a message that workflows are turned off, and no labels change.

## What changed

- **act tool.** Proposes one change to a saved set. It checks the action, its arguments and that the set holds the record type the action changes, saves the exact list of records to change, shows the approval card and pauses the turn. For a review it changes the matched conversations by default, or every conversation the review finished, including the ones screened out.
- **Actions.** Each action is one class in `Captain::Copilot::Actions` with a name, the record type it changes, a schema for its arguments and a method that changes one record. `add_labels` is the first action. A new action needs one class and one translation string for the card.
- **ActionJob.** Changes one record at a time. Before each change it checks access again with the record type's rules from #16093. It saves each outcome in `copilot_action_items`, so a retried job skips records that are already done, and activity messages name the agent who approved, e.g. "John added billing".
- **Approve and reject.** `POST /captain/copilot_runs/:id/approve` and `/reject`, allowed only for the agent who asked.
- **Expiry.** A scheduled job expires an undecided change after five minutes and continues the turn. A late approval is refused, because the saved list of records may be out of date.
- **Approval card.** A new `assistant_approval` message type is shown outside the collapsed steps. It links the first ten records the change will touch and counts the rest. A new `copilot.message.updated` event updates the card to Approved, Rejected or Expired without a reload.
- **Turning the feature off.** Approving while `copilot_workflows` is off rejects the change. An approved change that is still running stops before its next batch.
- **Recovery.** The recovery job from #16093 also requeues an approved change whose job was never queued, and wakes a turn whose change finished without waking it.
- **Shared job steps.** `ReviewJob` and `ActionJob` share the logic that claims a run, retries it and hands the result back to the waiting turn.

## Notes for reviewers

- RubyLLM's own tool approval approves a function call, and the records would only be chosen after the click. Here the agent approves a fixed list of records, and the changes run in their own job instead of inside the chat job.
- One change can target at most 500 records (`MAX_TARGETS`), and a card expires after five minutes (`APPROVAL_TTL`).
- The migration adds `copilot_action_items`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(voice): generate announcements through chat audio
body:
This PR moves saved voice announcement generation to `gpt-audio-1.5` through Chat Completions ahead of the current text-to-speech model's retirement. Admins continue using **Save announcement** and listening to the saved MP3 in the inbox Voice settings.

The request asks the model to read the supplied text verbatim in its original language. The existing Alloy voice, MP3 storage and playback, Twilio text fallback when generation is unavailable, and preservation of the prior announcement on generation errors remain in place.

Fixes https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/PLA-269/migrate-voice-announcement-generation-before-openai-tts-shutdown

### Things to know

- Generated audio is accepted only when its accompanying transcript matches the supplied text after whitespace normalization. Missing or mismatched transcripts return a clear error before changing the saved announcement or charging a Captain credit. This rejects the omitted-passage failure observed in the live trial. The model’s own transcript is still not independent proof that every spoken word matches; punctuation or number-format changes are also rejected rather than silently accepted.
- Existing saved MP3 files remain usable; no backfill is required.
- The current charge of one Captain response credit per generation is retained. Provider cost is different and credit pricing should be reviewed before release.
- Custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints must support the selected model and Chat Completions audio output. Unsupported requests return an error and preserve the saved announcement.
- No live Twilio call has been run for this migration yet. Real API trials produced MP3 samples for local playback.

### How to test

1. With Captain configured and credits available, open a Twilio inbox's Voice settings, edit the out-of-hours announcement, and save. Listen to the saved audio and confirm it reads the complete supplied text, including questions, numbers, and opening hours.
2. Repeat with German text and a long announcement containing repeated passages. Matching output should save normally. If the returned transcript omits or changes text, confirm the save shows an error and the prior announcement, audio, and call-hours settings remain unchanged.
3. Reload the settings and call outside business hours. Confirm the saved announcement plays and the call ends without ringing agents.
4. Make generation unavailable by using a test account without Captain credits. Save updated text and confirm Twilio reads the text fallback. If a generation request instead fails, confirm the previously saved announcement remains active.

### What changed

Replaces the speech-endpoint request with a Chat Completions audio request and decodes its base64 MP3 response. Validates the returned transcript before accepting audio or charging a credit. Updates the announcement model configuration and focused generation/preservation specs.

title: chore: Share Jev quotas across AI classification calls
body:
## Description

Monitors, automation Captain conditions, and label/priority suggestions now share the account's existing monthly and daily call allowances. Previously, Captain conditions and suggestions could call Jev without consuming or checking that allowance. Quota enforcement applies even when the account has no enabled monitors.

Accounting runs once at the shared Enterprise Jev client before contacting OpenRouter. The account shares develop's current Postgres-backed limits of 10,000,000 calls per month and 500,000 per UTC day. Existing usage and attempted-call charging are retained, so deployment preserves consumed credits without a migration. Redis token accounting has been removed upstream. Monitor callers no longer reserve separately, and quota errors retain their existing deferred retry behavior. Automation Captain conditions become unmet at exhaustion; both suggestion endpoints return `429` with a quota error and `Retry-After`. Quota responses, automation fallbacks, and the quota exception live in Enterprise overlays; OSS classes expose only extension hooks. The monitor allowance copy describes the shared usage.

## Type of change

- [x] New feature

## How to test

1. On an account with Captain classification enabled, request priority and label suggestions and run an automation with a Captain condition. Confirm each provider request increments the same account usage shown by monitor reports, including when monitors are disabled.
2. Evaluate a monitor and confirm it consumes one call rather than two.
3. With the account at its monthly allowance, confirm suggestion requests return `429` and `Retry-After`, Captain conditions are unmet, and monitor work waits for the quota reset. Ordinary automation conditions continue to decide the rule normally.
4. Exhaust the daily call allowance and confirm requests are blocked before contacting the provider or charging another monthly call. Confirm another account can still classify.

The 232-example Enterprise/client/monitor/automation run, 24-example OSS run, and direct cross-path HTTP checks passed, including both quota-exhaustion paths after moving the handlers into Enterprise overlays. Existing specs were adjusted for the shared quota exception and real account-backed client accounting; no new specs were added. Ruby lint, JSON validation, formatting, and Git hooks passed.

title: fix(voice): verify twilio webhook signatures
body:
This draft verifies that Twilio voice callbacks actually come from Twilio before Chatwoot processes call, status, conference, or recording events. Missing or invalid signatures return 403.

Deploy the token-update flow in [#16244](https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/pull/16244) and complete customer credential validation through [CW-8452](https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-8452/update-remaining-twilio-voice-account-tokens-before-signature) before merging or deploying this PR.

Fixes https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-8443

### Things to know

- Recording URL and redirect credential protections are separate in [#16250](https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/pull/16250), which can deploy independently without waiting for customer token updates.
- This PR remains deferred until the remaining Account Auth Tokens are validated. The collection flag does not bypass verification, and the API Key Secret cannot substitute for the account token.
- Proxies must preserve the external callback URL. SMS and WhatsApp messaging callback authentication are outside this change.
- All 13 existing voice-controller tests passed. Prior local checks also verified rejection of missing, invalid, API-key-secret, and tampered signatures on all four voice endpoints. Live outgoing-call testing still needs an account permitted to call the destination.

### How to test

1. With a validated Account Auth Token, make incoming and outgoing calls. Confirm answering, hangup, and final call status work.
2. Finish a recorded call and confirm its recording appears and plays.
3. Confirm unsigned or tampered voice callbacks return 403 without creating or changing calls.

title: fix: prevent duplicate Help Center article creation
body:
## Description

Creating a Help Center article now keeps title, content, author, and category changes made while the initial draft is being created. Pending changes are saved to that same article before navigation, and retries reuse the created record instead of producing duplicate drafts.

Newly generated article slugs also include a bounded random suffix. This prevents same-title articles created within the same second from colliding with the unique slug index, while existing article URLs remain unchanged.

## Closes

Closes https://github.com/chatwoot/chatwoot/issues/11352

## How to reproduce

1. Open Help Center → Articles → New article.
2. Enter a title, click directly into the editor, and immediately paste content while the create request is still running.
3. Confirm that only one draft article is created and the pasted content is present after navigation.
4. Retry after a failed post-create update and confirm that the existing draft is reused.

## What changed

- Buffer new-article edits without triggering additional create requests.
- Drain pending title, content, author, and category changes before redirecting.
- Retain the created article ID across synchronization failures and avoid redirects after leaving the page.
- Generate readable collision-resistant article slugs and validate their uniqueness.

title: fix: prevent multiple bot providers on an inbox
body:
An inbox can connect only one active bot provider at a time. Connecting Agent Bot, Captain, or Dialogflow while another provider is active now returns an error naming the provider to disconnect. Manual conversation-level Agent Bot assignment remains available.

### Closes
- https://linear.app/chatwoot/issue/CW-7835/prevent-multiple-bot-providers-from-connecting-to-an-inbox

### Why
Multiple inbox-level bot providers can compete to handle the same conversation.

### What changed
- Validate provider exclusivity when connecting or re-enabling Agent Bot, Captain, and Dialogflow.
- Leave existing connections unchanged; this does not migrate or disconnect historical setups.
- Concurrent cross-provider connection attempts are a narrow race and intentionally out of scope; this PR covers sequential setup.

### Validation
- Connect each provider to an inbox, then try connecting either of the other two. Confirm the second connection is rejected and names the current provider.
- Disconnect or disable the first provider, then confirm another can connect.
- Confirm a conversation-level Agent Bot assignment still works in a Captain-connected inbox.
